title: Sign-out is unreachable when the auth session is stale
description: When the browser's auth session goes stale (expired token that failed to refresh — e.g. a tab left open overnight or a laptop waking from sleep), the app keeps rendering the signed-in shell while every API call returns 401. The UI is inert, and the sign-out control itself depends on an API round-trip, so clicking it does nothing. The user cannot self-rescue: the only ways out are manually clearing cookies or knowing to type the logout URL by hand. Observed 2026-08-18 during local testing; this failure shape is invisible in logs-first triage because nothing errors client-side.
design:
SPEC (spec pass 2026-08-18, drafting agent). Direction decided at triage; this pass verifies mechanism against the code and pins pointers. Two changes, both frontend.

PROBLEM, verified:
A stale session means the auth cookie still verifies (12h maxAge — src/lib/auth-config.ts:9,:53) while the backend rejects the bearer token, so the middleware keeps serving the signed-in shell while every API call 401s. Two client-side gaps keep the user stuck:

(a) DETECTION GAP. The centralized 401 seam already exists: apiClient boots unrecoverable 401s to /login via handleTerminalAuthLogout (src/lib/api/client.ts:315-321; getBlob mirror :425-431; the handler itself :68-85 — provider signOut({wipePersisted:true}) then window.location.assign('/login?reason=…'), re-entry-guarded at :52). But the boot fires ONLY for envelope codes in TERMINAL_AUTH_CODES (:158-163) or IDLE_TIMEOUT. A 401 whose body carries no error envelope — the backend renders a plain-detail HTTPException as FastAPI-default {"detail": …} and logs it as "auth failed: UNKNOWN" (backend/app/api_errors.py:112-124 maps missing envelope code to UNKNOWN, log line :144; e.g. the bare fallback raise in backend/app/auth/providers.py:318) — maps to errorCode "UNKNOWN_ERROR" client-side (client.ts:300) and boots NOTHING. That is exactly the observed failure signature: repeated 401 "auth failed: UNKNOWN" on /api/auth/session while the shell renders inert. (The server-side rescue only covers full RSC loads: app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:92-98 redirects any 401 to /login?reason=…; a tab already rendered never re-runs it.)

(b) SIGN-OUT CONTROL. Header (src/components/layout/Header.tsx:24-31, wired at :85) awaits getClientAuthProvider().signOut() — for the default firebase provider that is firebaseSignOut (src/lib/auth/firebase/client.ts:284-300): SDK sign-out plus an UNBOUNDED fetch("/api/logout") at :296 (contrast syncAuthTick's /api/login fetch, which IS withTimeout-bounded at :167-175) — then a soft router.push("/login") with no reason param. Failure modes: any hang before the push leaves the click doing nothing; and if the cookie-clear fetch didn't land, the /login push bounces straight back to /dashboard (authenticated-on-/login redirect, src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts:65-67).

KEY FACT — /api/logout is ALREADY reachable with no or invalid session; no public-paths change is needed. proxy.ts:15 routes it into the middleware, and next-firebase-auth-edge short-circuits loginPath/logoutPath BEFORE any token verification (node_modules/next-firebase-auth-edge/lib/next/middleware.js:110-121 -> createAuthMiddlewareResponse :71-87), answering the logout path with removeAuthCookies — a 200 {"success":true} JSON carrying the cookie-removal Set-Cookie headers (lib/next/cookies/index.js:122-132). PUBLIC_PATHS (src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts:17) stays untouched. Consequence: a top-level navigation to /api/logout clears cookies but strands the user on a JSON body — so the middleware must answer NAVIGATIONS to logoutPath with a redirect to /login carrying those same cookie-removal headers.

MECHANISM:
1. Sign-out as navigation to logoutPath.
   a. Middleware (src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts): when the request path is logoutPath AND the request is a top-level navigation (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate, with Accept: text/html as fallback), take the library's logout response and return a redirect to /login instead, COPYING its Set-Cookie removal headers verbatim — never re-deriving them (flags and enableMultipleCookies behavior, auth-config.ts:48-56, must be byte-identical; cookie flags are a closed decision). fetch() callers (firebase/client.ts:122,:143,:296 — cors mode) keep today's 200 JSON. Forward a whitelisted reason query param (only values in FORCED_LOGOUT_REASONS, src/lib/auth/forced-logout.ts:16) from the logout URL onto the /login redirect. Also handle the DEV_MODE branch (middleware.ts:49-51 currently skips everything): redirect logoutPath navigations to /login there too — no app route exists for /api/logout (frontend/app/api has only auth/ and config/), so today a dev-mode navigation would 404.
   b. Header.tsx handleSignOut: bound the provider sign-out (best-effort; withTimeout already exists, firebase/client.ts:100-106) and pass {wipePersisted:true} (same bfcache rationale as client.ts:72-79), then HARD-navigate window.location.assign(logoutPath) (imported from @/lib/auth-config) instead of router.push. One navigation clears cookies and lands on /login in the same response — nothing to bounce, nothing for a dead session to block. PROVIDER CAUTION: oidcSignOut self-navigates to the IdP end-session URL (src/lib/auth/oidc/client.ts:163) and must keep owning its navigation — gate the Header's logoutPath assign so it never stomps that redirect (e.g. only for the firebase provider, or let the provider contract own the terminal navigation).
2. Unclassifiable 401 = terminal. In apiClient's 401 branch (client.ts:315-321) and getBlob's (:425-431): for client-managed-token requests (!token), a 401 whose body yields no recognized envelope code (errorCode UNKNOWN_ERROR — i.e. not MFA_REQUIRED, not IDLE_TIMEOUT, not in TERMINAL_AUTH_CODES) is treated as terminal -> handleTerminalAuthLogout("session_expired"). The refresh-retry gate (:248-253) is NOT widened — closed decision. MFA_REQUIRED stays excluded; IDLE_TIMEOUT keeps its own reason; the re-entry guard is unchanged. This makes the inert shell self-resolving: the first 401 from any call — including the IdleTimeout session peek (src/lib/api/session.ts:24-26, fired from src/components/IdleTimeout.tsx:102) — lands on /login?reason=session_expired, which the middleware lets render (isForcedLogoutArrival, forced-logout.ts:18-20, consumed at firebase/middleware.ts:65) and where LoginScreen clears the stale client session itself (src/lib/auth/firebase/LoginScreen.tsx:52-75 -> clearStaleSession, firebase/client.ts:114-126). If routing the terminal flow itself through logoutPath (assign logoutPath?reason=… so the cookie clear and the landing are one response) proves clean with 1a's reason forwarding, prefer it; otherwise handleTerminalAuthLogout's existing /login?reason=… landing stands.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: sign-out must work without a working API session; the redirect target is the existing logoutPath, not a new route; middleware auth semantics, cookie flags, and Secure-cookie behavior unchanged (the navigation answer copies the library's cookie-removal headers verbatim and changes no verification outcome on any path); do not touch token refresh logic (the :248-253 retry gate stays as-is), the login flow (LoginScreen untouched), or the public-paths list (verified unnecessary — logoutPath is handled pre-verification, pointers above).

OUT OF SCOPE: backend error envelopes (giving providers.py:318 a proper code is a separate bead — the client must tolerate unclassifiable 401s regardless, since any proxy or edge layer can also produce one); LoginScreen / forced-logout reason set; OIDC logout redesign (its self-navigation just must not regress); idle-timeout semantics; any new route.

SEQUENCING: siblings PABLO-bhz and PABLO-mep live in settings/calendar/availability surfaces (dashboard settings page, src/components/settings/, src/components/calendar/, scheduling engine) — checked against this bead's file set below: ZERO overlap, safe to run in parallel with both.

DONE SIGNAL: the unclassifiable-401 test is red on current main and green with the change (state red-then-green in the PR body); frontend vitest + lint green; exactly one PR.

title: Appointment dialog can only book the first 20 patients
description:
## Problem

`AppointmentModal.tsx` calls `usePatientList()` with no params. The backend default is `page_size=20` (`backend/app/routes/patients.py`), so the New appointment dialog's patient `Select` renders only the first 20 patients — `patients.map()` over one unpaginated page, with no search input.

Patients sort by `last_name, first_name`, so which 20 you get is alphabetical. A clinician with more than 20 patients simply cannot book an appointment for anyone outside that window: the option is not in the DOM, and there is no way to search for it from the dialog.

## Why it matters

21+ patients is an ordinary caseload for an established practice. For those users the calendar's primary create path is broken for most of their roster, with no workaround and no error message — the patient just isn't in the list.

## Related

PABLO-y93 fixed exactly this class of bug for the patient LIST (page_size=100 + 'showing N of M'), but the appointment dialog was not part of that change and still has the original default.
design:
## DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate

**Build the searchable typeahead. Do not simply raise page_size.** `GET /api/patients` already accepts a `search` param; query it server-side as the user types so roster size stops mattering. Raising `page_size` to 100 only moves the ceiling (the endpoint caps at 100) and would not satisfy the acceptance criteria, which require a practice above 100 patients to work.

**Debounce input ~250ms** and keep the currently-selected patient rendered even when it falls outside the active result set, so an edit-existing-appointment open does not blank the field.

**Keep the empty query working:** with no text typed, show the first page as today, so the common small-practice case is unchanged and needs no typing.

## Where

- `frontend/src/components/calendar/AppointmentModal.tsx` — the patient control is a plain shadcn `Select` today (`patients.map()` over `usePatientList()`); swap it for a `Command`/combobox that accepts input.
- `frontend/src/hooks/usePatients.ts` — `usePatientList` already takes params; pass `search` through. Do not change its signature for other callers.

## Do NOT touch

- `PatientTable.tsx` and the patient-list pagination — that surface was already fixed under PABLO-y93 and is out of scope here. Changing it widens the diff into a file this bead does not own.
- The backend route, its response model, or the appointment POST payload. This is a frontend-only change; the API already has everything needed.

## Tests

`frontend/src/components/calendar/__tests__/AppointmentModal.test.tsx` — add a case for selecting a patient that is NOT in the first page of results (i.e. only reachable via search).
acceptance_criteria:
- A practice with more than 100 patients can find and book any patient from the New appointment dialog.
- Selecting a patient still books correctly (POST /api/appointments unchanged).
- The dialog's existing unit tests pass, with a new case covering a patient outside the first page.
- No change to the appointment payload or backend route signature.
notes:
EVIDENCE STRENGTHENED 2026-08-15: this is not only a UX ceiling, it is actively breaking the deployed e2e gate, and the breakage is progressive rather than a clean pass/fail.

Measured against the shared test tenant: soft-deleting every patient made the scheduling e2e pass immediately; an hour of runs re-accumulated patients (~2 per run) and the same spec degraded in lockstep with the count — passed at 0 active patients, intermittent around 20-30 (a new patient sometimes still fell inside the first page, because patients sort by last_name,first_name so inclusion is alphabetical luck), and failed on every run at 44.

The user-visible consequence at >20 patients is worse than 'cannot find the patient': the picker silently offers no matching option, and an appointment can end up booked against the wrong patient or none at all rather than failing loudly. That is the part worth fixing carefully.

Practical note for whoever takes this: raising page_size is not enough even as a stopgap, because the ceiling just moves to 100 and the same silent-wrong-selection behaviour returns. The search-backed typeahead in the design section removes the ceiling entirely.

title: Give the free-slots route its first consumer: a 'find a time' affordance in the appointment flow
description:
Nothing calls GET /api/availability/slots. The settings surface added recently
lets a therapist author availability rules, and the engine evaluates them
correctly, but no part of the product ever asks the engine what is free - so a
therapist configures rules and sees no effect anywhere.

Add a "find a time" affordance to the appointment creation flow that pulls real
open slots for a date instead of asking the user to type a time and hope.
design:
FRONTEND, plus whatever thin client code the call needs.

  frontend/src/lib/api/availability.ts   - today exports only the four rules
                                           CRUD calls; add the free-slots read
  frontend/src/hooks/useAvailability.ts  - follow the existing hook pattern
  the appointment create surface         - add the affordance alongside the
                                           existing manual time entry, do not
                                           replace it

TWO EMPTY STATES, RENDERED DIFFERENTLY. This is the whole reason the sibling
bead about unconfigured-vs-no-openings exists: "you have not set up your
availability yet" is an onboarding prompt pointing at the settings surface,
and "no openings that day" is a real answer. Never render the first as the
second. Depends on that distinction being available from the engine.

KEEP MANUAL ENTRY. A therapist must still be able to book a time the rules do
not offer - overriding your own availability is a normal thing to do. This
affordance is a convenience, not a gate.

Mirror the test style of the settings surface's existing component tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The appointment create flow can list real open slots for a chosen date,
   sourced from the free-slots route.
2. Selecting a slot fills the appointment time; manual entry still works and
   is not gated by the rules.
3. "Not configured" and "no openings" render as visibly different states, and
   the first links to the availability settings surface.
4. Component tests cover: slots listed, slot selected, no openings, not
   configured.

title: Refuse double-booking on the appointment write path — create, update and recurring
design:
DOUBLE-BOOKING IS CURRENTLY ACCEPTED WITH A 201. Two appointments for the same
clinician at the same time are both created. Rules are policy; collisions are
physics, and this bead is only about the physics.

PROVEN 2026-08-02, not inferred:
  backend/app/routes/scheduling.py:193  create_appointment
    -> backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:42
  which validates ONLY (lines 53-62): patient_id non-empty; start_at and end_at
  present; duration_minutes is a positive int. Then it constructs the
  Appointment and calls repo.create (:92). There is no overlap check, no
  end > start check, no past-date check. SchedulingService never imports
  AvailabilityEngine.
  AppointmentConflictError already exists at
  backend/app/scheduling_engine/exceptions.py:25 and is raised NOWHERE - the
  only reference in the repo is its own definition.

DO NOT REUSE check_conflicts FOR THIS. AvailabilityEngine.check_conflicts
(backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:48) is RULES-ONLY: it
iterates the user's rules and returns [] when there are none, so a user with no
rules gets an empty conflict list for a time that exactly double-books. Wiring
it in and calling this bead done would leave the default case broken. Appointment
subtraction lives only in get_free_slots (:79-85), a different method with a
different signature. Use the repository primitive instead.

DEPENDS ON the list_overlapping primitive bead. Do not hand-roll a second
overlap predicate here.

WHERE TO ENFORCE - service layer, not the route. The route-level shortcut leaves
two holes: backend/app/services/ical_sync_service.py:321 writes straight to the
repo, and there is more than one write route. Put it in SchedulingService so
every caller inherits it.

  1. SchedulingService.__init__ (services/scheduling.py:39) currently takes only
     appointment_repo. Keep the signature backward-compatible for the many
     tests that construct SchedulingService(repo) directly.
  2. create_appointment (:42): after the existing validation, before constructing
     the Appointment, ask the repo for overlaps and raise
     AppointmentConflictError when any are returned.
  3. update_appointment (:105): the mutable allow-list includes start_at, end_at
     and duration_minutes (:114-129), so a legal booking can currently be MOVED
     on top of another one. Check there too, passing
     exclude_appointment_id=appointment_id so an appointment never collides with
     itself. CAREFUL: update_appointment is also called internally at
     routes/scheduling.py:414 to attach session_id during start-session. That
     call passes no times. Only run the check when a time field is actually
     changing, or start-session will begin returning 409.
  4. create_recurring (:154) validates per-series, not per-occurrence. Check
     each generated occurrence. Decide explicitly and write it in the bead notes:
     does one colliding occurrence fail the whole series, or is it skipped? Fail
     the whole series unless there is a reason not to - a partially-created
     series is harder to reason about than a rejected one.

ROUTE MAPPING: AppointmentConflictError -> HTTP 409 with a message naming the
conflicting time. Add the handler beside the existing InvalidAppointmentError
-> 400 mapping (routes/scheduling.py, create at :203, update at :277). 409 is
the correct code; do not fold this into the 400 branch.

DECIDED, so a worker does not have to guess:
  - Buffers do NOT apply here. This bead is pure collision. Buffer-aware
    refusal belongs with rule enforcement, in the follow-on bead.
  - Cancelled appointments never collide - handled inside list_overlapping.
  - Back-to-back is legal (half-open intervals).
  - A deliberate double-book (group session, overlapping intake) is NOT
    supported by this bead. If it is ever wanted it needs an explicit override
    flag, never a silent allow. Out of scope here.

OUT OF SCOPE: availability rules, HARD/SOFT enforcement, buffers, any UI.
acceptance_criteria:
1. POST /api/appointments returns 409 (not 201) for a time that overlaps an
   existing non-cancelled appointment on the same clinician's calendar.
2. PATCH /api/appointments/{id} returns 409 when the new time overlaps a
   DIFFERENT appointment, and succeeds when the only overlap is the appointment
   being moved.
3. The start-session flow still works: the internal update that attaches
   session_id (routes/scheduling.py:414) does not 409.
4. Back-to-back appointments are still accepted.
5. A cancelled appointment does not block rebooking its slot.
6. Recurring creation refuses a series containing a colliding occurrence, with
   the chosen semantic recorded in the bead notes.
7. Route tests exist that call POST /api/appointments directly - today NO test
   anywhere calls it, which is why this shipped. At minimum: the 201 happy path,
   the 409 collision, and the back-to-back 201.
8. `make check` passes at the repo root.
notes:
*** SCOPE SHRANK 2026-08-03 — the hard part already landed. ***
PR #639 ("Add overlap detection to the appointment repository", merged
2026-08-03) added list_overlapping to BOTH the Postgres and in-memory
appointment repositories, using the correct half-open predicate
(existing.start < proposed.end AND existing.end > proposed.start), excluding
cancelled appointments in-query, with an optional exclude_appointment_id for
the reschedule case. Test coverage exists for exact-match, containment,
back-to-back, cancelled, exclusion and cross-user.

So this bead is NO LONGER "write overlap detection". It is: CALL it from the
write path and raise. Specifically:
  backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:42 - the create path
  that today validates only patient_id / start_at / end_at / duration_minutes
  -> call list_overlapping (exclude_appointment_id on update/reschedule) and
     raise the already-defined AppointmentConflictError on a hit.
  Cover create, update, and every occurrence of a recurring series.

Do NOT reimplement the predicate. Reuse list_overlapping; a second, subtly
different overlap rule in the service layer is exactly the drift this note
exists to prevent.

title: Extract the shared sign-in credential block used by /login and /native-auth
description:
The web sign-in screen and the desktop-app sign-in handoff now carry near-identical credential blocks: Google button, passkey button + recovery-code link, email/password form, forgot-password, sign-up toggle, MFA challenge and verify-email steps. The two differ only in what happens after a credential resolves — one seeds a session cookie and routes to the dashboard, the other exchanges for a one-time code and hands back to the native app.

Every new factor has to be added twice, and the passkey gap on the handoff page (PABLO-bqz) is exactly what that costs: passkeys shipped on one surface and silently missed the other.

Proposal: extract a presentational credential block that takes an onCredential(credential, method) callback plus a few flags (allow sign-up, show 'last used' hints), and have both screens render it with their own completion handler. Keep the post-credential behaviour in each screen — that's the real difference.

Follow-up to PABLO-bqz.
design:
The web sign-in screen (`frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/LoginScreen.tsx`) and the
desktop-app sign-in handoff (`frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/NativeAuthScreen.tsx`)
carry near-identical credential blocks. They differ only in what happens AFTER a
credential resolves: LoginScreen seeds a session cookie and routes to /dashboard;
NativeAuthScreen exchanges the ID token for a one-time code and hands back to the
native app's redirect_uri.

That duplication has already cost us once — passkeys shipped on /login and silently
missed /native-auth (PABLO-bqz).

SEAM
Add `frontend/src/components/auth/CredentialBlock.tsx`, a presentational component
that owns credential acquisition and NOTHING about what follows. Export it from
`frontend/src/components/auth/index.ts`.

    type AuthMethod = "google" | "email" | "passkey"

    interface CredentialBlockProps {
      // Called exactly once, when a credential is fully resolved — including
      // after an MFA challenge or a recovery-code redemption. The host decides
      // what happens next. May be async; the block stays in its loading state
      // until it settles.
      onCredential: (credential: UserCredential, method: AuthMethod) => Promise<void>
      email: string
      onEmailChange: (email: string) => void
      // Show the "Create account" toggle and the sign-up form (default true).
      allowSignUp?: boolean
      // Show the "Last used" pill on the method this device last used (default false).
      showLastUsed?: boolean
      // Show the "Having trouble signing in?" storage-reset link (default false).
      showAuthReset?: boolean
      // Host-supplied message rendered in the block's error slot (e.g. the
      // forced-logout notice). The block may overwrite it with its own errors.
      notice?: string
    }

The block owns these internal steps and renders each in place of the sign-in form:
`sign-in` | `mfa` | `recovery-code` | `verify-email`. It keeps the existing
`MfaChallengeScreen`, `RecoveryCodeScreen` and `VerifyEmailScreen` components as-is —
this is a move, not a redesign.

It also owns: the Google button, the passkey button + "Lost your passkey?" link
(gated on `useConfig().passkeysEnabled && browserSupportsWebAuthn()`, resolved in a
post-mount effect to avoid an SSR mismatch), the email/password form, forgot-password,
the sign-up toggle, the `pablo:lastAuthMethod` localStorage hint, and the Terms /
Privacy footer text.

Take the RICHER of the two implementations wherever they differ. Specifically:
  - VerifyEmailScreen: LoginScreen's version (resend button + its own error state)
    wins over NativeAuthScreen's bare one.
  - Password autoComplete, minLength (15 on sign-up) and placeholder copy: LoginScreen's.
  - Layout order: Google, then passkey, then divider, then the email form — LoginScreen's
    order, applied to both.

WHAT STAYS IN EACH HOST
LoginScreen keeps: the brand panel + ThemeSwitcher, the mobile logo header, the
already-authenticated -> /dashboard effect, the forced-logout `?reason=` handling
(passed down via `notice`), `installAuthRecovery` / `consumeRecoveryNotice`, the
`?setup=` token prefill, and `finishLogin` (POST /api/login, then route to /dashboard).
It renders `<CredentialBlock showLastUsed showAuthReset ... />`.

NativeAuthScreen keeps: `redirect_uri` + `state` validation and its "Invalid Request"
screen, the "Sign-in complete" redirecting screen, and `redirectToApp` — including the
403 MFA_REQUIRED bounce to /mfa-enrollment. It renders
`<CredentialBlock allowSignUp ... />` with `onCredential={(c) => redirectToApp(c.user)}`.

CONSTRAINTS
- No behaviour change on either surface. This is a pure extraction; a user should
  not be able to tell the difference.
- Do not touch the backend, the OIDC surfaces, or any of the Auth* primitives in
  `frontend/src/components/auth/`.
- `AuthMethod` and the `pablo:lastAuthMethod` key move into CredentialBlock; nothing
  else should still reference them.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `frontend/src/components/auth/CredentialBlock.tsx` exists, is exported from
   `frontend/src/components/auth/index.ts`, and neither LoginScreen.tsx nor
   NativeAuthScreen.tsx still contains its own Google button, passkey button,
   email/password form, MFA-resolver branch, or verify-email branch. Both files
   get materially shorter.

2. New vitest component tests at
   `frontend/src/components/auth/__tests__/CredentialBlock.test.tsx` (mock
   `firebase/auth`, `@/lib/config`, `@/lib/api/passkey` and `@simplewebauthn/browser`
   the way `frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/__tests__/client.test.ts` mocks its
   dependencies). They assert:
   a. With passkeysEnabled true and WebAuthn supported, a "Sign in with a passkey"
      button and a "Lost your passkey? Use a recovery code" link render.
   b. With passkeysEnabled false, neither renders.
   c. A successful email/password sign-in calls `onCredential` exactly once with
      method "email".
   d. A successful passkey ceremony calls `onCredential` exactly once with method
      "passkey".
   e. `allowSignUp={false}` hides the "Create account" toggle.

3. `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit` exits clean.

4. `cd frontend && npx eslint src/components/auth src/lib/auth/firebase` exits clean.

5. `cd frontend && npx vitest run` passes, with no previously-passing test newly failing.

6. `make check` passes at the repo root.

title: Companion sign-in page omits passkey authentication
description:
The desktop companion's sign-in handoff page (/native-auth) offers only email/password and Google. A clinician whose second factor is a passkey has no way to complete it there: after the password step the native code exchange returns MFA_REQUIRED and the page bounces them into authenticator-app enrollment, even though they already have a passkey.

Fix: offer passkey sign-in on /native-auth the same way /login does — a 'Sign in with a passkey' button gated on the passkey config flag plus browser WebAuthn support, and the recovery-code fallback for a lost device. Both land on the same one-time-code redirect back to the app.

title: Booking modal: persist per-appointment note_type and seed the session/transcription path from it

title: Idle session can be silently revived via refresh-token swap
description:
The server-side idle timeout (backend/app/auth/idle_session.py, wired via auth/service.py::enforce_idle_session) should 401 any request whose session has been inactive past settings.idle_timeout_seconds, forcing re-auth. Two independent bugs let an idle session silently re-arm itself.

Bug A — get_current_user_no_mfa skips the idle check entirely. It verifies the Firebase token and resolves the user but never calls idle_session.check_and_touch, so every endpoint depending on it (including GET /api/users/me/status, the SPA cold-load call) bypasses the idle gate. The _no_mfa dependency exists for pre-MFA-enrollment flows; the idle check only reads uid/auth_time and has no MFA dependency, so _no_mfa should not also mean _no_idle.

Bug B — 'marker missing' is conflated with 'first request of a new session'. check_and_touch has three branches: marker+activity present -> refresh activity; marker present, activity absent -> burn marker + 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT; marker absent -> seed both keys + allow (treated as fresh sign-in). The third branch cannot distinguish a brand-new sign-in from a marker that was burned minutes ago on idle-out. Refresh-token swaps reuse the same auth_time, so a previously-timed-out session resurrects on the next request from any other live session.

Fix:
- Bug A: call idle_session.check_and_touch(decoded_token) inside get_current_user_no_mfa, after verify_firebase_token and before _resolve_user. Use a lazy import, mirroring enforce_idle_session.
- Bug B: add a tombstone key idle:revoked:{uid}:{auth_time} with TTL = _SESSION_MARKER_TTL_SECONDS. Before the marker check, redis.exists(revoked_key) -> if present, raise 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT immediately without touching marker/activity. When the burn-marker branch fires, SET the tombstone in the same pipeline as the marker delete so both land atomically. Tombstone TTL matches marker TTL because the only way a timed-out auth_time returns is via the same refresh token, itself capped by Firebase's inactivity window.

Tests (backend/tests/test_idle_session.py):
1. Tombstone set on idle expiry — extend the burn-marker test to assert redis.exists(revoked key) and TTL ~ _SESSION_MARKER_TTL_SECONDS.
2. Tombstone short-circuits later requests — pre-seed the revoked key with no marker/activity, assert 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT and that marker/activity are NOT created (regression for Bug B).
3. No-MFA path enforces idle — call get_current_user_no_mfa with Redis state matching 'marker present, activity expired', assert 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT (regression for Bug A).

Acceptance: make check passes (lint + mypy + pytest); the three tests above are present and passing.

title: New-chat first message lost — panel remounts on lazy conversation create
description:
## Symptom (user-reproduced)

Open a new chat (click "New", or just start typing on a brand-new patient), type the FIRST message, submit → the chat window flashes "Loading conversation…", the message is LOST, and the panel resets. Typing again works. Intermittent-feeling but deterministic given the code path.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanelWithHistory.tsx:95` keys the ChatPanel on the conversation id:

    key={`${activeConversationId ?? "new"}::${panelMountId}`}

The first send lazily creates the conversation: `ChatPanel.performSend` calls `onConversationCreated(id)` (`ChatPanel.tsx:239`) BEFORE it runs `streamChatMessages` (`ChatPanel.tsx:257`). The parent handler then sets `activeConversationId = id` (`ChatPanelWithHistory.tsx:107`), which changes the key from `new::N` to `<id>::N`. React unmounts the in-flight panel and mounts a fresh one with `conversationId={id}` → `hydrating = Boolean(initialConversationId) = true` → renders "Loading conversation…" (`ChatPanel.tsx:445`) and runs the hydrate effect, which `getConversation`s the just-created, still-EMPTY conversation. The optimistic user/assistant bubbles and the SSE stream belonged to the now-unmounted instance → first message + its response are lost. Second attempt works because `activeConversationId` is already set, so no key change, no remount.

"Brand-new patient, type without clicking New" is the same path: the panel starts at `conversationId=null`, first send creates → remount → loss.

## Fix

Decouple the panel's React `key` (mount identity) from `activeConversationId`:
- Key the ChatPanel on `panelMountId` ONLY. It is already bumped by the user-driven `handleSelect` / `handleNew` — the only moments a true remount is desired.
- `onConversationCreated` should update sidebar highlight (`activeConversationId`) + `listVersion`, but NOT anything in the mount key.
- Guard the hydrate path too: the `conversationId` prop passed to ChatPanel must not flip undefined→id on the LIVE instance, or the `[initialConversationId]` effect (`ChatPanel.tsx:130-165`) re-fires and clobbers in-flight messages via the prop path instead of the key path. Cleanest: track a separate `mountedConversationId` (set only by select/new) for the hydrate prop + key, leaving `activeConversationId` purely for sidebar highlighting.

## Why CI never caught it

The chat E2E (pablo-saas THERAPY-hd4h) is API-only — it hits `/api/chat/*` directly with no browser, so a React remount race is invisible to it. THERAPY-z3a5 (the known flaky chat E2E) is a DIFFERENT race (empty assistant message on SSE timeout in save-as-note), not this.

## Acceptance

- [ ] First message in a new chat persists and streams a response — no "Loading conversation…" flash, no loss
- [ ] Same for "type on brand-new patient without clicking New"
- [ ] Switching to an existing conversation via the sidebar still remounts cleanly (no stale stream)
- [ ] Browser-level regression test added (see related E2E coverage note) — API-only won't catch this
close_reason: Decoupled ChatPanel mount key/hydrate prop from sidebar-highlight state (mountedConversationId vs activeConversationId). Added jsdom+RTL regression test (verified fail-on-bug). Closing with the PR.

title: Document download 401s — <a href> can't send bearer token
description: ## Symptom Clicking a document in the patient Documents list to download it returns **401 (not authenticated)**. No document can be downloaded. ## Root cause \`frontend/src/components/patients/PatientDocuments.tsx:250\` renders the download as a plain anchor: \`\`\`tsx Download \`\`\` which points at \`/api/documents/{id}/file\` (\`frontend/src/lib/api/patientDocuments.ts:107\`). That backend route (\`backend/app/routes/patient_documents.py:405\`, \`download_document_file\`) is gated by \`Depends(require_baa_acceptance)\` — it needs the Firebase **bearer token** in the \`Authorization\` header. A raw \`\` navigation only sends cookies, never custom headers, and Pablo auth is bearer-token (not cookie-session). So the request arrives unauthenticated and 401s before the route can mint the signed GCS URL and 302 to it. The signed-URL design implicitly assumed the browser would hit \`/file\` authenticated; with header-based auth, link navigation can't. ## Fix options 1. **Return the signed URL as JSON, open it client-side (recommended).** Add/adjust the route to return \`{ url: }\` with 200 (or keep the 302 and add a JSON sibling). Frontend calls it through the authenticated fetch client (bearer token attached), then \`window.open(url)\` / \`location.assign(url)\` to the GCS signed URL directly. The signed URL itself needs no auth header — GCS authorizes via the signature — so this cleanly separates app-auth from object-auth. Audit event still fires server-side when the URL is minted. 2. Fetch \`/file\` with \`redirect: \"manual\"\`, read the \`Location\` header, then navigate. Riskier: forwarding the Authorization header into a cross-origin GCS redirect can make GCS reject the request; manual redirect handling across origins is fiddly. 3. Cookie-session auth for this one endpoint — rejected, diverges from the app's bearer-token model. Recommend option 1. ## Relationship to patient-ux-refactor epic The planned \`DocumentViewerSheet\` (design/patient-ux-refactor.md, Phase 1) loads the same signed-URL path to render PDFs/images inline. It MUST use the authenticated-fetch-then-open pattern from option 1, not a raw URL. **This bead is effectively a prerequisite for the viewer bead** — fix the download contract first, then the viewer reuses it. ## Acceptance - [ ] Clicking Download on a document returns the file, not a 401 - [ ] Works for all three categories (chart, therapist_private, psychotherapy_notes) - [ ] The patient-document-access audit event still fires server-side - [ ] Frontend obtains the signed URL via the authenticated API client (bearer token), then navigates to GCS - [ ] No token ever placed in a URL/query string
notes: PR #281 (claude/47h-document-download-signed-url) — /file returns {url} JSON, frontend fetches via authenticated client then navigates to signed GCS URL. Close on merge.
close_reason: Merged in #281 — /file returns signed URL as JSON, frontend fetches authenticated then navigates to GCS.

title: Per-tenant alembic fan-out is not thread-safe — default to serial
description:
`backend/app/db/migrate_tenants.fan_out` parallelizes `command.upgrade` calls across N tenant schemas using a ThreadPoolExecutor (default 8 workers). Alembic's EnvironmentContext is a process-global singleton, so concurrent calls into `command.upgrade` race on it — the second thread to call `context.configure` corrupts the first's state.

Symptom: no-op fan-out runs (every tenant already at head) pass cleanly, hiding the bug indefinitely. The first multi-tenant DDL after the parallelism was enabled fails on every tenant at once — observed today against ~19 schemas during the patient_documents OCR column migration. Serializing with `PABLO_MIGRATE_MAX_WORKERS=1` makes it pass.

Compounding the diagnosis: alembic's env.py calls `fileConfig()` at import, which wipes the root logger's handlers each time it runs. The per-tenant `logger.info`/`logger.exception` output never made it to Cloud Logging — only stdout `print()` calls did. Whatever path eventually re-enables parallelism should also fix this so the next failure is diagnosable on first occurrence.

Default flipped to 1 in the meantime. To re-enable parallelism safely, options worth exploring:
- Subprocess-per-tenant (each child has its own EnvironmentContext)
- Run alembic offline (`--sql`) per tenant and apply DDL ourselves
- Replace alembic at the fan-out layer with a thinner runner that drives migration scripts directly without context globals

Acceptance: fan-out can run with > 1 worker against multiple tenants with real DDL without context corruption. Per-tenant tracebacks surface in Cloud Logging on failure.

title: Claims end-to-end spec: coverage to paid against the fake clearinghouse
description: Browser proof of the whole claims path on the local harness: file a claim from the unbilled queue, watch the tracker move through submitted, payer accepted and paid on the fake clearinghouse's timers; prove the scrub blocks a bad claim before anything leaves; prove a vendor rejection renders and refiles as a corrected child.
design:
Read first: docs/design/e2e-harness.md (this repo); frontend/e2e/ as landed by the harness bead (fixtures/auth.ts, scenarios.ts, clearinghouse.ts); the claims Billing surface as landed (frontend/src/components/billing/claims/*, the tracker and claim detail routes); scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py control-number rules (REJ-DX / REJ-PTR / REJ-SUB) and its `/_fake/received`.

BUILD frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts (three tests, serial):
1. happy path: `givePatient` -> `giveCoverage` (Test Payer, member id any) -> `giveSessionWithCodes` (90834, one F-code at full specificity, POS 11, rate set) -> UI: Billing > unbilled row shows "File claim" -> click -> review shows no blocking scrub findings -> file -> tracker row reads "Queued to send" (never "Sent") -> within 10 s tracker shows submitted with a receipt time -> within 15 s payer accepted (fake 277CA) -> within 20 s paid with the amount from the fake 835; out-of-band: `clearinghouse.received()` lists exactly one submission for that control number with an Idempotency-Key header.
2. scrub blocks before the round trip: same setup with a category-level DX (F41): "File claim" review shows the blocking finding, the file button is disabled, `clearinghouse.received()` is empty.
3. vendor rejection: force a control number prefixed REJ-PTR through the test hook the assembly exposes (or a DX pointer defect the scrub does not cover) -> tracker shows rejected with the edit description rendered, and the "Correct and refile" action opens a child claim in draft carrying the parent's control-number lineage.
Add `giveCoverage` to fixtures/scenarios.ts (replacing the stub) against the coverage API. Extend the fake if a needed endpoint is missing, in the same PR.

DECISIONS CLOSED: assertions are on what the therapist sees plus the fake's received log; timers generous but bounded; no vendor network.
DO NOT TOUCH: backend behaviour; unit tests.
Verify: `make e2e` green locally; CI e2e job green. Commits human-written; no AI attribution.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `claims.spec.ts` happy path reaches `paid` on the tracker against the fake clearinghouse with the 835 amount rendered, and the fake received exactly one submission carrying an Idempotency-Key.
2. The scrub-block test proves nothing left the practice (fake received log empty) and the file action is disabled.
3. The rejection test renders the edit description and the corrected-claim action creates a draft child.
4. `giveCoverage` exists in scenarios.ts; `make e2e` and the CI e2e job are green.

title: Live clearinghouse suite: prove the adapter against the vendor's test mode, rejects included
description: The recorded fixtures prove our code; they cannot prove the vendor still behaves that way. An opt-in pytest suite runs the same operations against the clearinghouse test mode with a test key: payer search, mock eligibility, the edits that reject on purpose (each asserting our own pre-flight would have caught it), an idempotent success with replay and change, the acknowledgment and remittance round trip through the parsers, and a read-only enrollment check, every response shape-diffed against its recording so drift fails loudly.
design:
Read first: backend/app/claims/stedi.py, responses.py, and backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/README.md (which recording answers which call, and the platform provider record + Test Payer enrollment that ALREADY EXIST — never create another provider or enrollment). Clearinghouse API index: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt; the test-claims workflow page and the idempotency-keys section of the API reference.

BUILD backend/tests_integration/clearinghouse_live/ (pytest; module-level skip unless `CLEARINGHOUSE_LIVE_API_KEY` is set AND starts with the test-key prefix the credential provider recognises — never run with a production key; assert and abort if it does not):
- conftest.py: a `StediClearinghouseClient` built from the env key; a `fixture_shape(name)` helper loading the recorded JSON; `assert_same_shape(live, recorded)` comparing key sets and JSON types recursively (values may differ; missing keys or type changes fail with a diff).
- test_payer_search.py: `search_payers("STEDI")` and `("Aetna")` -> parsed `Payer` list; shape-diff against payer_search_test_payer.json.
- test_eligibility.py: mock eligibility using Stedi's documented mock member ids for active and inactive, plus an arbitrary id expecting the AAA 72 error path; shape-diff against eligibility_271_active.json.
- test_submission_rejects.py: one test per recorded edit rejection (dx_specificity: DX `F41`; dx_pointer: pointer 2 with one DX; subscriber_demographics: subscriber DOB/sex/address omitted with SBR02=18). Each builds the request from 837p_request_test_payer.json with the one defect applied, asserts HTTP 400 / `status == "ERROR"` / the expected `errors[].code`, shape-diffs against the recording, and asserts the local pre-flight would have caught it: today that is `backend/app/claims/validation.py::missing_fields` for the subscriber case; for the two DX cases write the two small pure checks (`dx_at_highest_specificity(code)` and `dx_pointers_valid(pointers, n_dx)`) in validation.py so the scrub bead can adopt them.
- test_submission_success.py: submit the recorded Test Payer request with a fresh random control number (<= 17 chars) and a fresh `Idempotency-Key`; assert `status == "SUCCESS"`; replay with the same key + body -> same `correlationId`; same key + changed charge -> 422; shape-diff.
- test_round_trip.py: after the success submit, poll `polling/transactions` (startDateTime = submit time) until a 277CA and an 835 for that control number appear (timeout 180 s, sleep 10 s), fetch each through the reports endpoints, parse with `responses.py`, assert the 835's `patientControlNumber` echoes ours and `claimPaymentAmount == totalClaimChargeAmount`; shape-diff against polling_transactions_277_and_835.json and 835_report_paid_in_full.json.
- test_enrollment.py: `list_enrollments` for the platform provider id from the README -> the Test Payer 835 enrollment is `LIVE`; shape-diff against enrollment_create_enrollment_835.json (read-only; no create).
- Makefile target `test-clearinghouse-live`; README section "Live vendor lane" mirroring docs/design/e2e-harness.md's section.
Logging/S3: never print the key, member ids or DX in assertion messages beyond the code itself.

DECISIONS CLOSED: opt-in by env var; test key only; the platform provider/enrollment from the README are reused; shape-diff is keys+types not values; no new fixtures are recorded by this suite (if a response has drifted, the test fails and a human re-records).
DO NOT TOUCH: backend/app/claims/stedi.py behaviour (if a live call reveals an adapter bug, fix it in the same PR only if it is a one-line request-shape fix; otherwise file it in the PR body); the fake clearinghouse (separate bead).
Verify: with the key exported locally (`gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=stedi-api-key --project=pablohealth-dev`), `make test-clearinghouse-live` green; without it, the whole module skips with a clear reason; `make check` green. Commits human-written, no bead ids, no AI attribution.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Without `CLEARINGHOUSE_LIVE_API_KEY` the suite skips with an explanatory reason; with a production-mode key it aborts before any call.
2. With the dev test key, all six modules pass: payer search, eligibility (active/inactive/error), the three deliberate rejects, idempotent success + replay + 422, the 277CA/835 round trip parsed by responses.py, and the read-only enrollment check.
3. Each reject test asserts the local pre-flight check (validation.py) flags the defect before the round trip.
4. Every live response shape-diffs against its recorded fixture (keys and types) and the helper fails with a readable diff on drift.
5. No key, member id or DX appears in logs or assertion output; `make check` green; PR open with no AI attribution.

title: End-to-end harness: compose stack, auth emulator, fake clearinghouse, Playwright fixtures
description: There is one Playwright scaffold with no auth and no way to run in CI. Bugs that reach users live between layers and only a browser driving the whole stack finds them. Build the harness in docs/design/e2e-harness.md: a docker-compose profile with the frontend, the Firebase Auth emulator and a fake clearinghouse that replays the recorded vendor responses, Playwright fixtures in the tiered style, the patients spec rewritten onto them, and the CI job definition.
design:
Read first: docs/design/e2e-harness.md (this repo) — the whole design; implement it as written. Reference material for fixture idioms: the deployed-environment Playwright suites you may have seen elsewhere use tiered fixtures (`onboardedUser` -> `signedInPage` with saved storageState) and API-driven "given" helpers; replicate that idiom here from scratch.

BUILD, in one PR:
1. `docker-compose.e2e.yml` extending docker-compose.yml: `frontend` (production build of frontend/, env from a `.env.e2e`), `firebase-auth` (Firebase emulator, auth only; pin the image tag), `fake-clearinghouse` (see 3). Backend env: `FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST=firebase-auth:9099`, `DATABASE_BACKEND=postgres`, clearinghouse base URL -> `http://fake-clearinghouse:8080`, a fixed webhook shared secret, MFA-required flag off (find the setting in backend/app/settings.py). Health route waits.
2. Frontend: `connectAuthEmulator(auth, ...)` behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST` in the one place Firebase is initialised (grep `initializeApp` under frontend/). One line, guarded; no other frontend change.
3. `scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py`: FastAPI app serving the Stedi endpoint paths the adapter in backend/app/claims/stedi.py calls (read that file for the exact URLs and the fixtures README for which recording answers which call), returning the recorded JSON from backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/. Rules: control numbers starting `REJ-DX` -> 837p_submission_edit_rejected_dx_specificity.json (HTTP 400), `REJ-PTR` -> ...dx_pointer.json, `REJ-SUB` -> ...subscriber_demographics.json; anything else -> 837p_submission_success_test_payer.json; 2 s later POST the backend webhook with a "transaction processed" event for a 277CA and expose the 277CA report; 5 s later the same for the 835 (835_report_paid_in_full.json with the claim's control number substituted). Sign webhooks with the Standard Webhooks HMAC the backend will verify (webhook-signature `v1,<base64>` + webhook-timestamp over `"<ts>.<body>"`). 4. `frontend/e2e/`: `playwright.config.ts` (baseURL http://localhost:3000, `webServer` = `docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml up --wait`, one chromium project, retries 0 locally / 1 in CI, trace on-first-retry); `fixtures/auth.ts` (create the user via the emulator REST API `http://localhost:9099/identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/accounts:signUp?key=any`, sign in through the real /login page once, save storageState; `signedInPage`); `fixtures/api.ts` (bearer client using the emulator ID token); `fixtures/scenarios.ts` (`givePatient`, `giveSessionWithCodes`, `giveBookingLink` — `giveCoverage` lands with the coverage bead; leave a typed stub that throws "coverage API not present"); `fixtures/clearinghouse.ts` (`received()`, `reset()`); `specs/patients.spec.ts` rewritten onto the fixtures (keep the same assertions).
5. Makefile: `e2e-up`, `e2e`, `e2e-down`. `frontend/package.json`: `test:e2e` script.
6. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: an `e2e` job per the design (compose up, playwright, upload report on failure, compose down), classified by the existing diff classifier, NOT required yet. This file is human-merged; include the change in the PR and say so in the PR body.

DECISIONS CLOSED: Firebase emulator, not a fake auth backend; the fake clearinghouse is a separate process, not monkeypatching; Playwright, not Cypress; the existing patients spec is rewritten, not deleted.
DO NOT TOUCH: backend/app/claims/* (the fake mimics them, the backend is unchanged except settings already present); anything under backend/tests/.
Verify: `make e2e` green on a clean laptop with Docker Desktop (`DOCKER_HOST=unix://$HOME/.docker/run/docker.sock` on macOS); `make check`; frontend lint/typecheck. Commit messages human-written, no bead ids, no AI attribution; PR title in plain language.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `make e2e-up && make e2e` on a clean machine with Docker runs `patients.spec.ts` green against the compose stack, authenticating through the Firebase Auth emulator via the real login page.
2. `scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py` answers every endpoint the Stedi adapter calls with the recorded fixture, honours the `REJ-DX` / `REJ-PTR` / `REJ-SUB` control-number rules, and delivers signed 277CA and 835 webhooks on its timers; `GET /_fake/received` lists what it received.

title: Claim lifecycle events: a listener registry so a deployment can route them to its own surfaces
description: Rejections, denials, stalls, deadlines and enrollment tasks are things a person must act on. Today each claims bead would write its own compliance reminder; that couples every worker to one notification surface and leaves a deployment no way to route the same events elsewhere. This bead adds one in-process event seam in backend/app/claims/events.py, mirroring the credential-provider registry, with the compliance reminder as the default listener. Everything needed is in the design field below.
design:
Read first: the claims code you extend is backend/app/claims/ (clearinghouse.py, credentials.py, stedi.py, responses.py, validation.py), merged today. Mirror the registry pattern in backend/app/claims/credentials.py (_ProviderRegistry + register_clearinghouse_credential_provider + get_...): a module-level registry, a register function, a default.

BUILD backend/app/claims/events.py:
- `ClaimEventKind = Literal["rejected","denied","partial","stalled","deadline_approaching","deadline_missed","enrollment_action_required","unmatched_remittance","paid"]`.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class ClaimEventDetail`: `codes: tuple[CodeRef, ...]` where `CodeRef(system: Literal["carc","rarc","edit","status"], code: str, description: str | None)`; `deadline_kind: Literal["filing","correction","appeal"] | None`; `deadline_date: date | None`; `days_left: int | None`; `payer_instructions: str | None` (enrollment only); `amount_cents: int | None` (paid/partial). Nothing else. No free-text fields.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class ClaimEvent`: `kind`, `control_number: str`, `claim_id: str`, `payer_id: str | None`, `payer_name: str | None`, `state: str`, `occurred_at: datetime`, `detail: ClaimEventDetail`, plus `def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]` for tests and audit.
- `ClaimEventListener = Callable[[Session, ClaimEvent], None]`.
- `register_claim_event_listener(listener) -> None` (appends; document that double registration invokes twice, like register_post_provision_hook in backend/app/db/provisioning.py), `clear_claim_event_listeners()` for tests, `emit(session, event) -> None`: calls every registered listener in order inside the caller's transaction; a listener that raises is logged at WARNING with the listener's qualname and the event kind + control number ONLY (never detail), and the exception is swallowed so the caller's state change commits regardless.
- DEFAULT listener, registered at import: `compliance_reminder_listener` — for every kind except `paid`, upsert one compliance_items row (backend/app/db/models.py ComplianceItemRow; follow the create path in backend/app/routes/compliance.py and backend/app/services/compliance_storage.py) with item_type `claim_<kind>`, label = short copy naming payer_name, control_number (first 8 chars), kind and, when present, the deadline date; due_date = deadline_date if any else occurred_at + 7 days; notes = the code descriptions joined. Idempotent on (item_type, control_number) via a lookup before insert. Register `claim_*` item types with the compliance template registry (see get_template / list_templates_for_edition in backend/app/routes/compliance.py) so the route's allow-list accepts them.
- `emit` must be safe to call with no listeners registered.

TESTS backend/tests/test_claim_events.py: registration order; a raising listener does not prevent the next listener nor the caller's commit (use a real session against sqlite or the test DB fixture the payments tests use); `to_dict()` of an event built from every kind contains none of: "member", "dob", "F41", "subscriber" (assert against a serialised event built from a realistic detail); default listener creates one compliance item and a second emit of the same event does not create a second; `paid` creates no item.

DECISIONS CLOSED, do not re-litigate: events are synchronous and in-transaction (no queue, no thread); detail carries codes and dates only; the compliance reminder is the only OSS consumer; listener errors never propagate.
DO NOT TOUCH: submit_worker/watchdog/remittance (those beads call emit later); any frontend; alembic (no schema change here; compliance_items already exists).
Verify: `make check` in backend (ruff + ruff format --check + mypy app + pytest). Commit message: human-written, no bead ids, no AI attribution. Open a PR against main titled in plain language, e.g. "Let claim lifecycle events reach a deployment's own notification surfaces".
acceptance_criteria:
1. `register_claim_event_listener` + `emit` exist in backend/app/claims/events.py with the ClaimEvent/ClaimEventDetail shapes in the design; mypy clean.
2. Test: a listener that raises is logged and swallowed; the next listener still runs; the caller's transaction commits.
3. Test: `ClaimEvent.to_dict()` for every kind contains no member id, DOB, ICD-10 code or subscriber field (string assertion on the serialised event).
4. Test: the default compliance-reminder listener creates exactly one compliance_items row per (kind, control_number) across two emits; `paid` creates none; `claim_*` item types are accepted by the compliance route's template allow-list.
5. `make check` green; PR open against main with a plain-language title and no AI attribution.

title: Clearinghouse response parsers: typed models for claim accept/reject, polling, 835 report, enrollment, from recorded fixtures
description: Every clearinghouse response the claims work has to read is now captured as a fixture under backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/ (see its README): the synchronous claim accept, three edit rejections, the polling listing with an inbound 277CA and 835, the 835 report as JSON, and the enrollment calls. This bead turns those into typed models and pure parsers so the submission worker and the remittance posting consume structured data, not vendor JSON. No network, no tables, no UI.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.
- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

FILES (new, backend/app/claims/responses.py + backend/app/models/claims_responses.py):
- Pydantic models, only the fields the claims work reads:
  * ClaimSubmissionResult: status ('SUCCESS'|'ERROR'), vendor_claim_id (claimReference.correlationId), patient_control_number, line_control_numbers (claimReference.serviceLines[].lineItemControlNumber), payer_id, errors (list of EditRejection{code, description, followup_action}), trace_id (meta.traceId). Both the 200 and the 400 bodies parse into this one model.
  * PolledTransaction: transaction_id, direction ('INBOUND'|'OUTBOUND'), mode, processed_at, transaction_set ('837'|'277'|'835' from x12.metadata.transaction.transactionSetIdentifier), business identifiers as a dict of element -> value (CLM-01, CLP-01, TRN-02, BHT-03). Plus parse_polling_page(json) -> (items, next_page_token).
  * Remittance (from the 835 report): payer name/id, payment method/date/amount from transactions[].financialInformation, and claims: list of RemittanceClaim{patient_control_number, payer_claim_control_number, claim_status_code, total_charge_cents, paid_cents, patient_responsibility_cents, claim_frequency_code, adjustments: [Adjustment{group_code, reason_code, amount_cents}], lines: [RemittanceLine{line_control_number, service_date, cpt, charge_cents, paid_cents, adjustments}]}. Money strings are dollars with optional decimals: convert with backend/app/money.py, never float.
  * EnrollmentRecord: id, status, payer stedi id, transactions requested.
- Parsers are pure functions: parse_submission(json), parse_polling_page(json), parse_835(json), parse_enrollment(json). Unknown fields ignored; missing required fields raise a typed ParseError naming the path.
- Tests: one test per fixture file asserting the parsed values (e.g. the 835 fixture parses to paid 15000 cents of 15000, patient responsibility 0, status code '1', control number '88659891'; the dx-specificity rejection parses to one error with code '33' mentioning F41). A hypothesis-free round-trip test that re-serializing a parsed model drops nothing the claims work reads.

DECISIONS CLOSED: no HTTP here (the adapter bead owns transport); no persistence here (submission/remittance beads own tables); no attempt to model the full X12; cents everywhere.
DO NOT TOUCH: backend/app/claims/stedi.py, credentials.py, clearinghouse.py (adapter bead); any table.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every file under backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/ has a test that parses it and asserts the key values named in the design.
2. parse_submission handles both the 200 and the 400 bodies and exposes errors[] on the 400.
3. parse_835 returns cents (ints) for every amount; a test proves 150.00 -> 15000 and 0.5 -> 50 via money.py.
4. mypy strict-clean on the two new modules; make check green.
5. No network access anywhere in the module (grep: no httpx/requests import).
notes:
worker exited with PR (open) — office poll tagged pr-open
PR merged (https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/927) — reconciled

title: CSP blocks Stripe.js, so card collection cannot mount in any browser
description:
The app CSP blocks Stripe.js, so card collection cannot work in a browser on any deployment. Observed on dev in a headed Playwright run:

  Refused to load the script "https://js.stripe.com/dahlia/stripe.js" because
  it violates the following Content Security Policy directive

The dialog opens, the card field never mounts, and Save card stays disabled because useStripe() never resolves. The e2e failure that reads as a selector problem ("Stripe card number field mounts") is this: there is no iframe to find.

Determined empirically with a local probe page rather than from Stripe documentation, since the last cycle was lost to a selector written from docs.
design:
Add https://js.stripe.com to script-src and to frame-src in BOTH buildCsp functions — frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts and frontend/src/lib/auth/oidc/middleware.ts. One host, two directives.

Measured, with a control to prove the probe could detect a violation at all:
- script-src: REQUIRED. The live dev run refuses js.stripe.com/dahlia/stripe.js.
- frame-src: REQUIRED. Dropping it from an otherwise-working policy produces
  "CSP-BLOCK frame-src <- https://js.stripe.com" and the element never mounts.
- connect-src api.stripe.com: NOT required for mount. Dropping it changed
  nothing — no violation, element still ready. Stripe.js proxies its API
  traffic through its own iframe, which runs on js.stripe.com and is governed
  by Stripe CSP, not ours. Left OUT deliberately rather than added on faith.

Not proven, and deliberately not pre-emptively allowed: the confirmSetup path and a 3DS challenge (which would render from hooks.stripe.com). Those could not be exercised locally because the deployment publishable key names the wrong Stripe account (separate issue). If either needs a host, the browser says so in one unambiguous line and it gets added with evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] js.stripe.com is in script-src and frame-src in both middlewares
- [ ] connect-src is unchanged
- [ ] The CSP unit tests pin both directives so a future edit cannot drop them
- [ ] make check passes

title: Remittance: 835 ingest, auto-post to claim lines, unmatched queue, patient-responsibility rollover
description: Close the loop. When the payer's remittance arrives, post allowed/paid/patient-responsibility and adjustment codes onto the claim lines, move the claim to paid, partial or denied, queue anything that cannot be matched instead of dropping it, and carry the patient's share onto the charge ledger as an amount owed, without copying adjudication detail across.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.
- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

- Table remittances (per-tenant): id, vendor_transaction_id (unique), received_at, raw jsonb (the parsed 835 from the adapter; encrypted at rest with the existing helper), parse_state, match_state CHECK IN ('matched','unmatched','partial'), matched_claim_id, payer_id, check_or_eft_number, total_paid_cents.
- backend/app/claims/remittance.py: ingest(vendor_transaction_id) fetches via get_transaction, stores the row, matches each claim payment by the echoed control number (CLP01) within the tenant; exact match -> post_lines: per service line write allowed_cents, paid_cents, patient_resp_cents, adjustments (group code + CARC + amount, RARC list); claim.total_paid_cents; state paid when all lines paid in full, partial when some, denied when paid 0 with a denial group; no match -> match_state unmatched + compliance reminder "Remittance <check#> references unknown claim". Never mutate a matched claim twice for the same remittance (unique on remittance_id + claim_id).
- Webhook/poll: extend the submission bead's webhook dispatcher for 835 'transaction processed' events; the status worker polls for remittances too.
- Rollover: when patient_resp_cents > 0 on a matched claim, create a patient_charges-side "amount owed" entry (status 'due', no card charge) referencing claim.control_number only: no CARC text, no member id, no diagnosis. Reuse the ledger row shape; do not invent a second ledger.
- UI: claim detail shows per-line adjudication with CARC/RARC codes and their standard descriptions (ship the code tables as data, e.g. backend/app/claims/carc.py); Billing page gets an "Unmatched remittances" list.

DECISIONS CLOSED: auto-post exact matches, queue everything else; the rollover carries amount + claim reference only; remittance raw payloads are financial records with no deletion path in this bead.
DO NOT TOUCH: submission worker internals beyond the dispatcher hook; charge card flows.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-06 (events): after posting, emit through `backend/app/claims/events.py::emit`: `denied` (CARC/RARC CodeRefs with descriptions from the code tables bead), `partial` (same, plus amount_cents = claim paid amount; include one CodeRef per fully-adjusted line so a consumer can tell a soft denial), `paid` (amount_cents), and `unmatched_remittance` (no claim_id; control_number = the 835's echoed PCN). Do not write reminders directly.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Fixture 835s for full pay, partial, denial and unknown-claim each produce the expected line postings, claim state and (for unknown) an unmatched row + reminder.
2. Re-ingesting the same remittance is a no-op.
3. A patient-responsibility amount creates exactly one ledger entry carrying control number and amount only (test asserts no CARC/member id/DX in the row).
4. Claim detail renders CARC/RARC descriptions from the shipped tables.
5. Migration + template regen; make check green.
6. Each fixture 835 outcome emits the matching ClaimEvent with code descriptions and amounts (fake-listener test); unmatched emits `unmatched_remittance`.
notes:
2026-09-06: the Test Payer loop is proven on the live account. Enroll the billing provider with payer STEDI for claimPayment (production key); status goes LIVE in under a minute. A test 837P to STEDI (test key, employerId = the enrolled tax id) yields an INBOUND 277CA and an INBOUND 835 within about a minute via GET core.us.stedi.com/2023-08-01/polling/transactions?startDateTime=... The 835 carries CLP-01 = patientControlNumber and TRN-02 = a remittance trace; the 277CA carries TRN-02 = the claim correlationId. Use those as the match keys.
2026-09-06: retrieve the ERA as JSON with GET https://healthcare.us.stedi.com/2024-04-01/change/medicalnetwork/reports/v2/{transactionId}/835 (277CA: .../{transactionId}/277). Shape verified on a test ERA: transactions[].detailInfo[].paymentInfo[].claimPaymentInfo.{patientControlNumber, claimStatusCode, totalClaimChargeAmount, claimPaymentAmount, patientResponsibilityAmount, payerClaimControlNumber, claimFrequencyCode} and serviceLines[].{lineItemControlNumber, serviceDate, ...}; adjustments in claimAdjustments[] and serviceLines[].serviceAdjustments[] with claimAdjustmentGroupCode + adjustmentReasonCode. Amounts are decimal strings in dollars; convert through money.py.

title: Claim submission: outbox worker, 277CA webhook + poll, corrected/void claims, watchdogs
description: File the claim and never lie about it. The claim's state column is the outbox: confirming writes 'validated' and returns; a worker submits from committed state and advances only on the clearinghouse's acceptance; acknowledgments arrive by verified webhook with polling as the backstop; every non-terminal state has a timeout that raises an alert rather than retrying into a duplicate.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.
- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

STATE TABLE (implement exactly; each row is a test):
  validated + worker submits, vendor sync-accepts (initial 277CA accepted) -> submitted
  validated + vendor sync-rejects (400 / initial 277CA rejected) -> rejected
  submitted + payer 277CA accept -> payer_accepted (more than 5 days without one -> stalled)
  submitted + payer 277CA reject -> rejected
  payer_accepted + 835 (remittance bead) -> paid | partial | denied (more than 30 days without one -> stalled; the alert names "confirm remittance enrollment is live")
  rejected | denied + human edits -> child claim (freq 7) in draft; void = freq 8
  any + watchdog timeout -> stalled (the alert IS the state; a human resumes)

FILES (backend/app/claims/):
- submit_worker.py: bounded, tenant-scoped scan of claims WHERE state='validated' ORDER BY created_at LIMIT n; builds the 837P from the snapshot (adapter models), sets usageIndicator from the credential mode, submits through call_with_retry with the idempotency class the adapter documented; on success stores vendor claim id + initial 277CA and advances; on rejection stores the 277CA edit findings on the claim and moves to rejected. A crash between submit and commit must not resubmit: write a pending marker BEFORE the call and reconcile on restart by get_transaction, the same pattern as the charge ledger's pending row.
- routes/claim_webhooks.py: POST /api/webhooks/clearinghouse. Verify the shared secret with hmac.compare_digest before reading the body; reject missing/invalid with 401, malformed with 400; dedupe on the vendor event id (unique index on a claim_events table); on a 'transaction processed' event for a 277CA, fetch the document via get_transaction, correlate by control number, advance. Follow the existing payment_webhooks.py shape.
- status_worker.py: poll backstop for claims in submitted/payer_accepted older than 1h without an event; manual POST /api/claims/{id}/status runs a 276 and stores the 277.
- watchdog.py: per the timeouts above, writes stalled + a compliance reminder carrying control number, state and age only.
- Confirm UI: the validate step becomes "Review and file" showing scrub findings; filing writes 'validated' and returns immediately with "Queued to send"; the tracker shows every hop with its receipt timestamp.

DECISIONS CLOSED: state advances only on a receipt; retries never cross a submitted boundary; resubmission reuses the parent control number lineage with frequency codes, never a fresh submit of the same content; alerts go to compliance reminders, not a new notification system.
DO NOT TOUCH: 835 handling (remittance bead), enrollment internals.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-06 (events + deadline ladder): every state change that needs a human is announced through `backend/app/claims/events.py::emit` (lands in its own bead; import it, do not write reminders directly — the default listener already writes the compliance reminder): rejected (with the 277CA/edit codes as CodeRefs), stalled (state + age), and from watchdog.py a deadline ladder: for each open claim call `deadlines.deadlines_for` and emit `deadline_approaching` at 14, 7 and 2 days before the applicable deadline and `deadline_missed` on/after it, once per (claim, deadline_kind, rung) — record the rung on the claim_events table (add `rung` to its unique key) so restarts never re-alert. title: Insurance claims through a clearinghouse: coverage, eligibility, 837P filing, remittance
description:
Let a practice check a client's insurance eligibility, build a claim from a session, file it electronically through the practice's own clearinghouse account (Stedi), track it to acknowledgment and remittance, and post what the payer paid back onto the charge ledger, with every state change driven by a receipt from the next hop and every stall alerted, never silent.

The chart already holds most of a claim: visit codes (CPT, modifiers, units, place of service, ordered ICD-10) live on the appointment; rates resolve from the client and the appointment type; the charge ledger and the unbilled-sessions queue exist. What is missing is coverage on file, the practice's billing identity, the claim assembly itself, and the transport.

Claim lifecycle (state may only advance on a positive artifact from the next hop):
  draft -> validated -> submitted -> ch_accepted (initial 277CA) -> payer_accepted (payer 277CA) -> paid | partial | denied (835)
  any -> rejected (277CA reject) [terminal until edited -> corrected claim]
  any non-terminal -> stalled (watchdog timeout) [an alert, never a retry]

Children, in dependency order: coverage tables (.1), billing identity (.2), clearinghouse client (.3), claim assembly + scrub (.4), biller export (.5), eligibility at intake (.6), enrollment (.7), submission worker + acknowledgments (.8), remittance posting (.9), EOB upload (.10), Billing page UI (.11), plus PABLO-y7u (superbill from the assembly).

Out of scope for the epic: institutional (837I) claims, secondary/tertiary claims, paper claims, any automated appeal. The epic is primary professional claims for outpatient behavioral health.

title: Charging a saved card 502s: off_session is passed on the unconfirmed PaymentIntent create
description:
Charging a saved card always fails with 502. The e2e run on 2026-09-05 hit "502 The card processor rejected the charge request"; Cloud Logging shows POST /v1/payment_intents returning 400, and a direct replay against the test-mode connected account gives Stripe reason verbatim:

  The parameter `off_session` cannot be passed when creating a PaymentIntent unless `confirm` is set to true.

The charge route creates the PaymentIntent deliberately unconfirmed (so the intent id is committed to the ledger before any money can move) and confirms it in a second call. off_session belongs on that second call, not the first. It has been on the create since the original payments PR (#906), so charging a saved card has never worked through the product — the earlier manual $150 charge went through the driver, which confirms in one step.

The payment_method_types[0]=card line added in #914 is NOT implicated: replaying without it fails identically, and replaying with it but without off_session succeeds.
design:
Move "off_session": "true" from the create payload to the confirm payload in charge_patient (backend/app/routes/patient_payments.py). The create keeps amount/currency/customer/payment_method/payment_method_types/metadata; the confirm call, which currently sends data={}, sends off_session=true.

Verified against the live test-mode connected account acct_1UCPjiAnt1oZMJjR:
- create without off_session -> 200 requires_confirmation; confirm with off_session=true -> 200 succeeded.
- same shape with tok_chargeDeclined -> confirm returns HTTP 402, error.code=card_declined, decline_code=generic_decline, so payment_intent_request keeps returning accepted=False and the ledger still records the decline code.

Unit tests: assert off_session is absent from the create body and present on the confirm body, so a move back to the create fails the suite.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] off_session is sent on the confirm call, not on the PaymentIntent create
- [ ] A unit test pins both halves (absent on create, present on confirm)
- [ ] make check passes
- [ ] After deploy to dev, specs/patient-card-charge.spec.ts no longer fails with a 502; the decline spec reports a decline rather than raising
close_reason: Fixed in pablo#917 (merged 2026-09-06). off_session moved from the unconfirmed PaymentIntent create to the confirm; verified against the test-mode connected account (success + 402 decline). Dev deploy and e2e re-run still pending.
