title: Availability engine evaluates rules and builds slots in an explicit timezone (UTC default, behaviour-preserving)
description: Step 1 of PABLO-38b. The engine reads weekday/hour/date off UTC datetimes and stamps a literal Z onto rule wall-clock minutes (backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:146-149, :209-214), so since #765 a non-UTC clinician with rules configured is refused for in-hours bookings and sees shifted slots. This bead adds a keyword-only tz to check_conflicts/get_free_slots (and SchedulingService pass-through) with a UTC default so nothing changes until PABLO-38b.2 wires the owner's preference.
design:
Make the availability engine compute in an explicit timezone instead of reading weekday/hour/date off UTC datetimes. Behaviour-preserving by construction: `tz` defaults to UTC, so every existing assertion in backend/tests/test_availability_engine.py passes unchanged; the new tests prove the zone-aware path. Parent PABLO-38b has the full diagnosis (this is a live bug since #765 for any non-UTC clinician with rules configured).

SCOPE: backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py, backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py (kwarg pass-through only), their tests. OUT OF SCOPE: routes (PABLO-38b.2 resolves the owner's timezone and passes it), frontend, recurrence.py (already zone-correct: :52-56, :78), Google sync (google_calendar_service.py:345-352 pushes UTC and stays as is).

VERIFIED POINTERS (main @ 84f9fb0), every site that must switch to local time:
- backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:7 imports only datetime/timedelta (add `from datetime import UTC, date, time, tzinfo` and `from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo` only in tests); :20-21 `_parse_iso` parses "Z" as aware UTC (keep); :24-26 `_time_to_minutes` (keep); :58 `check_conflicts(self, user_id, start, end)`; :90-92 `get_free_slots(self, user_id, date_str, duration_minutes=None) -> FreeSlotsResult`; :123-124 day window `f"{date_str}T00:00:00Z"` / `T23:59:59Z` (UTC window — replace); :146-149 slot strings `f"{date_str}T{start_h:02d}:{start_m:02d}:00Z"` (the false Z — replace); :209-214 `_check_working_hours` weekday/hour/minute off proposed_start; :244-247 `_check_block_time_range` same; :262, :291-293, :317-318, :337, :350 `strftime` date/day-boundary reads; :365, :379 weekday from `fromisoformat(f"{date_str}T00:00:00+00:00")`; :465-467 `_appointments_to_blocked_minutes` hour/minute off stored UTC start_at.
- backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:33-38 `_to_utc` (leave; inputs from routes are aware), :65-85 `_check_availability_rules(user_id, start_dt, end_dt)` → :81 `check_conflicts(user_id, start_dt, end_dt)`; :151 and :234 the two call sites (create, update); :349 recurring reads `recurrence["timezone"]`.
- Tests: backend/tests/test_availability_engine.py:36-39 `_parse_dt`, :87-90 the canonical rule + check_conflicts shape (UTC Z strings). backend/tests/test_scheduling_service.py for the service pass-through.

MECHANISM:
1. `check_conflicts(self, user_id, start, end, *, tz: tzinfo = UTC)` and `get_free_slots(self, user_id, date_str, duration_minutes=None, *, tz: tzinfo = UTC)`. Keyword-only so no positional caller breaks.
2. A single helper `_local(dt: datetime, tz) -> datetime` = `_parse_iso(dt) if str else dt` then `.astimezone(tz)`; every site listed above calls it before `.weekday()`, `.hour`, `.minute`, `.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")`. Per-rule `_check_*` methods receive `tz` (or a pre-localised datetime — pick one, apply consistently).
3. get_free_slots: `day = date.fromisoformat(date_str)`; `day_start = datetime.combine(day, time(0), tzinfo=tz)`; `day_end = day_start + timedelta(days=1)` (exclusive); query appointments between their UTC conversions (:123-124); weekday = `day.weekday()` (replaces :365/:379); slot start = `datetime.combine(day, time(h, m), tzinfo=tz).astimezone(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")` (replaces :146-149; the emitted Z is now true UTC). Blocked minutes from appointments (:465-467) use `_local(appt.start_at, tz)`.
4. scheduling.py: `_check_availability_rules(..., tz: tzinfo = UTC)`; `create_appointment`, `update_appointment`, `create_recurring_appointment` accept `tz: tzinfo = UTC` (keyword-only) and forward it at :151 / :234 and the recurring rule check. The recurring path keeps using the request's `timezone` for EXPANSION (recurrence.py) and uses `tz` for rule checks — they are the same zone in practice once 38b.2 lands, but this bead does not conflate them.
5. Do NOT change: stored rule params, `_time_to_minutes`, `_parse_iso`, FreeSlotsResult shape, the configured/unconfigured distinction from #651, the buffer/max_per_day semantics — only the frame in which they are evaluated.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: keyword-only `tz` with UTC default (behaviour-preserving; the flip happens in 38b.2); slot strings stay ISO-Z (true UTC) rather than gaining an offset — every consumer already parses Z; day window is local-midnight to next local-midnight, exclusive end; DST via ZoneInfo per-date arithmetic.

MIGRATION: none.

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI: none (synthetic fixtures) · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none · auth/RLS: none · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: none (timezone arithmetic, no known claim surface) · outbound: none.
acceptance_criteria:
1. backend/tests/test_availability_engine.py: every pre-existing test passes with NO assertion changed (UTC default preserves behaviour).
2. New tests with `tz=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")` and a working_hours rule Wednesday 09:00-17:00 (day_of_week 2): `check_conflicts(USER_ID, "2026-08-26T19:00:00Z", "2026-08-26T19:50:00Z", tz=NY)` (15:00 EDT) returns NO hard conflict; `check_conflicts(..., "2026-08-26T12:00:00Z", "2026-08-26T12:50:00Z", tz=NY)` (08:00 EDT) returns a conflict; the same two calls WITHOUT tz give the inverse results (pins that the flip is the tz, nothing else).
3. `get_free_slots(USER_ID, "2026-08-26", 50, tz=NY)` first slot start == "2026-08-26T13:00:00Z" (09:00 EDT) and last slot ends at or before "2026-08-26T21:00:00Z"; `get_free_slots(USER_ID, "2026-11-04", 50, tz=NY)` first slot == "2026-11-04T14:00:00Z" (09:00 EST after the fall-back) — DST handled per date.
4. Local day window: an appointment stored at 2026-08-27T02:00:00Z (22:00 EDT on the 26th) is counted on the 26th, not the 27th, with tz=NY — a max_per_day 1 rule refuses a second booking on the 26th local and `get_free_slots("2026-08-27", tz=NY)` is unaffected by it; with the UTC default the same appointment lands on the 27th (pins the window change).
5. Day-of-week is local: a block_day_of_week rule for Saturday (5) blocks "2026-08-30T02:00:00Z" (Saturday 22:00 EDT) with tz=NY and does not block it with the UTC default (that instant is Sunday UTC).
6. backend/tests/test_scheduling_service.py: a recording fake engine asserts `create_appointment(..., tz=NY)` and `update_appointment(..., tz=NY)` forward `tz` to check_conflicts; omitting it forwards UTC.
7. `make check` green (ruff, ruff format, mypy-clean annotations: `tzinfo`, not `Any`); no new alembic revision; no file outside backend/app/scheduling_engine/ and backend/tests/ modified.

title: Offload standalone-note dictation generation to the SOAP Cloud Tasks worker
description:
Creating a standalone note WITH a dictation transcript still runs the LLM on the request thread. backend/app/routes/notes.py create_standalone_note (:265) calls note_generation_service.generate_note inline (:348) whenever request.dictation_transcript is present (:336) — 15-60 s per request. The DB connection is released first (:346, release_db_connection) but the threadpool slot is held for the whole generation, so a handful of concurrent dictations saturate the anyio pool and every user feels it.

The two sibling call sites already moved off the request thread: upload_session persists a PROCESSING session, enqueues /api/internal/jobs/generate-soap and returns 202 (backend/app/routes/sessions.py:236-270, worker at :349-430), and upload_transcript_to_session does the same (:827-868). This is the last inline generation path. Same pattern, same queue, same invoker auth — nothing new in infrastructure.
design:
SCOPE: the standalone-note dictation path only. Persist the note skeleton, return 202, generate in a Cloud Tasks worker, mark the note complete/failed. Everything else about standalone notes (no-dictation create, PATCH edits, finalize, audit on create) stays as it is.

VERIFIED POINTERS (origin/main 84f9fb0, 2026-08-26 — re-locate line numbers before editing):
- Route: backend/app/routes/notes.py create_standalone_note :265; dictation branch :336-357 (Transcript build :337, release_db_connection :346, generate_note :348, BadRequestError NOTE_GENERATION_FAILED :353-357); persist via note_service.create_standalone_note :360; audit log_note_action(SESSION_CREATED) :368.
- Model: backend/app/models/note.py — Note has export_status :34 but NO generation status field.
- Service: backend/app/services/note_service.py create_standalone_note :115-147 (builds Note, self._notes.add).
- Queue seam: backend/app/jobs/task_queue.py enqueue(queue_name, handler_path, payload, *, dedup_key) :23-51 — thin wrapper over enqueue_cloud_task with named-task dedup.
- Worker precedent to MIRROR: backend/app/routes/sessions.py generate_soap_job :349-430 — Depends(require_cloud_tasks_invoker) for the OIDC invoker check, get_worker_session_service to scope to the job's tenant from the payload, non-retryable outcomes (unknown tenant / vanished row) answer 200 and drop, deterministic generation failure marks failed + 200, transient failure returns 503 so the queue retries, final attempt records failed. Enqueue precedent :300-315 (settings.soap_generation_task_queue, dedup_key=session.id).
- Settings: backend/app/settings.py soap_generation_task_queue :851 — REUSE this queue. No new queue, no IAM, no infra change.
- Frontend caller: frontend/src/lib/api/notes.ts createStandaloneNote :39 (post to /api/patients/{id}/notes); frontend/src/hooks/useNotes.ts useCreateStandaloneNote :86-98; consumer frontend/src/components/notes/NewNoteButton.tsx :74-79 (mutateAsync then router.push to the note page).
- Migration precedent: backend/alembic/versions/a91c5d3e7b28_audit_logs_actor_type.py (current head; additive column with a server default). Tenant template: backend/app/db/tenant_template.sql regenerated by backend/scripts/regen_tenant_template.py — notes lives in the practice schema, so the template must be regenerated in the SAME PR (CI diffs the template against alembic head and fails on drift).
- Route audit: backend/scripts/check_route_audit.py — internal job routes are listed there (:94-120); add the new route beside the existing generate-soap entry with the same rationale.
- Tests: backend/tests/test_routes_notes.py (test_creates_note_with_dictation_runs_generation :216 is the case that changes shape); worker-route test precedent backend/tests/test_routes_patient_documents.py :152 (mirrors generate_soap_job).

PLAN:
1. Model + migration: add Note.status: str = "complete" (values: processing | complete | failed). Alembic revision off the current head adding notes.status VARCHAR NOT NULL SERVER DEFAULT 'complete' — every existing row is complete; only dictation-created notes ever start as processing. Regenerate tenant_template.sql in the same commit. Expose status on the note response schema.
2. Route: when dictation_transcript is present, do NOT generate inline. Persist the skeleton via note_service.create_standalone_note with content=None and status='processing', keep the existing SESSION_CREATED audit, enqueue(settings.soap_generation_task_queue, "/api/internal/jobs/generate-standalone-note", {"note_id", "user_id", "note_type", "transcript": {"format", "content"}}, dedup_key=note.id), and return 202 with the note body (status=processing). Without dictation: unchanged synchronous 201.
3. Worker: new POST /api/internal/jobs/generate-standalone-note in notes.py, mirroring generate_soap_job line for line — require_cloud_tasks_invoker, a worker-scoped note service resolved from the payload the same way get_worker_session_service resolves the session's tenant, generate_note with the payload transcript, write content + status='complete'; on ValueError/KeyError (deterministic) write status='failed' with no content and answer 200; on transient errors answer 503 until the final attempt, then failed + 200. Audit the generation the way the SOAP worker audits SESSION_NOTE_GENERATED (actor = owning clinician, context = system-initiated delivery).
4. Frontend: the note page the NewNoteButton pushes to must poll GET /api/notes/{id} (refetchInterval while status === 'processing', stop on complete/failed) and render a "generating…" state and a failed state. Keep this small; if it balloons, ship the backend with the API documented in the PR and split the page work into a follow-up.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- A sibling internal route, NOT an overload of generate-soap with a note-shaped payload. The worker body differs (note, not session); the generation pipeline is shared.
- Transcript travels in the task payload (it is already in the request body; nothing else stores it). Do not add a transcript column.
- Reuse soap_generation_task_queue. No new queue.
- Retry/backoff/DLQ policy lives in queue config, not in app code.

title: A failed mutation tells the user nothing — non-optimistic mutations have no error path at all
description:
A create that fails shows the user nothing at all.

useAuthMutation (frontend/src/hooks/useAuthQuery.ts) only wires an onError when
the caller passes `optimistic` — it exists solely to roll the optimistic write
back. Every non-optimistic mutation in the app therefore has NO error handling
of any kind, and AppointmentModal renders no error state of its own.

So when booking an appointment fails, the mutation rejects, nothing catches it,
the modal stays open with the form filled in, and the clinician is given no
indication whether the appointment was created. The natural next move is to
press the button again.

Found while investigating PABLO-e1b (a booked appointment never reaching the
calendar). Independent of that bug and worth fixing on its own: silence on a
failed write is worse than the missing refresh, because the user cannot tell
the two apart.
design:
Handle it once, globally, rather than per call site.

react-query exposes a MutationCache-level onError on the QueryClient itself
(frontend/src/components/providers.tsx, where the QueryClient is constructed).
A single handler there covers every mutation in the app, including ones written
later that would otherwise inherit the same silence.

    new QueryClient({
      mutationCache: new MutationCache({
        onError: (error) => { /* surface it */ },
      }),
      ...
    })

Use whatever toast/notification surface the app already has; do NOT introduce a
new one for this. If there is none, render the message through the existing
error affordance rather than inventing a pattern.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate

* Global MutationCache onError, not a per-mutation onError threaded through
  useAuthMutation's options. The point is that a mutation cannot opt OUT of
  being visible by omission, which is exactly how this gap arose.
* A per-call-site override may still be added later for mutations that want
  bespoke copy; it is out of scope here.
* Do NOT change useAuthMutation's optimistic rollback path. It is correct and
  serves a different purpose.
* No PHI in the surfaced message: render the error's own text, never the
  request payload.

WHAT NOT TO TOUCH

frontend/src/hooks/useAppointments.ts — PABLO-e1b owns that file. Keep this
change to providers.tsx plus whatever the toast surface needs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The QueryClient is constructed with a MutationCache carrying an onError
   handler, so a mutation with no onError of its own still surfaces failures.
2. A failing create surfaces a visible message to the user; a unit test asserts
   the handler fires with the error when a mutation rejects.
3. The optimistic rollback path in useAuthMutation is unchanged — its existing
   tests still pass untouched.
4. The surfaced message contains the error text only, never the mutation
   variables or request payload.
5. frontend/src/hooks/useAppointments.ts is not modified by this change.
6. `make check` passes.

title: Scheduling engine speaks practice-local wall-clock, not real timezones
description:
Recorded in docs/design/public-booking.md 'What phase 1 deliberately leaves out', but the scope is engine-wide, not booking-links-specific.

The engine treats all times as practice-local wall-clock; the Z suffix in slot strings is cosmetic. The public booking page labels times as the practice's local time and relies on that convention. Real timezone conversion is an engine-wide change — a booker in another timezone currently has to reason about the practice's clock themselves.

Filed so the assumption is tracked somewhere other than a doc paragraph. Booking links make it more visible (an anonymous booker may be anywhere) but do not cause it.
design:
TRACKING PARENT — do not dispatch this bead; the work is split into PABLO-38b.1 (engine, behaviour-preserving) and PABLO-38b.2 (routes resolve the owner's timezone). Spec pass 2026-08-26, pointers verified on main at 84f9fb0.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE TODAY (it is worse than "cosmetic"): the codebase runs two incompatible time models.
- In-app path is REAL UTC: frontend/src/components/calendar/AppointmentModal.tsx:184-187 builds a local Date and :428-429 sends `start.toISOString()`; backend/app/models/scheduling.py:65-66 parses it as an aware datetime; backend/app/db/models.py:514-515 stores timestamptz; the grid and the slot picker convert back with `new Date(iso).getHours()` (frontend/src/components/calendar/editorial/dateUtils.ts:87-91; frontend/src/components/calendar/AvailabilitySlotPicker.tsx:8-15).
- The engine is WALL-CLOCK labelled Z: availability rules store "HH:MM" strings entered verbatim (frontend/src/components/settings/AvailabilitySettings.tsx:156, backend/app/db/models.py:570 JSONB params); backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:209-214 `_check_working_hours` compares the rule's minutes against `proposed_start.hour/minute` OF THE UTC DATETIME; :244-247, :262, :291-293, :317-318, :337, :350, :365, :379, :465-467 all read weekday/hour/date off UTC; :123-124 the free-slots day window is UTC midnight-to-midnight; :146-149 stamps a literal "Z" onto rule wall-clock minutes. backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:33-38 `_to_utc` stamps Z on naive input without converting.
- Consequence since #765 (rules enforced on writes): a clinician in America/New_York with a 09:00-17:00 working_hours rule is REFUSED for a 15:00 local booking (19:00Z is "outside" 09:00-17:00) and the slot picker shows 09:00Z slots as 5:00 AM. Permissive-when-unconfigured hides it until the first rule is saved. This bead should be treated as a bug, not a P3 refinement.
- The only real zone math in the engine is recurrence expansion: backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/recurrence.py:52-56, :78 (ZoneInfo from the request's `timezone` field, models/scheduling.py:89).
- A per-user timezone preference ALREADY EXISTS and the engine ignores it: backend/app/models/user.py:77 `UserPreferences.timezone` (IANA, default America/New_York, auto-detected from the browser on first save — frontend/src/components/calendar/WorkingHoursSettings.tsx:45-50, :131-137), read via backend/app/repositories/user.py:30 get_preferences and already used by backend/app/services/sync_scheduler_service.py:239. No practice-level timezone exists anywhere.
- Google Calendar push sends start_at as UTC with timeZone "UTC" (backend/app/services/google_calendar_service.py:345-352) — correct once stored values are true UTC; untouched by this work.

THE FIX, in two beads:
- 38b.1: AvailabilityEngine.check_conflicts / get_free_slots take `tz: tzinfo` (default UTC → every existing test passes unchanged); every weekday/hour/date read happens on `astimezone(tz)`; slots are built with `datetime.combine(date, time, tzinfo=tz).astimezone(UTC)` so the emitted Z is true; the day window is local midnight to next local midnight. SchedulingService forwards a `tz` kwarg. Engine + engine tests only.
- 38b.2: backend/app/routes/scheduling.py resolves `tz` from the owner's UserPreferences.timezone (fallback UTC on an invalid name) for free-slots, create, update and recurring, and passes it through. Route tests only. No frontend change: the picker and the grid already convert real UTC to the browser's zone.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: the engine's frame is the RULE OWNER's UserPreferences.timezone (rules are per-user: backend/app/scheduling_engine/models/availability.py:38 user_id) — not a new practice-level setting, not the caller's browser zone; a booker/viewer's browser zone is display conversion only. Rule params stay "HH:MM" wall-clock in the owner's zone (no data migration; every stored rule keeps its meaning). DST is handled by ZoneInfo arithmetic per date, not by a fixed offset.

OUT OF SCOPE: the public booking page's wall-clock display (lands with its own branch; once 38b.2 is in, its slots route passes the owner's tz the same way and its `slice(11,16)` rendering becomes a real `toLocaleTimeString` with the host's zone — file under the booking-links epic when phase 1 merges); a practice-level timezone; NL rule parsing reference dates (PABLO-4t0 reuses 38b.2's helper).

LANE: fleet-eligible (both children) — PHI: none (schedule math on synthetic fixtures) · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none (no settings, no migration) · auth/RLS: none · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: none (timezone arithmetic; no known claim surface) · outbound: none.
acceptance_criteria: Tracking parent: closes when PABLO-38b.1 and PABLO-38b.2 are both merged and a New York clinician with a 09:00-17:00 working_hours rule can book 15:00 local (start_at 19:00Z) and sees a 9:00 AM first slot in the picker.
notes: eng-head 2026-08-26: bumped P3→P1 — LIVE regression since pablo#765: availability.py:209-214 compares HH:MM rules against the UTC hour while AppointmentModal.tsx:428 sends real UTC; a NY 09:00-17:00 rule refuses a 15:00 local booking and the picker shows 5:00 AM slots. Hidden only while no rules exist. Not yet in BASE_IMAGE — land 38b.1 → 38b.2 before the next bump if possible.
close_reason: Fixed across three PRs: #777 (engine evaluates rules in an explicit tz), #779 (routes resolve the owner's preference), #787 (offset-less input reads as the practice's wall-clock, closing the _to_utc/_local residual). The #765 regression -- NY 3pm refused, picker showing 09:00Z as 5am -- is gone. Recurring-series path keeps its own explicit timezone field, deliberately untouched.

title: Chart invariant: an unverified email never attaches a booking to an existing chart
description:
Holds independently of the require_email_confirmation flag — this is the invariant that survives an operator relaxing that flag.

A matched email either completes confirmation or lands as a PENDING record the clinician reconciles (the EHR-import client-resolution shape) before it touches the chart. Relaxing the flag trades 'confirm to finalize' for 'book instantly as a fresh or pending record'; it can never reopen spoofed writes onto a real chart.

One carve-out: a 'personal'-edition practice, which declares it holds no clinical charts, may skip verification on attach-by-match — a rule keyed to a declared fact, not a toggle.

This closes the phase-1 limit recorded in docs/design/public-booking.md: today anyone who knows a client's email can put an attacker-authored note on that client's chart and the clinician's calendar.
design:
Spec pass 2026-08-26 (Pablo Engineering Head, pass 1). Pointer conventions as in PABLO-e3a.2: (main) = verified on OSS main at 84f9fb0; [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] = verified on origin/claude/public-booking-links. Same PRECONDITION as .2 (phase 1 on main — blocker bead PABLO-e3a.12), plus .2 and .3 merged: this bead reuses .2's pending placeholder shape and .3's promotion step.

THE INVARIANT, in one sentence: an email that has not been verified by a confirm click never causes a booking to attach to an existing chart — regardless of require_email_confirmation. After .2/.3, the born-true path already satisfies it (a hold is always a fresh placeholder; attach happens only after the click). This bead closes the OPERATOR-RELAXED path (require_email_confirmation = false, set by direct SQL), which today still runs phase 1's find_by_email reuse — the spoofed-write on a real chart that docs/design/public-booking.md [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] records as phase 1's real limit — and adds the personal-edition carve-out.

SCOPE:

1. THE RELAXED PATH. In create_public_booking (backend/app/routes/public_booking.py:280-350 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]), replace the `_find_or_create_patient` call (:247-277) on the instant path with `_patient_for_instant_booking(request, ctx, patient_repo, http_request, audit)`:
   - `existing = patient_repo.find_by_email(email, owner)` (excludes pending rows since .2).
   - No match → create an ACTIVE patient exactly as phase 1 does, plus `origin="public_booking"` (backend/app/db/models.py:136-143 main — the column exists for this; phase 1 predates it and does not set it). Audit PATIENT_CREATED changes={"source": "public_booking"}.
   - Match AND the practice is NOT personal-edition → create a PENDING placeholder exactly as .2's hold path does (status "pending", origin "public_booking", fresh id) and book the CONFIRMED appointment against the placeholder. The existing chart is never read further and never written. Audit PATIENT_CREATED changes={"source": "public_booking", "status": "pending", "reason": "unverified_email_matched_chart"} — a marker, no PHI. The clinician sees the appointment on the calendar under the placeholder's name; the chart list does not show the placeholder (.2's quarantine); resolving it is a person's job — see out-of-scope.
   - Match AND the practice IS personal-edition → return `existing` (attach-by-match), byte-for-byte phase-1 behaviour. Rule keyed to the declared fact, below.
   The confirmed-instant appointment, gcal push, audit and response (status "confirmed") are otherwise unchanged. Same response keys for every branch — the no-oracle property must survive (test_booking_reveals_nothing_about_existing_patients, backend/tests/test_public_booking_routes.py:315-364 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]).

2. THE DECLARED FACT. practices.edition exists on main (backend/app/db/platform_models.py:106-111, CHECK in ('therapist','personal'); enum backend/app/models/enums.py:109 PracticeEdition). Nothing in backend/app reads it yet. Plumb it to the public path the same way practice_schema already travels:
   - BookingLink dataclass (backend/app/models/booking_link.py:48-68 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]) gains `practice_edition: str | None = None` beside practice_schema (:64-68) — "populated only by get_by_slug".
   - PostgresBookingLinkRepository.get_by_slug (backend/app/repositories/postgres/booking_link.py:49-61 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]) already outer-joins PracticeRow for schema_name; select PracticeRow.edition too and set link.practice_edition. In-memory get_by_slug leaves it None unless a test sets it on the link object.
   - `_is_personal_edition(link) -> bool` = `link.practice_edition == PracticeEdition.PERSONAL.value`. None (single-schema deployment with practice_id NULL, or any unknown value) → False → therapist semantics. The safe default is the clinical one.
   - Not a setting, not a booking-link column, not a request field: the only way to get the carve-out is to be a practice whose registry row declares 'personal'.

3. TESTS ONLY, for the born-true path: re-assert that a hold never attaches (already pinned by .2's test_hold_never_attaches_to_an_existing_chart) — do not duplicate the test, reference it in the PR description.

4. DOC. Update the "chart invariant" paragraph of docs/design/public-booking.md [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] from "must land" to what shipped, in engine terms (OSS is public: no SaaS/tier/bead-id references), and move "Can an unverified email attach writes to a real chart?" from "Yes" to "No, since <this change>" with the relaxed-path and personal-edition wording above.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not touch:
- PABLO-e3a.2 owns the column, hold placement, quarantine filters, the send. PABLO-e3a.3 owns confirm/promote/sweep/lapsed-click. Neither changes here.
- A reconciliation UI/API for placeholder records created by the relaxed path (merge into the matched chart, or promote to a new chart) is NOT filed anywhere in PABLO-e3a. It is only needed by deployments that relax the flag; the born-true path resolves itself at the click. Flagged in the spec-pass report for Kurt to file if wanted; do not build it here.
- Do not introduce a "reconcile" flag, an allowlist of trusted domains, or any other second path around the invariant.
- Frontend: nothing (the booker sees the same confirmed card either way).

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- On the relaxed path a matched email lands as a PENDING placeholder with a CONFIRMED appointment (the flag traded "confirm to finalize" for "book instantly"; it does not trade away the chart). Not a pending appointment, not a rejection, not a silent fresh active chart (an active duplicate of a real client is worse than a quarantined one).
- Carve-out is keyed to practices.edition == 'personal' read through get_by_slug; no other signal qualifies; None means therapist.
- The placeholder created by the relaxed path uses exactly the .2 shape (status "pending", origin "public_booking") so the same quarantine, sweep-exclusion (it carries no token hash and is not pending-appointment-backed, so .3's sweep never touches it) and any future reconciliation apply uniformly.
- find_by_email semantics (exact, case-insensitive, live, non-pending, owner-granted) are unchanged.
- Audit markers only; no new AuditAction values.

SEQUENCING: after PABLO-e3a.3 (dependency edge on the board). Last of the three.

MIGRATIONS: none (edition column already exists on main; booking_links unchanged).

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI/HIPAA: this is a PHI-integrity control (who may write onto a chart) but it is built and tested entirely on in-memory fixtures; no real data, no PHI in logs, audit carries markers and ids — clear. money/entitlement: none — clear. prod infra: no migration, no infra — clear. auth/RLS design: this changes what an anonymous booker's unverified claim may do, not clinician authentication or any RLS policy; queries still run armed as the owner — I judge this NOT auth/RLS design; it is application-level integrity logic. vendor dashboards: none. patent-adjacent: OSS, trigger holds in full; "do not attach unverified identity to a record" is a textbook control, no marker in docs/design, not a known claim surface — clear. outbound communication: no send in this bead; tests use the in-memory sender via the shared fixture — clear.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE (spec pass 2026-08-26). In-memory tests in backend/tests/test_public_booking_routes.py [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]; `make check` in the OSS repo (ruff + format + mypy + pytest). All relaxed-path tests use `_link(require_email_confirmation=False)`.

1. The invariant with the flag OFF. `test_relaxed_link_never_attaches_unverified_email_to_existing_chart`: seed an active patient (email client@example.com, names Realfirst/Reallast); POST a booking with that email and names Wrong/Name on a relaxed link → 201, body status "confirmed"; the created appointment's patient_id != existing.id; the patient at that id has status "pending", origin "public_booking", first_name "Wrong"; existing chart names unchanged; `patient_repo.list_by_user(OWNER_ID)` total == 1; audit contains a patient_created whose changes carry reason "unverified_email_matched_chart". GET slots no longer offers the slot.

title: Hold semantics: pending_confirmation appointments + quarantined pending patients
description:
A hold IS an appointment row with status pending_confirmation, paired with a quarantined 'pending' patient record invisible in chart lists. Because the slot engine already treats every non-cancelled appointment as busy, a hold participates in ALL scheduling rules with no engine change: the slot leaves everyone else's list, buffers apply around it, and it counts toward max-per-day.

TTL ~15 minutes. Expiry flips the row to cancelled (releasing the slot through the same path a cancellation does) and sweeps the pending patient. Confirm flips it to confirmed, promotes the patient record, and triggers calendar sync. An expired-hold click must not be a dead end.

Also resolve the same-slot write race the design doc records: two confirmations against one slot must not both finalize.
design:
Spec pass 2026-08-26 (Pablo Engineering Head, pass 1). Pointer conventions as in PABLO-e3a.2: (main) = verified on OSS main at 84f9fb0; [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] = verified on origin/claude/public-booking-links. Same PRECONDITION as .2: phase 1 must be on main first (blocker bead PABLO-e3a.12, Kurt-paired), and this bead additionally needs .2 merged (the column, appointments.confirmation_token_hash, the status='pending' patient, HOLD_TTL_MINUTES).

WHAT A HOLD IS, restated so nobody rebuilds it: an appointments row with status 'pending' + pending_expires_at (engine request mode, #746, backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:143-148, :266-287 main), carrying confirmation_token_hash (.2), pointing at a patients row with status 'pending' and origin 'public_booking' (.2). Because list_overlapping and the availability engine treat every non-cancelled row as busy (backend/app/repositories/postgres/appointment.py:97-119 main; backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:296,321 main), a hold already leaves everyone else's slot list, has buffers applied around it and counts toward max_per_day WITH NO ENGINE CHANGE. Item 1 of acceptance only PINS that; it builds nothing.

SCOPE (backend only; the booker-facing confirm PAGE is a recommended new frontend bead, not yet filed):

1. TOKEN LOOKUP. New AppointmentRepository method `get_by_confirmation_token_hash(user_id: str, token_hash: str) -> Appointment | None` — ABC at backend/app/scheduling_engine/repositories/appointment.py:18 (main), in-memory impl beside list_expired_pending (:292), Postgres impl beside its sibling (backend/app/repositories/postgres/appointment.py:217-237 main), filtering `user_id == owner AND confirmation_token_hash == :hash` regardless of status (the branches below need cancelled rows too). The partial index from .2 backs it.

2. SERVICE CHANGES in SchedulingService (scheduling.py, main):
   a. confirm_appointment (:289-304): before flipping to CONFIRMED, run `self._reject_if_overlapping(user_id, _as_datetime(start_at), _as_datetime(end_at), exclude_appointment_id=appointment_id)` (:87-108; the _as_datetime coercion mirrors update_appointment :226-227). This is what makes two holds on one slot unable to BOTH finalize: the second confirm raises AppointmentConflictError. It is also correct for #746's own request mode (confirming a request that now collides should fail), and it never fires in the normal case because the hold itself is what blocks the slot.
   b. NEW `finalize_lapsed_hold(appointment_id, user_id) -> Appointment`: requires status CANCELLED and confirmation_token_hash not None (else InvalidAppointmentError); overlap check as in (a); sets CONFIRMED, pending_expires_at None, updated_at now. This is the "expired-hold click is not a dead end" path.
   c. cancel_appointment (:322-328): also set `appointment.confirmation_token_hash = None`. A clinician who cancels a hold in-app kills its token; the sweep (expire_pending_appointments :306-320) deliberately does NOT clear the hash, so a lapsed hold stays distinguishable from a clinician-cancelled one by "cancelled AND hash present". Do not change expire_pending_appointments.
   d. update_appointment allowed_fields (:194-214): add "confirmation_token_hash" ONLY if you need it; the design below never clears the hash on confirm (see decisions), so you may not need it.

3. THE SWEEP, lazy, as a route dependency. NEW `sweep_expired_holds(ctx=Depends(get_public_booking_context), scheduling=Depends(get_public_scheduling_service), patient_repo=Depends(get_patient_repository), audit=Depends(get_audit_service), http_request: Request)` in backend/app/routes/public_booking.py [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]: `for appt in scheduling.expire_pending_appointments(ctx.link.user_id)` → skip rows with confirmation_token_hash None (a request from another surface: expire it — that is the method's contract — but its patient is a real chart, never sweep it) → `patient = patient_repo.get(appt.patient_id, owner)`; if patient and patient.status == "pending": patient_repo.delete(patient.id, owner) (soft delete, backend/app/repositories/postgres/patient.py:273 main) and audit PATIENT_DELETED as the owner with changes={"source": "public_booking_hold_expired"}. Attach as `dependencies=[Depends(sweep_expired_holds)]` on the slots GET, the booking POST and the new confirm POST. Runs armed as the owner inside the tenant (the context dep does that: public_booking.py:92-124 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]). DatabaseSessionMiddleware commits on any method (backend/app/db/middleware.py:107-115 main), so a sweep triggered by a GET persists. No cron, no Cloud Tasks: a hold expires the next time anyone looks at that link, which is exactly when the slot matters. (The list_recently_deleted filter from .2 keeps swept placeholders out of the clinician's "Recently deleted" tab; hard-purge removes them on its normal clock.)

4. THE CONFIRM ENDPOINT. `POST /api/public/booking-links/{slug}/confirm`, body `{"token": str}` (NEW `ConfirmPublicBookingRequest` in backend/app/models/booking_link.py [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]), response PublicBookingConfirmation with status "confirmed", status_code 200. POST, not GET: mail scanners and link previewers fetch GET links and would consume or trigger the confirm; the page auto-POSTs on load (frontend bead). Router-level browse limiter applies (60/min/IP — a 256-bit token is not brute-forceable inside it); do not add the write limiter. Handler order:
   a. `_require_owner_may_accept_bookings(ctx.owner)` (:158-197 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]) — a wound-down practice does not finalize either.
   b. `appt = appt_repo.get_by_confirmation_token_hash(owner.id, sha256(token))`; None → NotFoundError("This confirmation link is not valid.") — one message for never-existed, wrong-link, and clinician-cancelled (hash cleared): no oracle.
   c. by status:
      - "confirmed" → return 200 immediately (idempotent: second click, double submit). No writes.
      - "pending" → `scheduling.confirm_appointment(appt.id, owner.id)`; on AppointmentConflictError: cancel THIS hold (scheduling.cancel_appointment), soft-delete its placeholder patient (if status pending), audit both, raise ConflictError(_SLOT_TAKEN) where _SLOT_TAKEN = "That time was taken while you were confirming. Please pick another slot." The loser's slot is thereby released.
      - "cancelled" (hash present ⇒ lapsed hold) → re-derive free slots for the hold's date with the engine (same call as the POST's re-validation, :296-300 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]); if a slot with start == appt.start_at is offered → `scheduling.finalize_lapsed_hold(...)` and `patient_repo.restore(appt.patient_id, owner.id)` (backend/app/repositories/patient.py:132 main; 30-day window). If the slot is not offered, or restore returns None (purged) → ConflictError(_SLOT_TAKEN) and leave the row cancelled.
      - anything else (completed/no_show — impossible for a hold) → NotFoundError as in (b).
   d. PROMOTE the placeholder — `_promote_pending_patient(appt, ctx, patient_repo, scheduling, http_request, audit)`: `placeholder = patient_repo.get(appt.patient_id, owner)`; if placeholder is None or placeholder.status != "pending": return (already promoted). `existing = patient_repo.find_by_email(placeholder.email, owner)` — .2 made that exclude pending rows, so this is "the real chart with this now-VERIFIED email", if any.
      - existing found → `scheduling.update_appointment(appt.id, owner, patient_id=existing.id)` (patient_id is an allowed field, :194-214), then `patient_repo.delete(placeholder.id, owner)`; audit APPOINTMENT_UPDATED changes={"source": "public_booking", "attached": "verified_email"} and PATIENT_DELETED changes={"source": "public_booking_placeholder_merged"}. The existing chart's own fields are never written (the no-oracle test's "unchanged" assertion continues to hold).
      - none → `placeholder.status = "active"`; `patient_repo.update(placeholder)` (backend/app/repositories/patient.py:96 main); keep origin "public_booking" (it is provenance, not state); audit PATIENT_UPDATED changes={"source": "public_booking", "status": "active"}.
   e. `appt = _sync_appointment_to_google(scheduling, gcal_service, ctx.owner, appt)` (backend/app/routes/scheduling.py:214-235 main; best-effort, never fails the confirm). Audit APPOINTMENT_UPDATED as the owner with changes={"source": "public_booking", "status": "confirmed"}.
   f. Return PublicBookingConfirmation(status="confirmed", link-derived fields only, same keys as the POST).
   Route-audit guardrail (backend/scripts/check_route_audit.py:383-406 main): the handler injects and calls the tenant AuditService, so it needs no entry in either exempt list. The sweep's audit calls happen inside the dependency and do not count for the handler — that is fine, the handler audits on its own.

5. SAME-SLOT WRITE RACE. Two bookers can pass the POST's re-validation in the same instant and both insert holds (the window the design doc records). Resolution in this bead is at CONFIRM time via 2a: the first confirm wins, the second gets 409 _SLOT_TAKEN and its hold is cancelled. The design doc's partial unique index on (user_id, start_at) over non-cancelled rows is NOT added here — see decisions.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not touch:
- PABLO-e3a.2 owns the column, the token hash write, the pending patient creation, the quarantine filters and the send. Do not re-open the hold path except to add the sweep dependency.
- PABLO-e3a.4 owns the relaxed-flag path and the personal-edition carve-out (_find_or_create_patient stays as is).
- Frontend bead (recommended, not yet filed; NOT PABLO-e3a.12, which is the phase-1 landing blocker): /book/{slug}/confirm page that auto-POSTs the token, renders the confirmed card on 200, and on 409 shows "pick another time" with a link back to /book/{slug}; plus the pending-state copy on the booker page. Nothing in frontend/ changes in this bead.
- No cron / scheduler wiring (sync_scheduler_service.py) — lazy sweep only.
- No reconciliation UI for pending records (none is filed; it is only needed by .4's relaxed path).

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- Confirm is POST with the token in the body. GET would be consumed by link scanners.
- The hash is NOT cleared on confirm: a second click is an idempotent 200 rather than a 404, and the token confers nothing beyond confirming (the response is link-derived fields only). cancel_appointment clears it; the sweep does not.
- Lapsed-hold revival is bounded by patient restore (30 days) and by the slot still being FREE per the engine's own free-slot computation (rules + collisions), not merely non-overlapping. Slot taken or placeholder purged → 409 _SLOT_TAKEN, never a silent rebook of a different time.
- Verified email attaches to an existing chart by re-pointing appointment.patient_id and soft-deleting the placeholder. The existing chart's fields are never written. That IS the "verified identity chain" the epic names; the unverified case is .4.
- Race closed at confirm by the overlap check, not by a unique index. Reason: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` over existing appointments fails the migration on any deployment holding pre-#760 duplicate rows (two non-cancelled appointments at one start), which cannot be verified from here and would block a deploy. If Kurt wants the index as a backstop it is a separate bead with a pre-flight duplicate query; it is not needed to satisfy this bead's acceptance.
- Sweep is a route dependency on exactly three routes; not in get_public_booking_context (that dep must stay read-only), not a background task.
- Loser cleanup (cancel hold + soft-delete placeholder) is explicit so the in-memory and Postgres paths agree; do not rely on middleware rollback.
- Audit stays attributed to the owner with source markers (PABLO-e3a.6 fixes the actor); no new AuditAction values — APPOINTMENT_UPDATED / PATIENT_UPDATED / PATIENT_DELETED (backend/app/models/audit.py:18-22,62-66 main) with changes markers are enough.

SEQUENCING: after PABLO-e3a.2 (dependency edge on the board); before PABLO-e3a.4. The frontend page (recommended bead, not yet filed) can be built in parallel once this bead's response contract (200/404/409 + status field) is on main.

MIGRATIONS: none. This bead adds no columns; it reads .2's.

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI/HIPAA: handles patient placeholders and re-points an appointment to a real chart, but only under in-memory fixtures; no real data, no PHI in logs (slug/kind only), audit entries carry ids and markers — clear. money/entitlement: reuses the subscription gate unchanged; nothing charged or entitled — clear. prod infra: no migration, no infra, no destructive op — clear. auth/RLS design: token redemption is identity verification of an anonymous booker; every query runs armed as the owner through the phase-1 context; no RLS policy or clinician auth path changes — I judge this NOT auth/RLS design, though a reviewer should read the confirm handler's status branches with care. vendor dashboards: none. patent-adjacent: OSS, trigger holds in full; hold/confirm/expiry is ordinary booking-system mechanics, no marker in docs/design, not a known claim surface — clear. outbound communication: this bead sends nothing (the send is .2's); tests use InMemoryEmailSender; no live send in the done-signal — clear.

title: Per-link require_email_confirmation, born true, no UI
description:
A column on booking_links whose true default is enforced at the DATABASE layer on insert, and which is deliberately ABSENT from the management API schemas and every settings surface. Every link ever created requires confirmation; relaxing a specific link is a conscious per-deployment operator action (direct DB update), not a preference a clinician can flip while chasing booking conversion.

When required, the booking POST places a short-TTL hold on the slot (rate-limited, capped per IP) and sends the confirmation link through the email seam; the appointment finalizes on click.

See docs/design/public-booking.md, security posture section. Depends on the email seam.
design:
Spec pass 2026-08-26 (Pablo Engineering Head, pass 1). Pointers marked (main) were verified on OSS main at 84f9fb0; pointers marked [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] were verified on origin/claude/public-booking-links (12 commits, no PR, 53 behind main).

PRECONDITION — READ FIRST. Phase 1 (the booking_links table, the /api/public/booking-links/* routes, the booker page) lives ONLY on branch claude/public-booking-links. Nothing in this bead can start until that branch is on main. Landing it needs: (a) a rebase/merge onto main, (b) re-pointing c8d2f4a71e93_booking_links_table.py's down_revision from b3a7f92c15e4 to the current single head a91c5d3e7b28 (c7e2b81f40a9 also revises b3a7f92c15e4, so merging as-is forks the chain), (c) a template regen because d1e7c4a92b58 adds a tenant index. That landing is NOT this bead — it is PABLO-e3a.12 (Kurt-paired), a dependency edge on the board.

1. THE COLUMN. `require_email_confirmation BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true` on platform.booking_links.
   - Alembic: NEW backend/alembic/versions/<rev>_booking_links_require_email_confirmation.py, raw `ALTER TABLE platform.booking_links ADD COLUMN require_email_confirmation BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true` (same raw-SQL style as c8d2f4a71e93_booking_links_table.py [does not exist on main yet: branch-only]). down_revision = whatever `cd backend && poetry run alembic heads` prints AFTER phase 1 lands (expected d1e7c4a92b58); exactly one head afterwards. booking_links is PLATFORM-scoped, so this migration changes nothing in backend/app/db/tenant_template.sql (the template captures the practice schema only).
   - ORM: BookingLinkRow in backend/app/db/platform_models.py:537 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] gains `require_email_confirmation: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, nullable=False, server_default=text("true"))` — server_default and NO Python `default=`. That is what "enforced at the database layer" means: the INSERT omits the column and Postgres fills it. (Contrast is_active at :565, which uses a Python default — do not copy that shape.)
   - Domain: BookingLink dataclass, backend/app/models/booking_link.py:48-68 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] gains `require_email_confirmation: bool = True` (after updated_at, next to practice_schema — dataclass default ordering). The in-memory repo therefore also births links true.

Management routes backend/app/routes/booking_links.py:55-82 [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] and :98-119 never read or write it.

No settings field, no env var, no frontend surface. Relaxing a link is `UPDATE platform.booking_links SET require_email_confirmation = false WHERE slug = ...` by whoever runs the database — document that one line in docs/design/public-booking.md [does not exist on main yet: branch-only] — its "Per-link require_email_confirmation" paragraph — and nowhere else.

title: Public booking links: phase 2 — verified identity, safe slugs, honest audit
description:
Booking links shipped in phase 1 behind PUBLIC_BOOKING_ENABLED (default off), covering the display card, free slots, and a booking POST that creates or reuses a patient record. See docs/design/public-booking.md.

Phase 1 books *time* safely. It does not yet establish *identity*: an unverified email can attach an appointment to a real chart, a released slug can be re-registered by another clinician, and the audit trail attributes anonymous bookings to the clinician. This epic is everything standing between phase 1 and positioning booking links as client self-scheduling against live charts.

Scope: the design doc's phase-2 plan (email confirmation, hold semantics, the chart invariant, the email seam, the CAPTCHA rung) plus the deferred findings from the 2026-08-20 branch review (slug tombstone, audit actor fidelity) and the missing clinician-facing management UI.

Out of scope: the four fixes already landed on claude/public-booking-links (owner subscription gate, rate-limit split, savepoint-scoped create, cross-user scoping tests).

title: NL rule entry v2: relative-date rules via deterministic resolution
description: Follow-up to the natural-language availability rule entry: v1 deliberately excluded the two date-carrying rule types (block_date_range, block_specific_dates) because sentences like "block next Friday" need calendar arithmetic, and the parse model is forbidden from computing dates. This closes that gap the same way the engine handles everything else — deterministically: the model emits date-intent TOKENS (day-of-week, "next"/"this" modifier, explicit date strings, ranges), and a pure resolver function turns tokens into concrete dates from a reference point, so "block next Friday" becomes a previewed, confirmable block on the actual date.
design:
Extends the v1 natural-language rule entry (merged as #753). All pointers below were re-verified against main on 2026-08-26.

SCOPE: the two date-carrying rule types the v1 frozenset excludes — block_date_range (engine params {"start_date","end_date"}, backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:335-336) and block_specific_dates ({"dates": [...]}, availability.py:349). The model emits date-intent TOKENS; a pure resolver computes concrete dates from a reference date; the existing preview/confirm UI shows the resolved dates; creation still flows only through POST /api/availability/rules (backend/app/routes/scheduling.py:809 create_availability_rule).

OUT OF SCOPE: engine slot computation; recurrence (recurring blocks are the existing day-of-week types, covered by v1); the settings form; timezone semantics of the engine itself (PABLO-38b — this bead only needs a reference DATE, which it derives from the user's timezone preference exactly as PABLO-38b.2 will).

V1 SUBSTRATE (verified):
- backend/app/services/availability_parse_service.py:42-51 COVERED_RULE_TYPES (six types; the two date types are out per the docstring at :19-20); :101 _RESPONSE_SCHEMA (a JSON-schema dict, not pydantic — proposal items carry rule_type, enforcement, day_of_week, start, end, max, minutes, human_summary); :126 ProposedRule / :136 AvailabilityParseResult dataclasses; :167-218 per-type param validators + _PARAM_VALIDATORS; :278-283 fail-closed: ONE bad proposal rejects the whole response with _DEFAULT_COULD_NOT_PARSE (there is no exception — coercion returns None); :299 `if rule_type not in COVERED_RULE_TYPES: return None`; :224 constructor takes `llm_gateway: StructuredLLMGateway | None` (tests pass FakeStructuredLLMGateway, backend/tests/test_availability_parse_service.py:23-34); :15-18 and :66-70 the prompt receives no date/timezone and tells the model to refuse dates; no datetime/now() anywhere in the file.
- Route: backend/app/routes/scheduling.py:896-897 POST /api/availability/rules/parse; :909 per-user daily limiter; :913 release_db_connection() BEFORE the LLM call — any DB read this bead adds must happen above that line.
- Models: backend/app/models/scheduling.py:215 ParseAvailabilityRulesRequest, :221 ProposedAvailabilityRule(rule_type, enforcement, params, human_summary), :234 ParseAvailabilityRulesResponse.
- Timezone preference: backend/app/models/user.py:77 UserPreferences.timezone (IANA string, default America/New_York); repository backend/app/repositories/user.py:30 get_preferences(user_id).
- Frontend preview already renders the two date types: frontend/src/components/settings/NaturalLanguageRuleEntry.tsx:26 proposalToRule, :42 ProposalCard, :82 `summarize(rule)`; summarize handles block_date_range/block_specific_dates at frontend/src/components/settings/AvailabilitySettings.tsx:129-140 and :168-171. Confirm fires useCreateAvailabilityRule (NaturalLanguageRuleEntry.tsx:43, :51-52; frontend/src/hooks/useAvailability.ts:32). So the preview of a RESOLVED date needs no new rendering code — only a test.

MECHANISM:
1. TOKENS. Extend the proposal item in _RESPONSE_SCHEMA (:101) with a nullable `date_intent` object: {"items": [ {"explicit": "YYYY-MM-DD"|"MM-DD"|null, "day_of_week": 0-6|null, "modifier": "this"|"next"|null} ], "range": boolean}. Exactly one of explicit / day_of_week per item. `range: true` means items[0]..items[1] and yields block_date_range; otherwise one date per item and yields block_specific_dates. The prompt (:66-70) is rewritten to describe this grammar: copy dates the user wrote (numeric month-day, year only if the user said it), map weekday words to 0-6 (0 = Monday, matching the engine), map "next"/"this" to modifier — and never compute a date. A date-type proposal that carries start_date/end_date/dates directly (i.e. the model resolved) is rejected by the validator exactly like :299/:304-306 today (return None → whole response could_not_parse). Extend COVERED_RULE_TYPES with the two date types and update the pinning test at backend/tests/test_availability_parse_service.py:39 (rename to eight types; do not delete it).
2. RESOLUTION. New pure module backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/date_intent.py (NEW): frozen dataclasses DateToken / DateIntent and `resolve_date_intent(intent: DateIntent, reference: date) -> ResolvedDates | UnresolvableDateIntent` where ResolvedDates carries either (start_date, end_date) or dates[] as ISO strings and UnresolvableDateIntent carries a human-readable reason. Plain date/timedelta arithmetic, no ZoneInfo, no clock — the caller supplies `reference`.
3. REFERENCE DATE. The parse service gains `parse(self, text: str, reference_date: date | None = None)`. The route resolves it ABOVE :913: `tz = ZoneInfo(user_repo.get_preferences(ctx.user_id).timezone)` (fall back to UTC on ZoneInfoNotFoundError), `reference_date = _now(tz).date()` where `_now` is a module-level callable tests monkeypatch. If reference_date is None and a date-type proposal appears, the service returns could_not_parse (fail closed, no guessing).
4. PARAMS. The service resolves tokens itself and emits ProposedRule.params in the ENGINE shape ({"start_date","end_date"} or {"dates": [...]}) — the token grammar never leaves the backend, so ProposedAvailabilityRule and the frontend types are unchanged.
5. PREVIEW. Unchanged code path; add the frontend test in acceptance #5 to pin that the concrete date renders and creation fires only on explicit Create.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- Model emits tokens; the resolver computes dates (two-stage, like the engine's other date handling).
- Reference = request receipt time in the user's UserPreferences.timezone (user.py:77), computed in the route, injected into the service as a date.
- Tie-breaks (pin each in tests): bare weekday and "this <weekday>" = first occurrence ON OR AFTER the reference date (today counts); "next <weekday>" = that occurrence + 7 days; month-day without year = first occurrence on or after the reference date (today counts); explicit full date strictly before the reference date = unresolvable with reason "that date has already passed"; a range end resolves relative to its start and must be >= start, else unresolvable. Anything else unresolvable → could_not_parse with the reason, never a guess. The human confirms the resolved date in the preview before any write, which is why a simple, documented tie-break is acceptable.
- Propose-then-confirm unchanged; no new write path; no recurrence in this bead.
- Do NOT touch: engine slot computation; the settings form; ProposedAvailabilityRule / frontend types.

MIGRATION: none (no schema change).

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI: none (input is the clinician's own schedule prose; tests use fixed strings) · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none (no new settings or secrets; reuses ai_model_flash and the existing daily limiter) · auth/RLS: none (existing authenticated route, same user scoping) · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: not a known claim surface — natural language → structured date intent → deterministic resolution is Duckling/Chrono-class prior art, unrelated to the inbox self-learning flywheel, stage-director/briefing composition, ordinal/anchored scoring, companion runtime governance; it resembles scaffold-vs-generate only in that the model defers a computation, but those placeholders are human-fill authority/fact gaps inside generated prose whereas these tokens are machine-resolvable structured params, and v1 (#753) already published the same two-stage shape here · outbound: none.

title: Code a visit — service code, modifiers, units, place of service, ICD-10 diagnoses
description: A clinician has no way to record what service was delivered, or what it was delivered for, in any coded form. Add coded service and diagnosis fields to the visit — enterable at note creation and editable standalone — so an itemised receipt can be assembled from records the practice already holds.
design:
CONTEXT (code-verified against pablo main, 2026-08-17):

- Rates landed 2026-08-15 (ccb1cd6): appointment-type default fees, per-patient
  override, and scheduling_engine/services/rate_resolver.py. Money is integer
  minor units and "unset" is already distinguishable from zero. Read the
  resolved rate; do not re-derive a fee here.
- patient.diagnosis (models/patient.py:25) is a free-text str | None. It is NOT
  a coded diagnosis list and cannot serve one.
- ICD-10 reference data is ALREADY in the repo:
  backend/app/diagnostics/data/icd10cm_2026.tsv. Validate against it rather than
  adding a second copy or calling out to a service.
- No service-code field exists anywhere in the tree, and no visit-code suggester
  exists either — an earlier spec assumed one and was wrong.
- The provider block a receipt needs is already on the user model: npi_number
  (:114), license_number (:107), license_state (:108), business_address (:109).

PROBLEM: a clinician cannot record what service was delivered or what it was
delivered for, in any coded form. That makes an itemised receipt for
out-of-network reimbursement (PABLO-y7u) impossible to assemble, and it is the
single reason that work is stalled.

SCOPE: let a clinician record billing codes on a visit.

WHERE THEY LIVE — on the VISIT (appointment/session), not on the note document.
One visit can carry several notes, and a visit can exist with no note at all, so
the note is the wrong owner. Anything that renders a receipt later must read one
authoritative place.

WHERE THEY ARE ENTERED — two surfaces, one store:
  (a) At note creation. This is the primary surface: the session duration and the
      clinical picture are both on screen, which is the accurate and
      audit-defensible moment to code. Coding a month later from memory is the
      error-prone chore this work exists to remove.
  (b) A standalone edit on the visit, for after-the-fact correction and for
      visits that never get a note.
Both paths write the same record.

FIELDS per visit:
  - service code (CPT), free-entry string
  - up to four modifiers (e.g. 95 telehealth, 93 audio-only)
  - unit count
  - place-of-service code — a closed enum (11 office, 02 telehealth other than
    home, 10 telehealth in home). Payers deny on a missing or wrong value, so it
    is a field, not a rendering-time guess.
  - an ORDERED list of ICD-10 diagnosis codes (order matters — the first is
    primary)

NOTHING INFERS. No code is suggested, defaulted, or derived — from duration, from
note text, or from anything else. Coding is the clinician's professional
judgement and this surface must not influence it. Duration-derived CPT
suggestion is explicitly OUT of this bead; it is a separate change with a
different risk profile.

The free-text patient.diagnosis field stays exactly as it is. This is additive.

FILES: backend/app/models/scheduling.py, backend/app/db/models.py,
backend/app/db/tenant_template.sql, a new alembic revision,
backend/app/routes/scheduling.py, the note-creation route, and the booking +
note-creation frontend surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A visit can carry a service code, up to four modifiers, a unit count, a
   place-of-service code, and an ordered list of ICD-10 diagnosis codes. All of
   them round-trip through the API, and diagnosis order is preserved.
2. Every field is optional. Existing appointments keep working with all of them
   null, and the migration adds no NOT NULL column without a default.
3. An ICD-10 code absent from backend/app/diagnostics/data/icd10cm_2026.tsv is
   rejected with a clear message naming the offending code; a code present in it
   is accepted. Tests cover both.
4. Place of service is a closed enum. An unknown value is rejected, not stored.
5. Codes are settable from the note-creation flow and from a standalone edit on
   the visit, and both write the same record. A test asserts the two paths
   converge on one stored value.
6. Nothing infers or defaults a code. A test asserts that creating a visit, and
   creating a note on a visit, both leave the codes unset rather than populated.
7. "Unset" stays distinguishable from empty everywhere the codes surface — an
   uncoded visit must not render as a blank code.
8. An Alembic revision ships in the same commit as the model change, upgrades
   cleanly from the current head, and tenant_template.sql is regenerated.
9. Lint, format and type checks pass, and the existing test suite stays green.

title: Record what kind of operator a practice serves, defaulting to clinical
description:
Everything downstream assumes a practice is clinical — patients, appointments, notes, charts. A deployment serving a non-clinical operator has none of those, and there is currently no way to declare that, so surfaces would have to infer it from which tables are empty.

Adds an edition column to the practice record defaulting to the clinical case, so the fact is declared rather than guessed. No behaviour branches on it in this change.
design:
Code-verified 2026-08-11.

`PracticeRow` (`backend/app/db/platform_models.py:42`, platform schema) records
what a practice IS, but not what KIND of operator it serves. Everything
downstream currently assumes a clinical practice: patients, appointments,
notes, charts. A deployment serving a non-clinical operator has none of those,
and today there is no way to say so.

Add an `edition` column recording the kind of operator, so surfaces can branch
on a declared fact instead of inferring one from which tables happen to be
empty.

## Values

- `therapist` — a clinical practice. THE DEFAULT, so every existing row and
  every new row is unchanged in behaviour.
- `personal` — a non-clinical operator. No patients, no charts, no clinical
  severity floors.

## String + CHECK, not a native enum

Follow the column style this table already uses (`is_pentest`,
`audio_retention_days` are both plain columns with DB-level CHECK
constraints). A native Postgres enum type requires `ALTER TYPE` to gain a
value; a CHECK constraint is a plain constraint swap. Editions are expected to
grow, so the cheaper-to-change form wins. Python-side it is still a proper
enum/Literal — the looseness is only in the storage type.

`NOT NULL` with `server_default='therapist'` so the migration needs no
backfill pass and no window where the column is null.

## Deliberately NOT in this change

- No behaviour branches on the value yet. This lands the fact; consumers adopt
  it separately. A migration that also rewires six read paths is unreviewable
  and un-revertable.
- No API for changing it. Editions are set at provisioning time; a
  self-service switch is a different question with data-migration
  consequences (a practice with patients cannot simply become non-clinical).
- No new enum for anything else. `product` already exists on this table, only
  ever holds `"pablo"`, and is not the same axis — leave it alone rather than
  overloading it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `practices` gains an `edition` column, NOT NULL, server default
   `'therapist'`, constrained at the DB level to the allowed values.
2. An Alembic revision ships in the same commit and upgrades cleanly from the
   current head. Every pre-existing row reads `therapist` afterwards with no
   backfill step.
3. The constraint rejects an unknown value at the database level. A test
   asserts the insert fails rather than silently storing it.
4. The Python-side type is a proper enum/Literal, not a bare string, and is
   exported for consumers.
5. No existing read path changes behaviour. The full test suite passes
   unchanged, and a test asserts a default-edition practice behaves exactly as
   before.
6. Downgrade drops the column and the constraint cleanly.
7. `product` is untouched.
8. Lint, format, and type checks pass.

title: Superbill: deterministic itemised receipt for out-of-network reimbursement
description:
Patients seeing an out-of-network clinician submit an itemised receipt to their own insurer to get reimbursed. Producing one by hand each month is a recurring, error-prone chore, and an error costs the patient a denied claim.

Generates the document deterministically from records the practice already holds. No claim submission and no clearinghouse — the patient files, not the practice.
design:
Code-verified 2026-08-11 against the repo.

A superbill is an itemised receipt the patient submits to their own insurer for
out-of-network reimbursement. The practice never files anything; the document
is generated, handed to the patient, and that is the end of the workflow. This
is deliberately NOT claim submission — no 837, no clearinghouse, no eligibility
check, no accounts-receivable tracking. Those are a different product.

## Composition

Fixed-format PDF, entirely deterministic. **No language model anywhere in this
path** — every field is copied from a record or computed arithmetically. A
reimbursement document that paraphrases is a document that can be wrong in a
way nobody catches until the patient's claim is denied.

- **Provider block** — name, NPI, license. `npi_number` already exists on the
  user model (`backend/app/models/user.py:114`, validated to 10 digits); read
  it rather than adding a second home for the same fact. A missing NPI must
  block generation with a clear message, not render an empty line: a superbill
  without an NPI is not reimbursable and issuing one wastes the patient's time.
- **Patient block** — name, date of birth, address as recorded.
- **Per-visit lines** — date of service, CPT/service code, ICD-10 diagnosis,
  fee, amount paid. Fee resolves through the rates work rather than being
  entered twice.
- **Totals** — sum of fees and sum of payments, computed from the lines shown.
  The document must never total anything it does not also itemise.

## Codes

Service and diagnosis codes are entered or confirmed by the clinician. Nothing
in this path infers, suggests, or defaults a diagnosis code — coding is the
clinician's professional judgement and a receipt is the wrong surface to
influence it.

## Boundaries

Generation is on demand for a chosen patient and date range. Rendering happens
server-side; the PDF is streamed to the caller and not persisted as a new
document type in this piece of work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Generating a superbill for a patient and date range returns a PDF
   containing the provider block, patient block, one line per visit in range,
   and totals.
2. No language-model call occurs anywhere in the generation path. A test
   asserts this.
3. Generation with a missing provider NPI fails with an explicit error naming
   the missing field, and produces no PDF.
4. Per-visit lines carry date of service, service code, diagnosis code, fee,
   and amount paid. A visit missing a required code is reported, not silently
   omitted from the document.
5. Totals equal the sum of the lines rendered. A test with a date range that
   excludes some visits proves the totals move with the lines.
6. The same inputs produce a byte-identical document across runs, apart from
   any generation timestamp. A test asserts determinism.
7. No diagnosis or service code is inferred, suggested, or defaulted anywhere
   in the path.
8. The fee shown comes from the resolved session rate rather than a second
   independent source.
9. Lint, format, and type checks pass, and the existing test suite stays green.

title: Session rates: appointment-type defaults, per-patient override, sliding-scale note
description:
Clinicians charge different amounts for different appointment types, and reduced-fee arrangements are per-person. Today neither is recorded anywhere, so any statement or receipt has to be assembled by hand.

Adds a practice-level default fee per appointment type, an optional per-patient rate override, and a free-text sliding-scale note, plus one resolver that expresses the precedence between them.
design:
Code-verified 2026-08-11 against the repo.

Two independent places a rate can come from, resolved in a fixed order.

1. **Appointment-type defaults** — a practice-level default fee per appointment
   type, edited in practice settings. This is the common case: most clinicians
   charge one number for a standard session and another for an intake.
2. **Per-patient override** — a rate on the patient record that wins over the
   type default when set. Reduced-fee and sliding-scale arrangements are
   per-person by nature, so this must be a real column and not a note someone
   has to remember to read.
3. **Sliding-scale note** — free text on the patient record recording the
   arrangement in the clinician's own words (e.g. "reduced through June,
   revisit at intake anniversary"). Never parsed, never used in arithmetic;
   it exists so the reason survives staff turnover and the clinician's memory.

Resolution order is patient override -> appointment-type default -> unset.
"Unset" is a legitimate state and must not silently become zero: a statement
line with a blank fee is a visible prompt to fill it in, while a zero is a
wrong number that looks deliberate.

Fees are stored as integer minor units (cents), never floats. Currency is a
single practice-level setting; do not thread a currency per row until there is
a second one to thread.

Schema lives alongside the existing patient and scheduling models
(`backend/app/models/patient.py`, `backend/app/models/scheduling.py`), with an
Alembic revision in `backend/alembic/versions/` in the same style as its
neighbours. Anything that later renders money — statements, receipts — reads
the resolved rate rather than re-deriving the precedence rules itself, so the
order above has exactly one implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A practice can set a default fee per appointment type, and the value
   round-trips through the API.
2. A patient can carry a rate override plus a free-text sliding-scale note;
   both are optional and both round-trip.
3. A single resolver returns the effective rate for (patient, appointment
   type) using patient override -> type default -> unset, and it is the only
   place that precedence is expressed. A test covers all three outcomes.
4. "Unset" is distinguishable from zero everywhere it surfaces. A test asserts
   an unresolved rate does not render as 0.
5. Fees are stored and returned as integer minor units; no float arithmetic
   appears in the rate path.
6. An Alembic revision ships in the same commit as the model change and
   upgrades cleanly from the current head.
7. Existing patients and appointment types keep working with every rate field
   null — the migration adds no NOT NULL column without a default.
8. Lint, format, and type checks pass, and the existing test suite stays green.

title: Make the scheduling engine authoritative: cover the write path, enforce what it evaluates, and give the read path a consumer
description:
The availability engine is well tested and almost unused. It evaluates all
eight rule types correctly with 34 passing tests, but it is wired into two
read-only routes that nothing calls, and the appointment write path never
consults it at all. A booking at 3am on a blocked day returns 201, and two
appointments at the same time both succeed.

This epic gives the engine arteries and teeth: characterize the write path as
it behaves today, then make it refuse what is physically impossible, then make
it honour the rules it already evaluates, and finally give the read path a real
consumer in the scheduling UI.
design:
SEQUENCE MATTERS. Characterization tests land first so the two behavioral
changes flip existing assertions rather than authoring them from scratch -
there is currently NO test anywhere that calls POST /api/appointments.

  1. Characterize the write path (start node).
  2. Refuse double-booking - collisions are physics.
  3. Enforce availability rules - HARD refuses, SOFT warns. Rules are policy.
  4. Distinguish "not configured" from "no openings" so callers can tell them
     apart, and keep the write path permissive when nothing is configured.
  5. Give the read path a consumer: a "find a time" affordance in the
     appointment flow, the first caller of the free-slots route.

PERMISSIVE WHEN UNCONFIGURED is load-bearing throughout: most practices have
no rules today, and enforcement must not break their booking.

KEY PATHS:
  backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py  (engine)
  backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:42 (write path)
  backend/app/routes/scheduling.py:193                    (create route)
  backend/tests/test_availability_engine.py               (34 tests to mirror)
