title: Adjustment and status code tables as data: CARC, RARC, group codes, 835 claim status, with categorization
description: Remittances and denials speak in codes: CARC claim adjustment reason codes, RARC remark codes, claim adjustment group codes (CO, PR, OA, PI), and 835 claim status codes. The remittance posting, the claim detail UI and any later denial handling all need the human descriptions and a coarse category per code. Ship them as data in the repo, with a lookup API, so nothing has to call out to learn what CO-45 means.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.
- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

- backend/app/claims/codes/ package with three data modules generated from public code lists: carc.py (adjustment reason codes: code, description), rarc.py (remark codes: code, description), groups.py (CO/PR/OA/PI/CR with descriptions), claim_status.py (835 CLP02 claim status codes 1,2,3,4,19,20,21,22,23,25). Source the lists from the X12 external code lists published at x12.org/codes (CARC/RARC are public reference data; cite the list version and retrieval date in each module docstring). Store as tuples/dicts, not JSON files, so mypy types them.
- lookup API: describe_carc(code) -> str | None, describe_rarc(code) -> str | None, describe_group(code) -> str, describe_claim_status(code) -> str, and categorize(group, carc) -> Literal['paid','patient_responsibility','contractual','enrollment','coding','timely_filing','eligibility','needs_records','duplicate','other'] as a small hand-written table over the most common behavioral-health codes (e.g. PR-1/2/3 deductible/coinsurance/copay -> patient_responsibility; CO-45 -> contractual; CO-16/CO-4 -> coding; CO-29 -> timely_filing; CO-27/CO-26/CO-31 -> eligibility; CO-197/CO-198 -> needs_records (authorization); CO-18 -> duplicate; CO-B7/CO-8 -> enrollment). Unknown -> 'other'.
- Tests: every category has at least one code test; describe_* return None/str correctly for known/unknown; a size test asserting the CARC table has at least 300 entries and RARC at least 900 so a truncated regeneration fails loudly.

DECISIONS CLOSED: data lives in code, not the database; no model calls; categories are the fixed set above.
DO NOT TOUCH: anything outside backend/app/claims/codes/ and its tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. describe_carc('45') and describe_rarc('N30') return the published descriptions; describe_carc('nonsense') returns None.
2. categorize covers every category in the design with a test each; unknown pairs return 'other'.
3. Table size tests pass (CARC >= 300, RARC >= 900).
4. Each data module cites its source list and retrieval date.
5. make check green.

description: Before a payer accepts claims or returns remittances electronically, the billing provider must be enrolled with that payer through the clearinghouse (one request per provider per payer per transaction type; remittance always requires it). This bead creates the provider record from the billing profile, files enrollment requests for payers in use, mirrors status, and turns "provider action required" into a compliance reminder with the payer's instructions.

SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.

title: Charge ledger is silent about disputes and knows nothing about fees
description: Two facts Stripe already knows are missing from the charge ledger. Disputes are not subscribed to at all, so a chargeback leaves the ledger reporting a payment as succeeded when it is not. And the ledger records what was charged but not the fee or net, so a clinician reconciling against their bank finds a gap on every transaction. Both live in the same receiver and the same row, so they ship together.
design:
The charge ledger is missing two facts Stripe already knows, and both make it
misreport reality.

1. DISPUTES ARE INVISIBLE. The payment webhook subscribes to
   payment_intent.succeeded, payment_intent.payment_failed and
   charge.refunded - not dispute events. When a client charges back, Stripe
   emails the practice, this app stays silent, and the ledger keeps reporting
   the payment as succeeded, which is now false. Disputes carry evidence
   deadlines, so the silence has a cost.

2. FEES ARE UNKNOWN. The ledger stores the amount charged and nothing about
   what the practice actually received. A clinician reconciling against their
   bank finds a gap on every transaction: charged 150.00, received 145.35.
   Stripe exposes this as the charge's balance transaction, which carries
   amount, fee and net.

Both are handled in the same receiver and the same ledger row, so they ship
together rather than colliding.

SCOPE:

- Handle `charge.dispute.created` and `charge.dispute.closed`, reflecting the
  outcome on the charge row. A dispute is NOT a refund: a disputed charge later
  won is still a successful payment; one lost is money gone. Model that
  distinction rather than flattening it into the refunded status.
- Capture fee and net onto the charge row from the balance transaction.
  Prefer taking it at webhook time over fetching in the charge path: for some
  payment methods the balance transaction settles slightly AFTER the charge, so
  a fee read at charge-creation time can legitimately be null.
- Ship the model change with its migration, per the repo's usual rule.

Follow the receiver's existing shape exactly - it is correct and hard won:
verify the signature over the raw body BEFORE parsing; record the event for
deduplication only once it is genuinely handled; return 5xx so Stripe retries
when a row that should have matched did not; keep the attribution check on the
update.

DECISIONS CLOSED:
- No dispute evidence handling, upload, or deadline tracking. That belongs in
  Stripe's dashboard, which stays authoritative. This makes the ledger honest,
  nothing more.
- No new notification channel and no UI in this task. Surfacing a disputed or
  fee-adjusted charge is separate work.
- Storing the fee does not remove the "Stripe is authoritative" framing
  elsewhere: payouts batch, disputes reverse later, and a practice may have
  income this app never sees.
- The endpoint's subscribed event list is dashboard configuration, not code.
  Say so in the PR body: the dispute events will not arrive until it is
  updated.

DO NOT TOUCH: the charge-creation path beyond what the fee column requires, the
credential provider, or any settings UI.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `charge.dispute.created` moves the matching ledger row into a state that
   records the charge is disputed, without reusing the refunded status.
2. `charge.dispute.closed` records the outcome, distinguishing won (payment
   stands) from lost (funds gone).
3. The charge row carries the fee and net amounts once the balance transaction
   is available, and tolerates it being absent at charge-creation time rather
   than failing or storing a wrong zero.
4. An event whose charge matches no ledger row is treated exactly as the
   existing receiver treats that case, and is NOT silently recorded as handled.
5. Signature verification still runs on the raw body before any parsing; a bad
   signature is rejected with 401.
6. A duplicate delivery of the same event id is a no-op.
7. The model change ships with its migration in the same commit.
8. Tests cover: dispute created; dispute closed won; dispute closed lost; fee
   captured; fee not yet available; unknown charge; bad signature; duplicate
   delivery.
9. The PR body states that the endpoint's subscribed events must be updated in
   the Stripe dashboard for dispute events to be delivered.
10. `make check` passes, with actual output reported.

title: Billing becomes a top-level page showing the unbilled-sessions queue
description: Clicking Billing in the left nav lands on a Settings configuration page, when the clinician came to do work. Make Billing a top-level surface whose content is the queue of completed sessions that have not been charged - a list the app can build accurately because it knows the session happened, and the way back for anyone who skipped charging when signing the note.
design:
Billing is currently a section inside Settings, so clicking "Billing" in the
left nav lands the clinician on a configuration page when what they came to do
is work. Calendar is not in Settings for the same reason. Make Billing a
top-level working surface whose content is the unbilled queue.

WHY THE QUEUE IS THE RIGHT CONTENT: the app knows a session actually happened -
there is a finalized note, an appointment, and often a service code. "Sessions
completed but not charged" is therefore a list it can build accurately. It also
rescues the charge-at-signing flow: a clinician who skips charging when signing
a note - busy, no card on file, client said they would pay later - currently
has no way back to it. The queue is that way back.

SCOPE:

1. A top-level Billing route and nav entry, alongside Calendar rather than
   inside Settings.
2. The unbilled queue: finalized sessions with no succeeded charge, newest
   first, showing client, date and resolved amount. Each row links to the
   session, where the existing charge action already lives.
3. A backend endpoint for that query. Derive "unbilled" from the charge ledger
   and the note's finalized state; do not add a denormalised flag column.
4. An extension slot rendered ABOVE the queue, for deployment-specific setup
   content. Follow the slot pattern in DashboardHomeSlot - return null here.

MIRROR THIS PATTERN: frontend/src/components/calendar/connect/
CalendarSetupWizard.tsx and CalendarConnectStep.tsx are the closest sibling for
an inline first-run setup prompt on a working page. Match their structure and
density.

DECISIONS CLOSED - do not re-litigate:

- Settings keeps the configuration surface. This work does not delete or move
  it; it stops it being the destination of the nav item.
- Amounts shown are what was CHARGED. Stripe is the authoritative source for
  money, and the page must say so plainly near any figure: fees and payouts are
  not shown, so these numbers will legitimately differ from a bank statement.
  Explain the difference rather than merely disclaiming it.
- Do NOT add revenue totals, date-range summaries, or any export that could be
  mistaken for an accounting record. This app is not accounting software, and
  that line is easy to cross one helpful figure at a time. (Goal-oriented
  summaries, if they ever exist, belong on a different surface with their own
  framing - not here.)
- No payout, fee, tax or dispute data on this page. Those live in Stripe.

DO NOT TOUCH: the charge API, the payment webhook, or the existing settings
pages. Filling the extension slot is follow-up work, not this task.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A top-level Billing nav entry exists alongside Calendar; clicking it opens
   the Billing page, not a Settings page.
2. The page lists sessions with a finalized note and no succeeded charge,
   newest first, each showing client, session date and resolved amount, and
   each linking to that session.
3. A successfully charged session does not appear. A session whose charge
   FAILED does appear, so it can be retried.
4. The list comes from a backend endpoint that derives the state at query time;
   the diff adds no denormalised billed/unbilled column.
5. Near the amounts, the page states that figures are what was charged and that
   Stripe is the source of truth for fees, payouts and net.
6. An extension slot renders above the queue and returns null by default.
7. No revenue total, date-range summary, or export control anywhere on the page.
8. Tests cover: empty queue, populated queue, a failed-charge entry, and the
   slot rendering nothing by default.
9. `make check` passes, with actual output reported.

title: audit_logs append-only trigger silently no-ops UPDATE under the purge GUC
description:
`audit_logs_append_only()` (migration b33a493310b6, baked into tenant_template.sql) ends its authorized-purge branch with:

    IF current_setting('app.allow_audit_purge', true) = 'on' THEN
        RETURN COALESCE(OLD, NEW);
    END IF;

In a BEFORE row trigger the returned row is what gets written. For DELETE, NEW is NULL so COALESCE yields OLD and the delete proceeds — correct. For UPDATE, OLD is not null, so it returns OLD and the UPDATE writes the old values back.

The result: with the purge GUC armed, an UPDATE reports success, reports rowcount 1, and changes nothing.

Confirmed empirically against a provisioned tenant schema under the NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role:

    UPDATE under purge GUC -> raised: no, rowcount: 1
    stored action afterwards: 'read'  (silent no-op: True)

The append-only property survives, which is why this has never surfaced. The problem is that it lies about it: an operator running a corrective UPDATE with the purge GUC armed gets a clean success and no change, with nothing in the result distinguishing that from a real write.
design:
Decide what an armed UPDATE should mean before writing code — the current behaviour is a third thing (silently discarded) that nobody chose.

Option A — RETURN NEW for UPDATE, OLD for DELETE. Makes the purge GUC a genuine write escape hatch. Widest, and arguably wrong: the GUC exists for the retention purge, which never updates.
Option B — keep refusing UPDATE regardless of the GUC; only DELETE and TRUNCATE are exempt. Narrowest and probably right: it matches what the GUC is actually for, and turns today's silent no-op into the loud error the unarmed path already gives.
Option C — leave the behaviour, document it. Rejected: a compliance table that reports a successful write it discarded is the wrong failure mode to keep on purpose.

Leaning B. Note TG_OP is already available in the function, so the branch is a two-line change.
acceptance_criteria:
- An UPDATE on audit_logs with app.allow_audit_purge armed either applies, or fails loudly. It does not report success while discarding the write.
- DELETE under the purge GUC still works (the retention cron depends on it).
- UPDATE without the purge GUC still raises 'audit_logs is append-only', as test_audit_logs_append_only asserts today.
- An integration test covers the armed-UPDATE case. The existing suite only asserts that UNARMED updates raise, which is why this was invisible.
notes: Found while adversarially reviewing #837 (see #840, #841). Predates that PR — migration b33a493310b6. Not urgent: no code path issues an UPDATE against audit_logs, and the row stays immutable either way. Filed so the deferred decision is tracked rather than rediscovered.

title: A failed recording start leaves the session in_progress with no way back
description: When the desktop app's audio capture fails to start, the backend session it just flipped to in_progress stays there with no audio and nothing rolls it back. Found while tracing a real Start Session in pablo-companion#118 and left for a status decision. The client flips status BEFORE capture starts (ContentView.swift:356-380 in the Mac app: `startSession` → PATCH status=in_progress, then `startRecording`); when capture throws (RecordingService.swift:136-160, e.g. the macOS 26 system-audio permission case) the error alert says "then start the session again" — but the retry hits 409 ALREADY_IN_STATUS because the session is already in_progress, and the state machine offers no way back: VALID_TRANSITIONS[in_progress] is {recording_complete, cancelled}. The therapist's only exits are cancel (terminal, hides the session from Today) or a phantom "recording complete" with no audio. This is the backend half: a revert edge the client can call. The client half (calling it on capture failure) lands in the desktop-app repo separately.
design:
Backend half only. One production file, two test files.

CHANGE — backend/app/services/session_service.py:
1. VALID_TRANSITIONS (session_service.py:144-156): add SessionStatus.SCHEDULED to the in_progress row → `{RECORDING_COMPLETE, CANCELLED, SCHEDULED}`. This is the "recording never started, put the session back" edge.
2. Side effects in `transition_status` (session_service.py:694-710): when target == SCHEDULED, clear `session.started_at` and `session.ended_at` (the session has not happened; started_at was set by the in_progress flip at :697). Extend the `_update_next_session_date` trigger set at :708 to include SCHEDULED, so the patient's next-session pointer is recomputed exactly as it is for the in_progress flip.
3. No route change: PATCH /api/sessions/{id}/status (backend/app/routes/sessions.py:797-832) already accepts any SessionStatus value, maps InvalidStatusTransitionError → 400 and SessionAlreadyInStatusError → 409, and audits `changes={"status": ...}`. The enum is backend/app/models/enums.py:8-22.

WHY SCHEDULED, not cancelled or failed (decision closed here, with reasons): cancelled is terminal (TERMINAL_STATUSES, session_service.py:158) — it hides the session from Today and blocks the retry the error message asks for; failed is not reachable from in_progress, implies a recording existed, and carries an error string the therapist has to dismiss. Reverting to scheduled restores the exact pre-Start state, so the therapist's next Start goes scheduled → in_progress normally. A session in in_progress cannot have audio yet (upload-audio requires recording_complete/transcribing/failed, sessions.py:1195-1205), so nothing is lost by reverting.

TESTS (mirror the existing shapes, do not restructure):
- backend/tests/test_scheduling_service.py, class TestTransitionStatus (starts :180; uses the `service`, `session_repo`, `user_id`, `patient` fixtures and `_make_session(session_repo, user_id, patient.id, <status>)`):
  test_in_progress_reverts_to_scheduled — seed IN_PROGRESS with started_at set (flip it via a scheduled→in_progress transition first so started_at is real), transition to SCHEDULED → status == SCHEDULED, started_at is None, ended_at is None.
  test_revert_recomputes_next_session_date — after the revert, the patient row's next_session_date reflects the session's scheduled_at again (compare with what the existing cancel test asserts for the pointer).
  test_scheduled_to_scheduled_still_409 — SessionAlreadyInStatusError unchanged.
  test_revert_not_allowed_from_recording_complete — RECORDING_COMPLETE → SCHEDULED still raises InvalidStatusTransitionError (the edge is from in_progress only; audio may exist past that point).
- backend/tests/test_routes_sessions.py: one route test, test_patch_status_scheduled_reverts_an_in_progress_session — seed via `_seed_session(..., status=SessionStatus.IN_PROGRESS)` (:38-60), PATCH {"status": "scheduled"} → 200, body["status"] == "scheduled", body["started_at"] is None; and the audit spy sees `changes={"status": "scheduled"}`.

OUT OF SCOPE (say so in the PR): the client change — on capture-start failure the desktop app should PATCH status=scheduled (the app repo has its own CI and lands separately; this edge is what it will call); a periodic sweep for sessions left in_progress by a crashed client (needs a scheduling decision; not part of this change); any change to the cancel or recording_complete edges; the appointment link (start-session from an appointment creates the session; the revert leaves the link intact).

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: the revert target is scheduled; the edge exists only from in_progress; started_at/ended_at are cleared; no new endpoint, no new request field, no audit action enum change (the route's existing audit call is the record); no migration (status is a string column).

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI: none (in-memory fixtures, synthetic ids, no transcripts) · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none · auth/RLS: none (same ownership lookup `session_repo.get(session_id, user_id)`) · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: OSS-landing so walked in full — a state-machine edge is not a claimed construct · outbound: none.
acceptance_criteria:
1. FAILING-FIRST: `test_in_progress_reverts_to_scheduled` in backend/tests/test_scheduling_service.py raises InvalidStatusTransitionError on main and passes after the change.
2. After the revert, started_at and ended_at are None and the patient's next_session_date is recomputed (asserted in the two service tests).
3. RECORDING_COMPLETE → SCHEDULED still raises InvalidStatusTransitionError; SCHEDULED → SCHEDULED still raises SessionAlreadyInStatusError.
4. The route test in backend/tests/test_routes_sessions.py returns 200 with status "scheduled" and started_at null for an in_progress session, and audits changes={"status": "scheduled"}.
5. Diff touches backend/app/services/session_service.py and the two test files only; no migration.
6. `make check` green (ruff + mypy + full pytest).
7. PR text reads as ordinary OSS work and states that the desktop-app half (calling the revert on capture failure) is separate; no tracker ids.

title: Let a deployment enable speaker labels on the second audio channel, and keep the labels in the transcript
description:
Dual-channel transcription treats each channel as one voice: backend/app/services/assemblyai_transcription_service.py:355-358 names the channels "Therapist" and "Client", :319-333 submits each job with only audio_url / language_code / speech_model, and parse_result (:405-449) stamps every word with the channel's single speaker name. That is right for a 1:1 session. It is wrong whenever the second channel carries several people — a group call recorded through the desktop app, a family session on speakerphone — where everyone on that channel collapses into "Client", and any note that attributes statements to people is guessing.

AssemblyAI can diarize a job (speaker_labels: true; each word then carries a speaker letter). Make that a per-deployment, per-channel option, default off, and carry the label through to the transcript text so downstream readers see "Client A" / "Client B" instead of one merged voice.
design:
SCOPE: one settings field, one submit-body parameter, one parse-side change, tests. FILES: backend/app/settings.py, backend/app/services/assemblyai_transcription_service.py, backend/app/routes/internal_transcription.py (only if the service needs anything beyond `settings` — today it is constructed from settings at :461, so probably no change), backend/tests/test_assemblyai_transcription_service.py, plus one transcript round-trip test.

VERIFIED POINTERS (main 84f9fb0, 2026-08-26):
- settings.py:1116-1127 assemblyai_api_key / assemblyai_speech_model / assemblyai_vad_enabled — add the new field beside them, following whatever list-from-env convention the other list-valued settings in settings.py already use (check before inventing one).
- _submit_transcription (:319-333) builds the JSON body {"audio_url","language_code","speech_model"}; submit_dual_channel (:335-380) iterates [("Therapist", therapist_audio, 1), ("Client", client_audio, 2)] and records {"transcript_id","speaker","offset_map"} per job (:377).
- parse_result (:405-449) maps each word to {"start","end","speaker": job_meta["speaker"],"text"} then _words_to_utterances(words, speaker) (:472+), which groups by time gap only. _merge_segments (:500-514) renders "[hh:mm:ss]\n<speaker>: <text>".
- backend/app/models/transcript.py:72-73 parse_transcript_segments matches "([^:]+):" for the speaker, so a two-word speaker like "Client A" already round-trips.
- Submit happens in internal_transcription.py:462 with no knowledge of the session's note type (the note type is chosen later, in the generate-soap job enqueued at :316). That is why this is a deployment setting and not a per-note-type switch; per-note-type routing would need the session's note type at submit time and is a separate change.
- Test harness: backend/tests/test_assemblyai_transcription_service.py — _settings(**overrides) :47, _install_mock_transport :76, _channel_handler(calls) :251 (captures every httpx request), _SILENCE_PCM :248, TestSubmitDualChannel :311 (the :370-385 case pins today's exact body), TestParseResult :543.

MECHANISM:
1. settings.py: `assemblyai_speaker_labels_channels: list[str]` default empty — "channels ('Therapist' / 'Client') submitted with speaker_labels so several people on one channel are told apart; empty keeps today's behaviour".
2. Service: __init__ keeps the set; _submit_transcription(client, audio_url, *, speaker_labels: bool) adds "speaker_labels": True to the body ONLY when set — with the default the body is byte-for-byte today's. Job meta gains "diarized": bool.
3. parse_result: when job_meta.get("diarized") is true and a word carries "speaker", the word's speaker becomes f"{channel} {word['speaker']}" ("Client A"); words without a speaker key keep the channel name; on a non-diarized job the word's speaker field is ignored. _words_to_utterances also breaks an utterance when the speaker changes (pure-function change; keep the gap rule).
4. Nothing else: timestamps, offset maps, VAD, the whole-file AAC path, and the merged transcript format are untouched.

PRE-ANSWERED: default off; the therapist channel is never diarized unless configured; labels are "<Channel> <Letter>", never names — nothing here infers who a speaker is; no prompt changes — the transcript simply carries more speakers and the existing parser accepts them.

OUT OF SCOPE: per-note-type or per-session selection; the Whisper provider; any note-generation prompt.

1. FAILING-FIRST in backend/tests/test_assemblyai_transcription_service.py: TestSubmitDualChannel gains test_speaker_labels_sent_only_for_configured_channels (_settings(assemblyai_speaker_labels_channels=["Client"]) → the second /transcript body has "speaker_labels": true and the first has no speaker_labels key; returned job meta has diarized False/True in that order) and test_default_submit_body_has_no_speaker_labels (default settings → neither body carries the key; the existing :370-385 assertions still hold). TestParseResult gains test_diarized_words_keep_channel_and_letter (words with speaker "A"/"B" on a diarized "Client" job → utterances "Client A" and "Client B", split at the speaker change, timestamps mapped through offset_map) and test_undiarized_job_ignores_word_speaker_field (same words on a non-diarized job → every utterance says "Client").
2. One round-trip test (beside the existing transcript parser tests): a merge containing "Client A: …" parses back through parse_transcript_segments with speaker "Client A".
3. Settings round-trip: the field defaults to [] and parses "Client" from the environment the same way the other list-valued settings do (one test beside the existing settings tests, or in the service test via _settings()).
4. `make check` green (ruff + mypy + pytest — mypy included).
5. git diff touches only the files listed in FILES plus the two test files.

title: Extension slots may require app providers: document the contract and give component tests a renderWithProviders helper
description:
frontend/src/lib/companion.extensions.ts:19-21 declares useCompanionAccess as a plain function and its docstring (:13-16) calls it UI-only, but nothing states whether a replacement implementation may be a real hook that needs the app's providers (React Query, config, auth). Component tests currently render most components bare — frontend/src/components/sessions/__tests__/NoteViewer.test.tsx calls render() at :113/:702/:873 with no QueryClientProvider, for example — which is only valid while every slot implementation stays provider-free. A downstream build whose implementation consults server state hits "No QueryClient set, use QueryClientProvider to set one" across 15 component test files (165 cases) the moment its files are laid over the tree.

Two fixes, both here: say what the contract is, and give tests one helper that renders inside the real provider stack so a slot that needs data has a supported path. No runtime behaviour changes.
design:
FILES: frontend/src/lib/companion.extensions.ts (docstring only); (new) frontend/src/test/renderWithProviders.tsx; (new) frontend/src/test/__tests__/renderWithProviders.test.tsx; frontend/src/components/dashboard/__tests__/TodayPanel.test.tsx (swap its hand-rolled wrapper for the helper). Rewiring the other 14 bare-render files is optional — do it only where render→renderWithProviders is a one-line mechanical swap, and list the ones done in the PR body.

VERIFIED POINTERS (main 84f9fb0, 2026-08-26):
- providers.tsx:16-28 Providers = ToastProvider > QueryProviders; QueryProviders :52-80 = QueryClientProvider(createAppQueryClient(showToast), :35-50) > outerProviderWrappers (providers.extensions) > OidcSessionProviderWrapper > ConfigProvider > AuthProvider > ThemeProvider.
- ConfigProvider (config-provider.tsx:41-58) fetches /api/config with useQuery and calls setApiUrl synchronously; useConfig (:92-98) throws outside the provider. useAuth (auth-context.tsx:48-50) returns a safe default outside AuthProvider — that is the posture slots should be allowed to assume for auth but NOT for React Query.
- TodayPanel.test.tsx:5 imports QueryClient/QueryClientProvider and :74-80 wraps by hand — the pattern the helper replaces.
- vitest: happy-dom, setupFiles ./vitest.setup.ts, alias "@" → src (frontend/vitest.config.ts). Existing shared fixtures live in frontend/src/test/factories.ts — put the helper beside it.

MECHANISM:
1. renderWithProviders(ui, options?) — wraps ui in QueryClientProvider (fresh QueryClient, retry: false, gcTime: 0) and ToastProvider, returns the RTL render result plus the queryClient. Config: give the helper an option `config?: RuntimeConfig` and, when set, satisfy useConfig without a network call — prefer mocking fetch for "/api/config" inside the helper over changing config-provider.tsx; only add a test-only prop to ConfigProvider if it stays under ten lines and defaults off. AuthProvider is NOT included (useAuth already defaults safely); document that.
2. companion.extensions.ts docstring: "An implementation MAY be a hook and MAY require the app's providers (React Query, runtime config). The default build's implementations require nothing. Tests that render a consumer of a slot should use test/renderWithProviders so a data-backed implementation stays renderable." useCompanionAccess itself is untouched.
3. TodayPanel.test.tsx: replace :74-80 with renderWithProviders; assertions unchanged.

PRE-ANSWERED: default implementations stay provider-free (the cheapest slot needs nothing); this change is documentation + test infrastructure and must not add providers to production component code; the 15-file rewiring is not required for done.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what any slot returns; a download-URL slot for the companion dialog (its own change).

title: Companion download URL becomes a configurable extension slot in companion.extensions.ts, consumed by CompanionGetDialog
description:
The dashboard's "Get Pablo for Mac" dialog (frontend/src/components/dashboard/CompanionGetDialog.tsx:51-60) hardcodes the macOS button's href to https://pablo.health — the project homepage, which never starts a download. A deployment that hosts its own build of the desktop app has no supported way to point that button at its artifact: the only option today is replacing the whole file, and a whole-file replacement silently drifts on every change to the dialog's markup or copy.

The companion surface already has an extension slot for exactly this kind of per-deployment decision (frontend/src/lib/companion.extensions.ts, useCompanionAccess). The download URL belongs in the same file: one function a downstream build replaces, consumed by the dialog, with the default build's behaviour unchanged.
design:
SCOPE: one new slot function + one consumer change + tests. FILES: frontend/src/lib/companion.extensions.ts, frontend/src/components/dashboard/CompanionGetDialog.tsx, (new) frontend/src/components/dashboard/__tests__/CompanionGetDialog.test.tsx. Nothing else. VERIFIED POINTERS (main 84f9fb0, 2026-08-26): - CompanionGetDialog.tsx:14 imports isMacOS from @/lib/companion; :25 `const mac = isMacOS()`; :51-60 renders ``; :61-66 the non-mac "isn't supported yet" copy; :67-69 the Close button. - companion.extensions.ts:19-21 `export function useCompanionAccess(): boolean { return true }`, docstring :5-16. That docstring says "same pattern as client.extensions.ts" — the file is frontend/src/lib/api/client.extensions.ts; correct the reference while there. - TodayPanel.tsx:15 imports the dialog and :98 renders it — the only consumer. Its test frontend/src/components/dashboard/__tests__/TodayPanel.test.tsx (12 cases) mocks @/lib/companion at :27-30 with the vi.hoisted pattern (:9-10) and must keep passing unchanged. - No test exists for CompanionGetDialog today (frontend/src/components/dashboard/__tests__/ has none). vitest: happy-dom, setupFiles ./vitest.setup.ts, alias "@" → src (frontend/vitest.config.ts). MECHANISM: 1. companion.extensions.ts — add export function useCompanionDownloadUrl(): string | null { return "https://pablo.health" } Named as a hook so a downstream implementation MAY read React context or state; the default needs nothing. Doc comment on the slot: "null means this deployment has no artifact to offer — the dialog renders the button disabled with a short explanation instead of a dead link." Extend the file docstring to name both slots. 2. CompanionGetDialog.tsx — `const downloadUrl = useCompanionDownloadUrl()` beside `isMacOS()`. mac && downloadUrl → today's anchor with href={downloadUrl} (keep target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"). mac && downloadUrl === null → `` plus `

Download unavailable — install later from Settings.

`. Non-mac branch and Close button unchanged. 3. Tests mock the slot with `vi.mock("@/lib/companion.extensions", () => ({ useCompanionDownloadUrl: () => slot(), useCompanionAccess: () => true }))` using vi.hoisted, and mock @/lib/companion the way TodayPanel.test.tsx:27-30 does. PRE-ANSWERED: the default stays the homepage, so the default build behaves byte-for-byte as today. No env-var plumbing and no Settings-page entry — the slot IS the configuration surface. Do not touch frontend/src/lib/companion.ts, TodayPanel.tsx, or any provider. OUT OF SCOPE: stating whether slot implementations may require the app's providers (its own change); a Windows CTA.

title: Note-generation eval: --samples N with a worst-case gate and a CI-tested aggregator
description:
backend/evals/run_note_generation.py runs the real note pipeline against the note_generation.yaml corpus and gates on the faithfulness judge's hallucination findings (hard) with omissions advisory. A single run is noisy: generation runs at temperature 0.2 and the judge is itself non-deterministic, and one full-length case (the alcohol-ambivalence intake) intermittently inflates the drinking severity — a real faithfulness miss that a single sample catches only sometimes. The gate therefore cannot distinguish "flaky" from "regressed".

Add repeat sampling with a worst-case gate: `--samples N` generates and judges N samples per case, and a case passes only if EVERY sample is free of hard failures. The aggregation is a pure function with unit tests that run in CI; the end-to-end multi-sample run stays a documented, deliberately-run step because it costs real model spend.
design:
VERIFIED POINTERS (origin/main 84f9fb0, 2026-08-26):
- Runner: backend/evals/run_note_generation.py — _hard_failures(verdict) :130, _advisory_omissions :154, _score_case(case, model, judge_model) :163-219 (generates once, judges once, returns the per-case dict with passed/hard_failures/advisory_omissions/judge_notes), main() :221 (argparse :222-234: --case, --tier, --dataset, --model, --judge-model, --output), results loop :250, report dict :253-261 (generated_at, gen_model, judge_model, n_cases, n_passed, all_passed, cases), exit 0 iff all_passed :278.
- Judge: backend/evals/scorers/llm_judge_faithfulness.py JudgeVerdict :151-166 (passes, hallucinated_facts, missing_facts, judge_notes, raw_response; to_dict).
- Baseline: backend/evals/baselines/note_generation_baseline.json — written by --output; must still load and compare.
- Test collection: CI runs `cd backend && pytest tests/` (Makefile:58, .github/workflows/ci.yml:149; pyproject testpaths = ["tests"]). backend/evals/test_*.py are NOT collected by CI and backend/evals/harness.py imports braintrust (optional dependency group `evals`, not installed in CI). backend/evals/__init__.py is a docstring only, so a braintrust-free module under backend/evals/ IS importable from backend/tests/ (tests already import backend.app.* — e.g. backend/tests/test_structured_llm_gateway.py:18).

PLAN:
1. backend/evals/sampling.py (NEW), stdlib-only imports (no harness, no scorer import at module level): 
   - a small dataclass SampleResult(hard_failures: list[str], advisory_omissions: list[str], judge_passes: bool, gen_seconds: float, generated_chars: int, hallucinated_facts, missing_facts, judge_notes) or a plain dict contract — pick the dataclass;
   - aggregate_sample_verdicts(samples: list[SampleResult]) -> CaseAggregate with: passed = all samples have zero hard failures (worst-case), n_samples, n_failed_samples, union of hard failures (deduped, order-preserving), per-sample list for the report. Raises ValueError on an empty list.
2. Runner: add --samples N (int, default 1, must be >= 1). _score_case runs generate+judge N times, builds SampleResult per run, aggregates via aggregate_sample_verdicts. The per-case dict keeps every existing key with N=1 semantics (passed, hard_failures, advisory_omissions, judge_notes, gen_seconds, generated_chars, hallucinated_facts, missing_facts, judge_passes) and ADDS "samples": [per-sample dicts] and "n_samples". Top-level report gains "samples_per_case". Console output prints one status line per sample plus the case verdict.
3. Baseline compatibility: reading/comparing backend/evals/baselines/note_generation_baseline.json (written before this change, no "samples" key) must not error — treat a missing "samples" as a single-sample record.
4. Docs: runner module docstring + README section "Repeat sampling": how to run `--samples 3 --tier 2`, that it multiplies model spend by N, and that it is a deliberate local/manual step — the CI gate is the aggregation unit test, never the live run.
5. Tests: backend/tests/test_eval_sampling.py (NEW), importing backend.evals.sampling only — all samples pass => case passes; one failing sample among N => case fails with that sample's hard failures surfaced; N=1 parity (one sample in => identical verdict fields out); empty list raises; hard-failure union is deduped and ordered. Network-free, no model calls, no braintrust.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- Worst-case gate (any failing sample fails the case), NOT majority vote.
- Exit code stays 0 iff every case passes; default invocation (no flag) behaves exactly as today.
- --samples applies to tier-1 and tier-2 alike.
- Generation temperature stays at the pipeline default; do not add a temperature flag here.
- No change to the judge rubric, prompts, dataset, or the note pipeline.
- The live multi-sample run is NOT wired into CI (real spend); refreshing the baseline with a multi-sample run is a separate, manual act.

OUT OF SCOPE: any eval-in-CI wiring; baseline refresh; judge or prompt changes; comparing two configurations (diffing is separate work).

FILES: backend/evals/sampling.py (NEW), backend/evals/run_note_generation.py, backend/evals/README.md, backend/tests/test_eval_sampling.py (NEW). scorers/llm_judge_faithfulness.py only if a verdict serialisation helper is genuinely needed.

Commit and PR text are read by the public: plain, human-toned, no tracker ids, no internal paths.
acceptance_criteria:
1. backend/tests/test_eval_sampling.py (NEW) imports only backend.evals.sampling (no harness/judge/braintrust import), runs under `cd backend && pytest tests/`, and covers: all-pass => pass; one failing sample of N => fail with that sample's hard failures in the aggregate; N=1 parity; empty input raises; hard-failure union deduped and order-preserving. Green in `make check`.
2. run_note_generation.py accepts --samples N (default 1; N < 1 rejected); with N > 1 each case is generated and judged N times and passes only if every sample has zero hard failures.
3. Default invocation (no flag) is behaviourally identical to today: one sample, same per-case keys, exit 0 iff all cases pass.
4. The JSON report carries per-sample verdicts under each case ("samples", "n_samples") and "samples_per_case" at top level; loading/comparing the existing backend/evals/baselines/note_generation_baseline.json (no "samples" key) does not error.
5. --samples is documented in --help and in backend/evals/README.md as a deliberate, spend-multiplying manual step; nothing new runs in CI beyond the unit test.
6. `make check` green (ruff, ruff format, mypy, pytest). Single PR.

title: Accept session audio in segments during recording and transcribe each as it arrives
description: A recorded session is uploaded as two whole-channel files at the end, so a 45-minute session becomes one large upload followed by one large transcription job before note generation can begin. Letting a client send the recording in segments as the session progresses — each transcribed on arrival, all merged on the original timeline — moves most of the transcription work into the session itself, so the note starts almost immediately after the last segment lands. This is the server half: an additive contract on the existing multipart upload route. Clients keep working unchanged until they opt in.
design:
Server side only; omitted fields = today's behaviour byte-for-byte. Whisper provider is out of scope (segment fields with provider=whisper → 400, code SEGMENTS_UNSUPPORTED).

WHY the current path cannot take segments (each is a change below): (a) backend/app/routes/sessions.py:1195-1205 rejects any session not in recording_complete/transcribing/failed, so a mid-session upload (in_progress) is refused; (b) `_audio_multipart_object_name` (sessions.py:1008) names one object per channel, so a second upload overwrites the first; (c) the submit task is deduped on `aai-submit-{session_id}` (sessions.py:1126) and the worker short-circuits with already_submitted once `metadata["jobs"]` exists (backend/app/routes/internal_transcription.py:410-418), so a second segment is never transcribed; (d) the poller finishes as soon as every recorded job has utterances (internal_transcription.py:611-649), which with segments would generate the note after segment 0.

CONTRACT — `POST /api/sessions/{id}/upload-audio` (sessions.py:1151) gains three optional multipart form fields: `segment_index` (int ≥ 0), `segment_offset_seconds` (float ≥ 0; seconds from session start to this segment's first sample), `final` (bool, default false; true on the last segment). `segment_index` present ⇒ segmented mode; the other two are validated only then (offset required in segmented mode, 422 if missing).

ROUTE (sessions.py, `_stream_and_submit_assemblyai` :1075-1150 and the gate at :1195):
- Segmented mode also accepts status in_progress; on the first segment the session moves to transcribing exactly as today.
- Objects: `_audio_multipart_object_name(session_id, channel, segment_index=None)` — with an index, append `.seg{index:03d}` before the extension so segments never overwrite each other.
- Manifest lives in the existing JSONB column `transcription_job_metadata` (backend/app/db/models.py:177 — NO schema change): `{"provider": "assemblyai", "segments": [{"index": n, "offset_seconds": x, "therapist": obj, "client": obj}], "final": bool, "jobs": [...]}`. Re-uploading an index replaces that entry (idempotent retry); `final` is sticky once true. Non-segmented uploads keep today's `{"provider": ..., "state": "submitting"}` shape.
- `audio_gcs_path` keeps the latest segment pair (the existing "incomplete audio" guard at internal_transcription.py:420-428 reads it).
- Dedup key becomes `aai-submit-{session_id}-{segment_index}` and the task payload gains `segment_index`; the whole-session key is unchanged when no index is given.

WORKER (`assemblyai_submit`, internal_transcription.py:371-488): when the payload carries `segment_index`, resolve that segment from the manifest (missing → log + return not_found, non-retryable); if a job tagged with that index already exists → already_submitted (idempotent); otherwise download that segment's two objects, call `service.submit_dual_channel` (backend/app/services/assemblyai_transcription_service.py:335-383, returns one job per channel with an `offset_map` relative to the segment), tag each job with `segment_index`, and add `offset_seconds` to every `offset_map` entry's original-timeline value so `parse_result` (:392-437) needs no change; APPEND to `jobs` rather than replace. Enqueue the poller only when the manifest is `final` (or in non-segmented mode, as today) — polling before the last segment would burn the 240×15 s budget (:502-503) on a session still being recorded.

POLLER (`transcription_poll`, :551-660): one extra completion condition — in segmented mode, finish only when `final` is true AND every manifest segment has at least one tagged job; otherwise persist progress and re-enqueue with the normal delay (covers a final segment whose submit task ran before an earlier segment's). `merge_utterances` (:449-455) already sorts by original start across jobs, so the transcript is time-correct without further change.

TESTS (extend, do not rewrite): backend/tests/test_audio_upload_async.py — new class TestSegmentedUpload mirroring `test_streams_to_storage_and_enqueues_submit` (:54) and its `_seed_recording_complete` (:23) / `_assemblyai_settings` (:38) helpers: in_progress + segment_index=0 → 202 and objects named `...seg000`; second segment appends to the manifest and enqueues with the `-1` dedup key; re-upload of index 0 replaces, not duplicates; `final=true` sticks; segment fields with provider=whisper → 400 SEGMENTS_UNSUPPORTED; segment_index without offset → 422; all existing tests unchanged and green. backend/tests/test_internal_transcription.py — in TestAssemblyAiSubmitWorker (:32): segment submit appends tagged jobs with shifted offset_map and does not enqueue the poller when not final; a second segment is not short-circuited by already_submitted (:83 stays green for the non-segmented case); in TestTranscriptionPoll (:171): all jobs complete but final=false → re-enqueued, not completed; final=true with a segment lacking jobs → re-enqueued; final=true and all segments' jobs complete → completion with a transcript whose utterances are in original-time order across two segments (fixture: segment 0 offset 0, segment 1 offset 300, synthetic word timestamps). Audio bytes in every test are synthetic (a few KB of zeros / the existing helpers) — never real recordings.

OUT OF SCOPE: client-side segmentation (companion apps, separate work); the signed-URL init/finalize path (sessions.py:1326-1420 — stays whole-file); Whisper; any retention/purge change (segment objects live under the same session prefix the purge job already deletes — verify by reading the purge's prefix match, do not change it); note generation.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: offsets are supplied by the client, not inferred from byte counts (VAD trimming makes server-side inference wrong); the manifest lives in the existing JSONB column, no migration; poll only after final; whole-session uploads are untouched; no new queue.

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI/HIPAA: session audio is PHI at runtime; every test uses synthetic bytes, in-memory repos and the mocked provider, no captured audio or real transcripts · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none (same queue, same bucket; object naming is additive) · auth/RLS design: none (same dependencies, same tenant resolution via `_resolve_schema_for_user`) · vendor dashboards: none (AssemblyAI only through the mocked service) · patent-adjacent: OSS-landing so the trigger is walked in full — segmented transport and offset bookkeeping are upload plumbing, not runtime governance or scoring · outbound: none.

SIZE NOTE: three production files (sessions.py, internal_transcription.py, a helper in the assemblyai service for the offset shift) and two test files; about two hours for one worker. Do not split — a route that accepts segments without the worker/poller changes silently drops every segment after the first.
acceptance_criteria:
1. FAILING-FIRST: the new TestSegmentedUpload and the segment cases in TestAssemblyAiSubmitWorker / TestTranscriptionPoll fail on main (segment fields are ignored, in_progress is rejected, the second segment is short-circuited) and pass after.
2. A request with none of the three fields produces exactly today's object names, metadata shape, dedup key and response — every pre-existing test in backend/tests/test_audio_upload_async.py and backend/tests/test_internal_transcription.py passes unmodified.
3. Segment objects are named `<channel>.seg000`, `.seg001`, ... under the existing per-session prefix; re-uploading an index replaces its manifest entry.
4. The worker appends jobs tagged with `segment_index` whose `offset_map` original-timeline values are shifted by `segment_offset_seconds`; the poller is enqueued only when the manifest is final.
5. The poller completes only when final is true and every segment has a job; the merged transcript from a two-segment fixture (offsets 0 and 300) is in original-time order.
6. Segment fields with provider=whisper → 400 SEGMENTS_UNSUPPORTED; `segment_index` without `segment_offset_seconds` → 422.
7. No Alembic migration in the diff (JSONB manifest only); `make check` green (ruff + mypy + pytest).
8. PR text reads as ordinary OSS work; no tracker ids.
notes:
llama-ok + budget:7200 applied by eng-head 2026-08-26 (pass 2): server slice only (segment_index/offset/final on upload-audio, JSONB manifest, per-segment submit key, offset-shifted jobs, poll gates on final; whole-file path byte-identical). Honest size ~2h so the budget label is set; the spec must not be split further (a route without worker/poller silently drops segments). Synthetic audio only. Public-repo rules apply.

title: Cover PATCH /api/sessions/{id}/status and PATCH /api/sessions/{id} with route tests
description: The two session-lifecycle endpoints the desktop clients drive after Start Session — PATCH /api/sessions/{id}/status (state-machine transition) and PATCH /api/sessions/{id} (reschedule / metadata) — have no route tests. The service layer is covered, but the HTTP status and error-code mapping (409 ALREADY_IN_STATUS, 400 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION, 400 TERMINAL_STATUS, 404 for another clinician's session) and the audit call are unverified at the route boundary. Sibling routes in the same file are covered by test_routes_sessions; these two were skipped.
design:
Tests only — no production code changes. NEW file backend/tests/test_routes_session_lifecycle.py (new file; keep it separate from test_routes_sessions.py so it does not collide with in-flight work there).

Routes under test: backend/app/routes/sessions.py:797-832 (`update_session_status`) and backend/app/routes/sessions.py:835-865 (`update_session_metadata`). Service behaviour they map: backend/app/services/session_service.py:664 (`transition_status` — raises SessionNotFoundError / SessionAlreadyInStatusError / InvalidStatusTransitionError against VALID_TRANSITIONS at :144-156) and :712 (`update_session_metadata` — raises SessionInTerminalStatusError for TERMINAL_STATUSES at :158). Request models: backend/app/models/session.py:106-122.

Fixtures: reuse the conftest `client`, `mock_session_repo`, `mock_user_id`, `mock_audit_service` (backend/tests/conftest.py:140,192,261,309; the session repo and audit service are dependency-overridden at :331 and :361). Copy the `_seed_session(...)` helper shape from test_routes_sessions (lines 38-60) — owner, status, scheduled_at — into the new file rather than importing it across test modules. Spy the audit with `patch.object(mock_audit_service, "log_session_action")` as the audit tests in test_routes_sessions do.

Cases (each its own test, names as listed):
status —
  test_status_scheduled_to_in_progress_returns_200: seed SCHEDULED, PATCH {"status": "in_progress"} → 200, body["status"] == "in_progress", repo row updated.
  test_status_same_status_returns_409_already_in_status: seed IN_PROGRESS, PATCH in_progress → 409, error code "ALREADY_IN_STATUS".
  test_status_disallowed_transition_returns_400: seed SCHEDULED, PATCH {"status": "finalized"} (not in VALID_TRANSITIONS[scheduled]) → 400, code "INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION".
  test_status_unknown_value_returns_422: PATCH {"status": "nope"} → 422 (pydantic enum).
  test_status_other_users_session_returns_404: seed owned by another id → 404 (no leak of existence).
  test_status_audits_the_transition: assert `log_session_action` called once with `changes={"status": "in_progress"}`. Do not assert the AuditAction enum value: the route passes SESSION_CREATED today (sessions.py:822), which reads like a copy-paste slip — leave a one-line comment and do not change it here.
metadata —
  test_metadata_reschedule_returns_200_with_new_time: seed SCHEDULED, PATCH {"scheduled_at": <iso>, "duration_minutes": 30} → 200; body reflects both.
  test_metadata_empty_body_is_a_noop_200: PATCH {} → 200; audit changes["changed_fields"] == [].
  test_metadata_on_finalized_session_returns_400_terminal: seed FINALIZED → 400, code "TERMINAL_STATUS".
  test_metadata_duration_out_of_range_returns_422: duration_minutes 0 → 422.
  test_metadata_other_users_session_returns_404.

title: Settings → Booking links: list, create, shareable URL, activate/deactivate
description:
The management API at /api/booking-links has full CRUD (create, list, update copy/duration, activate/deactivate, delete) and ZERO frontend. grep finds no reference to it outside the public booker page. A therapist cannot create, rename, deactivate, or delete a booking link from the app at all — someone has to POST to the API by hand.

The public booker page (app/book/[slug]/page.tsx) shipped in phase 1; this is the other half.

Should surface: slug availability feedback (reserved slugs 400, taken slugs 409), the copy/duration/session-type fields, an active toggle, the shareable URL with a copy button, and — once the tombstone work lands — a deletion flow that explains the slug stays claimed.

Noted in docs/design/public-booking.md under 'Frontend' as the natural next step.

SCOPE (first half of the Settings UI — split 2026-08-26 to fit one worker-hour; edit/delete are PABLO-e3a.13): a "Booking links" section on Settings that LISTS the caller's links, CREATES one with usable slug feedback, shows the shareable URL with a copy button, and toggles active/inactive. OUT OF SCOPE: editing copy/duration and deleting (e3a.13); any backend change (the API is complete: POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/booking-links, backend/app/routes/booking_links.py:50-130); e3a.5 tombstone copy (e3a.13 owns it); e3a.8 CAPTCHA site key on the card; e3a.11 per-practice domains (the URL is always `${window.location.origin}/book/${slug}` — the booker page lives at frontend/app/book/[slug]/page.tsx on the same origin); prefilling host_name from the profile; slug availability pre-check (the server's 400/409 IS the feedback — one round trip, no new endpoint).

COMPONENT BEHAVIOUR:
- Loading: Skeleton rows (pattern: AvailabilitySettings). Error: inline "Couldn't load your booking links." Empty: "No booking links yet." with the create button visible.

title: Audit trail attributes anonymous public bookings to the clinician
description:
From the 2026-08-20 review of claude/public-booking-links.

create_public_booking logs PATIENT_CREATED and APPOINTMENT_CREATED with ctx.owner as the actor, because AuditService has no representation for an anonymous booker. The trail therefore reads as though the clinician created that chart.

changes={'source': 'public_booking'} marks the provenance, but the actor field itself is wrong — and it is wrong precisely in the spoofed-booking case the design doc accepts as a phase-1 limit, where the audit trail is exactly what a clinician would consult to work out where a chart came from. HIPAA 164.312(b) wants to know WHO acted.

Fix: give AuditService a real anonymous-actor concept (public booking link + client IP, no PHI) rather than borrowing the owner's identity. Check every consumer of the actor field before changing the record shape.

Recorded in docs/design/public-booking.md under 'What phase 1 deliberately leaves out'.
design:
BLOCKED BY PABLO-e3a.12: public_booking.py paths are cited from origin/claude/public-booking-links (tip 34465f8). audit_service.py, backend/app/models/audit.py / users.py / test_audit_actor_type.py paths are on main today.

SCOPE: have a public booking's audit rows say an ANONYMOUS principal acted, using the actor_type discriminator that #771 (a91c5d3e7b28, "Record what kind of principal performed an audited action") added — NOT a second principal marker. Carry link provenance in `changes`, PHI-free. Keep the row inside the owner's scope so it is still writable under RLS and still visible in the owner's own trail.

OUT OF SCOPE: e3a.2/.3/.4 (identity chain) — but e3a.3's new writes (pending_confirmation appointment, quarantined pending patient) and e3a.9's booker-side cancel MUST reuse ACTOR_TYPE_ANONYMOUS from this bead; e3a.5 tombstones; e3a.7/.13 UI; the audit_logs RLS policy (explicitly deferred by #771's own commit message; does not change here); adding `changes` to the self-audit response; the SaaS outbox shipper (see CONSUMERS 5 — pre-existing gap, THERAPY follow-up, not OSS work).

MECHANISM, in order:
1. Vocabulary backend/app/models/audit.py:261-271: add `ACTOR_TYPE_ANONYMOUS = "anonymous"` and set `ACTOR_TYPES = (CLINICIAN, PATIENT, ANONYMOUS)`. Comment: "an unauthenticated principal acting through a public surface (today: a booking link). For this kind, user_id names the SCOPE principal — the clinician whose RLS context the write happened under — not the actor; the actor is identified by ip_address plus the provenance in changes." AuditLogEntry (:273-330) already carries actor_type; nothing else changes in the model.
2. NO MIGRATION. audit_logs.actor_type is `VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'clinician'` with no CHECK constraint (backend/alembic/versions/a91c5d3e7b28_audit_logs_actor_type.py:55-62; backend/app/db/tenant_template.sql:141). "anonymous" fits. No tenant_template regen.
3. backend/app/services/audit_service.py: `log` (:131-162) gains `actor_type: str = ACTOR_TYPE_CLINICIAN` and passes it to AuditLogEntry (:150-160). title: Tombstone deleted booking links so a released slug cannot be re-registered
description:
From the 2026-08-20 review of claude/public-booking-links.

BookingLinkRepository.delete is a hard DELETE, so a released slug is immediately re-registrable by ANY clinician on the deployment. A therapist who prints /book/dr-smith on a business card, then deletes the link, hands whoever claims that slug next the still-circulating traffic — and with it the names and emails of the original practice's clients, collected on a booking form that looks legitimate.

RESERVED_SLUGS guards app routes; nothing guards reuse. This is an impersonation vector, not just a hygiene issue.

Fix: soft-delete the row (deleted_at) and keep the slug claimed. get_by_slug must treat a tombstoned link as missing; create must still 409 against a tombstoned slug. Needs a migration and a regenerated tenant_template.sql in the same commit — booking_links is platform-scoped, so confirm which template applies.

Recorded in docs/design/public-booking.md under 'What phase 1 deliberately leaves out'.
design:
BLOCKED BY PABLO-e3a.12: every path below is cited from origin/claude/public-booking-links (not yet on main). Line numbers are from that branch tip (34465f8).

SCOPE: soft-delete booking links. Add a nullable deleted_at to platform.booking_links; DELETE stamps it (and clears is_active) instead of removing the row; every read path treats a tombstoned row as absent; the existing UNIQUE(slug) keeps the slug claimed forever. No new endpoint, no response-shape change.

OUT OF SCOPE (siblings own these): e3a.2/.3/.4 identity chain (e3a.2 also adds a column + migration to this table — see SEQUENCING); e3a.7 / e3a.13 the Settings UI and its "slug stays reserved" copy; e3a.10 owner account state — note platform.booking_links.user_id is ON DELETE CASCADE (migration c8d2f4a71e93:38-39), so deleting a platform user still releases their slugs; that is owner-lifecycle territory, leave it; e3a.11 domains (when UNIQUE(slug) relaxes to UNIQUE(practice_id, slug) the tombstones relax with it, nothing to pre-build). Also out: any restore/undelete endpoint, and letting the original owner re-claim their own tombstoned slug (see DECISIONS).

MECHANISM, in order:
1. Domain model backend/app/models/booking_link.py:48-68 (BookingLink dataclass): add `deleted_at: datetime | None = None` after practice_schema. BookingLinkResponse (:88-113) does NOT gain the field — a tombstoned link never reaches a response.
2. ORM backend/app/db/platform_models.py, class BookingLinkRow (appended by the branch after PasskeyBackupCodeRow, ~:537-575): add `deleted_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True))`. Keep `slug ... unique=True` exactly as is — that constraint IS the tombstone.
3. Migration (NEW) backend/alembic/versions/<rev>_booking_links_deleted_at.py: `ALTER TABLE platform.booking_links ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ`; downgrade drops it. down_revision = the OSS chain head at merge time (`cd backend && poetry run alembic heads`) — after e3a.12 that is d1e7c4a92b58 unless e3a.2 has landed first, then e3a.2's revision. No new index: one row per link, the table is tiny. TEMPLATE: none. backend/app/db/tenant_template.sql is the per-tenant schema; platform tables are not in it (the branch's own template diff is only ix_patients_email_lower on patients). That answers the description's "confirm which template applies".
4. Repository contract backend/app/repositories/booking_link.py:26-59: docstrings only. get_by_slug (:30-35): "Resolve a LIVE slug; a tombstoned link resolves to None, exactly like a missing one." delete (:57-59): "Tombstone a link, scoped to its owner. Returns whether a live row existed." No new abstract methods.
5. In-memory backend/app/repositories/booking_link.py:62-101: get_by_slug/get/list_by_user skip rows with deleted_at set; create (:83-88) keeps checking EVERY row for the slug, live or tombstoned (it already iterates all of _links — the change is that delete no longer removes the row); update must refuse a tombstoned row (return path: treat as missing, the route 404s via get first anyway); delete (:95-101) sets deleted_at=utc_now(), is_active=False, updated_at=now, returns True; a second delete returns False.
6. Postgres backend/app/repositories/postgres/booking_link.py: `_row_to_link` (:28-42) maps deleted_at. get_by_slug (:49-61), get (:63-68), list_by_user (:70-76), update (:110-122): add `BookingLinkRow.deleted_at.is_(None)` to the WHERE. create (:78-108): UNCHANGED — the UNIQUE(slug) violation already maps 23505 -> SlugTakenError, and a tombstoned row still holds the slug, so a tombstoned slug 409s with zero new code; the comment at :22-25 stays true. delete (:124-136): replace the DELETE with `update(BookingLinkRow).where(id == link_id, user_id == user_id, deleted_at.is_(None)).values(deleted_at=now, is_active=False, updated_at=now)`; keep the CursorResult cast and `bool(result.rowcount)`.
7. Route backend/app/routes/booking_links.py: delete_booking_link (:122-130) keeps 204 / 404-on-repeat; docstring becomes "Tombstone a booking link. Its public URL 404s immediately and the slug stays claimed." create_booking_link (:80-81): the 409 message becomes "This slug is taken. Slugs stay reserved after a link is deleted, so pick another." — one message for live and tombstoned collisions (no live-vs-deleted oracle between clinicians; the owner who just deleted it gets the explanation they need).
8. Public path backend/app/routes/public_booking.py:104-106: no change — get_by_slug returning None already yields the shared _LINK_NOT_FOUND 404, so tombstoned == missing == inactive on the public surface.
9. docs/design/public-booking.md: add a `deleted_at` row to the Data model table (:42-54) with "tombstone; the slug stays claimed"; in Request flow step 2 (:62-63) say "missing, inactive, or deleted links are an identical 404"; rewrite the "Slug reuse after deletion" bullet (:277-287) as shipped behaviour and move it out of "What phase 1 deliberately leaves out".
10. backend/scripts/check_route_audit.py: no route added, no change.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- A tombstone is permanent and binds everyone, INCLUDING the original owner. No restore endpoint, no "revive if same user_id". A clinician who may want a slug back deactivates (is_active=false, already supported) rather than deletes; the UI child e3a.13 says so at delete time. This is the acceptance text as filed ("creating a link with a tombstoned slug 409s", unqualified).
- delete also sets is_active=false, so any future code that checks is_active alone still hides the row. The deleted_at filter is the real gate; this is belt-and-braces, not the mechanism.
- Repeat DELETE stays 404 (unchanged), not idempotent 204.
- Tombstoned links are absent from GET /api/booking-links and from PATCH (404). Not listed-but-greyed.
- UNIQUE(slug) remains the sole reuse guard. No separate reserved-slug table, no RESERVED_SLUGS growth.
- No tenant template regen (platform table). No SaaS-side change.
- Owner-deletion CASCADE releasing slugs is accepted for now (e3a.10).

SEQUENCING: after e3a.12 (code must be on main). e3a.2 (P1) also adds a column + migration to platform.booking_links on the same alembic chain — two migrations on one chain are a hub-file collision git cannot see; land e3a.2 first and re-point this bead's down_revision at merge time (whoever merges second re-points; never `alembic merge`). e3a.13 (delete UI) depends on this bead.

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI/HIPAA: none; the table holds slug/copy/duration, tests run on in-memory fixtures with synthetic data, and the fix exists to keep client names away from a slug squatter. money/entitlement: none. prod infra: one additive nullable column via the normal alembic/deploy path; no destructive op. auth/RLS: platform schema has no RLS; owner scoping stays the user_id WHERE filter; no policy touched. vendor dashboards: none. patent-adjacent: OSS, so the trigger holds in full — booking-link tombstones are not in any claim family (inbox self-learning, stage-director/briefing, ordinal/anchored scoring, companion runtime governance, scaffold-vs-generate) and docs/design carries no Patent note / counsel-gated / candidate claim marker for this surface. outbound communication: none.

1. test_deactivate_and_delete_booking_link (branch :429-443) extended: after `DELETE /api/booking-links/{id}` -> 204, `link_repo.get_by_slug("intro-call") is None` still holds AND `POST /api/booking-links` with slug "intro-call" -> 409 (fails today: the slug is re-registrable), AND a second DELETE -> 404.
2. NEW test_deleted_slug_cannot_be_reclaimed_by_another_user: owner creates and deletes "intro-call"; `link_repo.create(_link(slug="intro-call", user_id="other-user-999"))` raises SlugTakenError (in-memory), and the same via the route for a second authed caller if the suite has one -> 409.
3. NEW test_tombstoned_link_is_a_public_404: public_client; create a link, call `link_repo.delete(link.id, OWNER_ID)`; GET card and GET slots both 404 with the same body as an unknown slug (`_LINK_NOT_FOUND`), and POST bookings 404 too.
4. NEW test_deleted_links_are_absent_from_owner_reads: after delete, `GET /api/booking-links` total == 0 and `PATCH /api/booking-links/{id}` -> 404.

6. backend/tests_integration/database/test_booking_link_tombstone_db.py (NEW) (mirror the fixtures in backend/tests_integration/database/test_appointment_overlap_db.py): on real Postgres, delete then `PostgresBookingLinkRepository.create` with the same slug raises SlugTakenError (the 23505 path), get_by_slug returns None, and `SELECT deleted_at FROM platform.booking_links WHERE slug=...` is not null.
7. Migration file present in backend/alembic/versions/ in the same commit as the model change; `poetry run alembic heads` prints one head; backend/app/db/tenant_template.sql is untouched by this bead.

title: Optional onboarding step: capture working days and hours, create availability rules
description: Booking availability is the one setting whose absence silently disables behavior: with no availability rules, free-slot queries return nothing and scheduling features have nothing to offer. Today nothing in the first-run experience captures it — a new clinician has to discover the availability settings on their own. An optional onboarding step ("When do you work?") that creates per-weekday working-hours rules closes the cold-start gap at the moment of highest intent, and makes the zero-rules empty-state seeding an occasional fallback instead of the primary path.
design:
Add an optional, skippable last step to the stock onboarding surface: pick working days (checkbox per weekday) and one time range applied to all selected days. Completing it creates one working_hours rule per selected day through the existing availability API; skipping creates nothing. Both paths mark the step done so the resolver moves on.

SUBSTRATE (verified against main 2026-08-26):
- Onboarding router: frontend/app/onboarding/page.tsx:29 `firstIncompleteStep(getOnboardingSurface(), status)`, :31-35 redirects to `next.path` or /dashboard. Dashboard gate: frontend/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:73 uses `firstIncompleteRequiredStep`, which skips steps with `required: false` (frontend/src/lib/onboarding/types.ts:68-74). Step shape: types.ts:25-42 `StepDef { id, path, gate(status) => boolean, required?, group? }` — completion IS the gate; "optional" IS `required: false`. There is no existing optional step to mirror: the stock surface is frontend/src/lib/onboarding/minimal.ts:35-42 (passkey only). frontend/src/lib/onboarding/surface.ts:10-13 documents that a downstream build may shadow the module with its own step list — such builds register this step themselves; this bead edits only minimal.ts.
- Done-signal without backend changes: the backend already returns `onboarding_state` in GET /api/users/me/status (backend/app/routes/users.py:170) and accepts it in PATCH /api/users/me (users.py:368-370; backend/app/models/user.py:34 UpdateUserRequest.onboarding_state, values "in_progress" | "completed"). The frontend types don't carry it yet: add `onboarding_state: string | null` to UserStatusBase (frontend/src/lib/api/users.ts:35) and `onboarding_state?: "in_progress" | "completed"` to UpdateUserRequestBase (users.ts:67); send it via the existing updateUserProfile (users.ts:114, PATCH /api/users/me).
- Rule creation seam: frontend/src/hooks/useAvailability.ts:32 useCreateAvailabilityRule → frontend/src/lib/api/availability.ts:26 createAvailabilityRule → POST /api/availability/rules. Payload shape to copy EXACTLY from the settings seed handler frontend/src/components/settings/AvailabilitySettings.tsx:819-821: `{ rule_type: "working_hours", enforcement: "hard", params: { day_of_week, start, end } }` with day_of_week 0 = Monday (backend/app/scheduling_engine/models/availability.py:14 RuleType.WORKING_HOURS; param validation backend/app/services/availability_parse_service.py:174-180) and start/end as "HH:MM".
- Page pattern: frontend/app/onboarding/passkey/page.tsx (server component: auth check + redirects at :33-53) — mirror its auth handling for the new page. Hour Select control to reuse: frontend/src/components/calendar/WorkingHoursSettings.tsx:88-97 (hour integers, formatted as `${String(h).padStart(2,"0")}:00` like AvailabilitySettings.tsx:817-818).

MECHANISM:
1. minimal.ts: add `SCHEDULE_STEP = { id: "schedule", path: "/onboarding/schedule", gate: (status) => status.onboarding_state === "completed", required: false }` appended AFTER the passkey step (steps = [...passkey if enabled, SCHEDULE_STEP]).
2. New page frontend/app/onboarding/schedule/page.tsx (NEW) — a server component mirroring the auth handling of frontend/app/onboarding/passkey/page.tsx rendering a client component frontend/src/components/onboarding/ScheduleStep.tsx (NEW): seven weekday checkboxes (Mon–Fri checked by default), start/end hour selects (default 09:00–17:00), buttons "Save" and "Skip for now".
3. Save: for each selected day call the create mutation with the payload above (sequential mutateAsync so a failure stops before the profile update), then `updateUserProfile({ onboarding_state: "completed" })`, then `router.push("/onboarding")` so the resolver advances. Save is disabled with zero days selected or end <= start.
4. Skip: `updateUserProfile({ onboarding_state: "completed" })` only, emit the existing analytics event `onboarding_step_skipped` (frontend/src/lib/analytics/types.ts:33) with step "schedule", then `router.push("/onboarding")`.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: step is optional (`required: false`) and last; done-signal is `onboarding_state === "completed"` set on both Save and Skip (existing field and endpoint, no backend or schema change); one time range for all selected days (per-day ranges belong to the settings surface); enforcement "hard" (matches the settings seed handler); rules are created only on explicit Save, never on Skip; no session-length/break/alignment inputs (defaults apply; settings owns them).
Do NOT touch: the availability engine; AvailabilitySettings.tsx and WorkingHoursSettings.tsx (their beads #755/#757 have landed — reuse their API layer only); the passkey step; surface.ts.

MIGRATION: none.

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI: none (clinician's own working hours, no patient data) · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none · auth/RLS: none (the new page reuses the passkey page's existing auth check; no auth logic added) · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: none (a weekday/hours form; none of the known claim surfaces) · outbound: none.
acceptance_criteria:
1. frontend/src/lib/onboarding/__tests__/surface.test.ts: the stock surface contains a step with id "schedule", `required === false`, positioned after "passkey" (passkey remains index 0 when enabled); `firstIncompleteRequiredStep` returns null for a status with mfa_enrolled_at set and onboarding_state null (the optional step never blocks the dashboard); `firstIncompleteStep` returns the schedule step for that status and null once onboarding_state === "completed".
