title: Egress seam: a redacted-text type plus a sink registry, so unredacted text cannot leave
description:
Redaction exists as a service but nothing enforces that it ran. Whether sensitive text is redacted before it leaves the process currently depends on each call site remembering to redact — an invariant that holds until someone adds a log line.

Introduces a type that can only be produced by the redaction path, and a registry of egress points that accept only that type, so the guarantee is structural rather than remembered.
design:
Code-verified 2026-08-11.

`backend/app/services/pii_redaction_service.py` defines `PIIRedactionService`
and currently has **no callers anywhere in the tree**. Redaction exists as a
capability but nothing structurally guarantees it is applied before text
leaves the process. Today "we redacted it" is a property of whoever wrote the
call site remembering to, which is the kind of invariant that holds until the
day someone adds a log line.

Make it a property of the type system instead.

## Two pieces

**1. A `RedactedText` type.** A thin wrapper that can only be constructed by
passing text through the redaction service. It is not a subclass of `str` and
does not implicitly coerce to one — the whole point is that an unredacted
`str` cannot be substituted for it by accident. Unwrapping to a raw string is
possible but explicit and greppable, so the escape hatch is auditable rather
than invisible.

**2. A sink registry.** The places text can leave the process — log emission,
outbound HTTP bodies, object storage writes, anything rendering to a file —
register themselves as sinks that accept `RedactedText` only. A sink that
receives a bare string raises rather than emitting. Registration is explicit
so the set of egress points is enumerable and reviewable; a new sink that
forgets to register is a code-review finding, not a silent leak.

## Why the guard belongs at this layer

An egress guard is only as good as the lowest layer it covers. Building it
above the code that handles sensitive text leaves that code unguarded, and
anything layered on top inherits the gap permanently rather than temporarily.
Putting the type and the registry here means every consumer can adopt it,
and the enforcement point sits underneath the paths that need it.

## Scope discipline

This piece of work delivers the type, the registry, the enforcement, and
conversion of a small number of representative sinks — not a tree-wide
migration. A guard nothing uses proves nothing, and a tree-wide migration in
one change is unreviewable. Pick the sinks that carry the highest-risk text
today and leave the rest for follow-on work, with the registry making the
remaining unconverted sinks visible.

Failure mode to avoid: a guard that is easy to bypass silently. If unwrapping
becomes the path of least resistance the seam is decorative. Unwrapping should
be more effort than doing it correctly.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A `RedactedText` type exists that can only be constructed by passing text
   through the redaction service. A test asserts it cannot be constructed
   directly from an arbitrary string.
2. `RedactedText` does not subclass `str` and does not implicitly coerce. A
   test asserts a function annotated for `RedactedText` rejects a bare string
   at runtime.
3. A sink registry exists, sinks register explicitly, and the registered set
   is enumerable at runtime for review.
4. A registered sink receiving a bare string raises rather than emitting. A
   test proves the raise, and proves the text does not reach the sink.
5. At least two representative real sinks are converted and pass their
   existing tests unchanged.
6. Unwrapping to a raw string is possible, explicit, and greppable by a
   single distinctive name. A test asserts the unwrap path is the only way to
   obtain the raw value.
7. No behavior change for callers that were already redacting correctly — the
   existing suite stays green.
8. Lint, format, and type checks pass.
notes: Not authorized yet — prerequisite. This builds an egress seam around backend/app/services/pii_redaction_service.py, but that module's dependencies (presidio-analyzer, faker) are not installed anywhere, so it is currently dead code — the subject of its own open issue. Building a sink registry on top of a module that cannot import will not produce a working seam. Sequence the dependency fix first, then this.

title: Zero availability rules means two different things depending on which engine path you ask
description:
With no rules configured, get_free_slots returns [] (default DENY -
scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:69 returns early when there is no
working_hours rule) while check_conflicts returns no conflicts (default ALLOW -
zero rules means nothing to violate). So "what is free?" answers nothing and
"is this time OK?" answers yes. The two halves of the engine disagree about
what an unconfigured therapist means, and callers cannot tell "not configured"
from "no openings" because both arrive as an empty list.
design:
SEMANTICS: zero rules means NOT CONFIGURED - a state the product names -
rather than open or closed. Nothing is asserted about availability that the
therapist did not configure.

READ PATH. Distinguish "no working hours configured" from "no openings in this
window". Callers must be able to tell them apart without guessing: a typed
result or explicit sentinel, not an empty list for both. The first case is an
onboarding prompt pointing at the availability settings surface; the second is
a real answer. Never render "not configured" as "no availability".

WRITE PATH. Stay PERMISSIVE when nothing is configured. Default-deny would
break booking for every practice that has not set up rules - which is most of
them - the moment enforcement lands. Make the unconfigured case observable
rather than silent.

This keeps the two halves consistent in MEANING even though they differ in
mechanism. Enforcement work on the write path must honour the permissive rule:
a practice with zero rules keeps booking exactly as it does today.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A caller of get_free_slots can distinguish "no working hours configured"
   from "no openings in this window" without inspecting the rule set itself.
2. A test per case: unconfigured practice, configured practice with a full
   day, and configured practice with openings.
3. check_conflicts and get_free_slots agree in meaning for an unconfigured
   practice - neither claims the calendar is open, neither claims it is closed.
4. Enforcement on the write path remains permissive with zero rules, proven by
   a test that books successfully for a practice with no rules.

title: Purge-cron and export tests: assert real delete ordering + scoped notes fetch
description: Residual from the test-hardening sweep (rest verified done: auth-recovery client tests, session-status/dashboard-banner component tests, user-scoped notes fetch in export_service). Two assertions remain: (a) confirm test_hard_purge_cron exercises the real _delete_* ordering rather than mocking it out — if mocked, rewrite against the real functions with a fake store; (b) test_multi_tenant_security should explicitly assert export_service fetches notes via notes_repo.list_by_patient(patient_id, user_id) (the user-scoped call), so a regression back to an unscoped fetch fails the suite.
design:
Residual from the test-hardening sweep. The rest of that sweep is verified done
(auth-recovery client tests, session-status / dashboard-banner component tests,
user-scoped notes fetch in export_service). Two assertions remain, both about tests
that currently pass without proving what they claim.

## Design

(a) Purge ordering — `test_hard_purge_cron`.
    Determine whether the test exercises the real `_delete_*` functions or mocks them
    out. If they are mocked, the test proves nothing about ordering: rewrite it against
    the REAL `_delete_*` functions backed by a fake store that RECORDS the call order,
    then assert that order explicitly. Blob deletes must be asserted to happen before
    the row deletes that reference them, so a future reordering fails the suite.
    Do not assert on mock call-order against mocked-out delete functions — that just
    re-states the mock.

(b) Export scoping — `test_multi_tenant_security`.
    Add an explicit assertion that `export_service` fetches notes via
    `notes_repo.list_by_patient(patient_id, user_id)` — the user-scoped call — and not
    an unscoped variant. Assert on the ARGUMENTS, not merely that some fetch happened,
    so a regression that drops `user_id` fails.

## Constraints

- Test-only change. Do not modify the purge cron or export service themselves; if
  either turns out to be genuinely wrong, stop and note it on the bead instead of
  fixing it here.
- Both tests must FAIL when the behaviour they guard is reverted. Demonstrate this by
  temporarily breaking each behaviour locally and confirming the failure, then restore.

## Files

- backend/tests/ — the existing `test_hard_purge_cron` and `test_multi_tenant_security`
  modules.
acceptance_criteria: Both assertions exist and pass in CI; purge-ordering test fails if blob/row delete order regresses; export test fails if the notes fetch loses user scoping.

title: Guard remaining patient-repo methods against non-UUID ids (restore, close_chart)
description: Follow-up from the non-UUID 4xx sweep: the two named repros (GET /api/patients/<non-uuid> and appointments ?start=garbage) are fixed — _is_uuid guard in PostgresPatientRepository.get() returns 404, and list_appointments types start/end as datetime giving 422. Residual: restore and close_chart call _session.get(PatientRow, patient_id) WITHOUT an _is_uuid guard, so a non-UUID id may still surface a DB-layer 500. Confirm at runtime, add the guard + a test asserting 404, and sweep any other unguarded patient-repo methods.
design:
Follow-up from the non-UUID 4xx sweep. The two named repros are already fixed:
`GET /api/patients/<non-uuid>` returns 404 via the `_is_uuid` guard in
`PostgresPatientRepository.get()`, and `list_appointments` types `start`/`end` as
`datetime` so a garbage value gives 422.

Residual: `restore` and `close_chart` in `PostgresPatientRepository`
(backend/app/repositories/patient_repository.py) call
`self._session.get(PatientRow, patient_id)` with NO `_is_uuid` guard, so a non-UUID id
can still surface as a DB-layer 500 instead of a clean 404.

## Design

1. Confirm the 500 at runtime first — drive each unguarded method with a non-UUID id
   and capture the actual behaviour. If a route already rejects the id upstream (path
   converter, Pydantic), say so on the bead rather than adding a redundant guard.
2. Apply the SAME `_is_uuid` guard already used by `get()` to `restore` and
   `close_chart` — return the same not-found result `get()` returns, so the route
   layer maps it to 404 exactly as it does today. Do not invent a new error type.
3. Sweep the rest of the class for the same shape: any method taking a `patient_id`
   and reaching `_session.get(PatientRow, ...)` or filtering on the id column without
   a guard. Fix each the same way.
4. Keep the guard in the repository, not the route — that is where `get()` puts it,
   and it is the layer every caller shares.

## Files

- backend/app/repositories/patient_repository.py
- backend/tests/ — the existing patient-repository / patient-route test module that
  already covers the `get()` non-UUID 404 case; extend it rather than adding a new file.
acceptance_criteria: restore/close_chart (and any other unguarded patient-repo method) return 404 for non-UUID ids; regression test covers each; suite green in CI.

Two-layer assertion (app round-trip + inspect the credential row), mirroring the established upload-e2e pattern. This is a new capability — OSS frontend/e2e/ currently has only an unauthenticated scaffold (patients.spec.ts) and is not a CI gate; the virtual authenticator is what finally makes auth e2e runnable OSS-locally without the secret-laden deployed harness. Note the friction items in the design doc: WebAuthn is origin-bound (test backend must allow the test origin + rp_id), the custom-token mint needs the Firebase emulator or a dev project, and the native/desktop + cross-device-hybrid paths are out of virtual-authenticator scope. See docs/internal/passkey-auth-e2e-design.md.

title: Consolidate dashboard data fetching: aggregate summary endpoint + dedupe per-navigation status fetches
description:
The dashboard currently issues ~11 API calls per page load: each panel (Today, Week, AwaitingReview, Compliance, Banners) fetches its own endpoints (appointments x2 ranges, sessions, patients, compliance, compliance/templates, supervision), layout chrome adds baa-status/preferences/devices, and /api/users/me/status is fetched server-side in both layout.tsx and page.tsx with no dedup (server fetches bypass the React Query cache). Every call pays fixed per-request overhead: token verification, idle-session check, identity lookup, audit write, one pooled DB connection.

PROPOSAL:
1. New GET /api/dashboard/summary returning {appointments_today, appointments_week, awaiting_review, compliance_summary, supervision_summary} in one response — one connection, one auth resolution, one audit entry. Panels keep their components; they read slices of the one query via React Query select. Detail endpoints stay for drill-down pages.
2. Dedupe the per-navigation getUserStatus server fetch with React cache() so layout+page share one call per request.
3. Audit layout-level queries (baa-status/preferences/devices) for staleTime: Infinity — they change rarely; refetch on explicit mutation instead of every mount.

title: apiClient: response-interceptor seam so deployments can observe responses without forking the client
description: apiClient is a single module with no extension point, so a deployment that needs to react to response shapes (maintenance-mode banners, telemetry) must fork the whole file — and forks silently miss upstream fixes (the 204 empty-body guard had to be applied twice). Add registerResponseInterceptor(fn): interceptors receive response.clone() after fetch, before parsing; errors in interceptors must not break the request path. Keep it dependency-free.

title: Make practice.audit_logs append-only (block UPDATE/DELETE at role level)
description:
PABLO-006 in the 2026-06-07 pentest (the run's one genuine finding). The per-tenant practice.audit_logs table does not block UPDATE/DELETE for the application DB role, so a compromised app role or insider could alter/erase the audit trail — a §164.312(c)(1) integrity gap. Cross-tenant isolation is unaffected (RLS intact); exploit requires already holding the app DB role, so low external reachability.

Fix: enforce append-only on audit_logs in the tenant template. Options: (a) REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_logs from the app role, or (b) a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that raises. Whatever is chosen must land in backend/app/db/tenant_template.sql AND the provisioning path (create_practice_schema reads the template directly — see CLAUDE.md guardrail #4), and be regenerated via regen_tenant_template.py. Retention/hard-purge jobs that legitimately DELETE expired audit rows (audit_retention_cron.py) run as a different role or must be exempted — verify the purge path still works after the REVOKE. Add an integration test asserting the app role cannot UPDATE/DELETE an audit_logs row while the retention job still can.
acceptance_criteria: app DB role cannot UPDATE or DELETE practice.audit_logs (verified by integration test); audit_retention_cron purge path still functions; tenant_template.sql regenerated and committed in the same change

title: Platform-audit high-value non-PHI events (admin/auth/account)
description:
The fail-closed route-audit guardrail (PABLO-xo3) classifies many handlers as non-PHI and therefore exempt from the per-tenant HIPAA audit_logs. Several of those are still operationally valuable and belong in the platform audit stream (PlatformAuditService -> platform_audit_logs, the PHI-free cross-tenant ops record) even though they carry no patient PHI:

- admin: disable_user / enable_user, add/remove allowlist entry (security-relevant account + access changes)
- auth: native code create / exchange (auth + token issuance events)
- users: accept_baa, record_mfa_enrollment, acknowledge_security_guide (compliance-evidence events)

Scope: add PlatformAuditAction values + emit PlatformAudit rows from these handlers. Keep payloads PHI-free (ids/emails/timestamps, no patient data). This is the 'valuable to the operator, not HIPAA-required' tier — distinct from the tenant audit the guardrail enforces. Decide per-handler which events are worth the row; not every exempt route needs one.

title: Make route-audit guardrail fail-closed (classify every route, not just known PHI paths)
description:
The route-audit guardrail (backend/scripts/check_route_audit.py) flags only handlers whose mounted path matches a known PHI marker (deny-list). A route at an unrecognized path (e.g. /api/encounters) is silently treated as non-PHI — fail-open, wrong default for a PHI surface.

Flip to fail-closed: every @router handler must EITHER inject+call AuditService OR appear in AUDIT_EXEMPT_PHI_ROUTES with a justification; a marker-matching path may never be exempted (backstop against a lazy exemption). Requires classifying the ~55 currently-non-auditing handlers into audit-vs-exempt — that pass becomes a documented PHI-classification inventory of the API surface.

Running the fail-closed lens already surfaces handlers that return PHI/identifiers but do not audit — decide per-route (add auditing or justify exemption):
- ical_sync.sync_ical_calendar — returns client_identifier + appointment start_at + ehr_appointment_url for unmatched events
- ehr_routes.ehr_navigate — ships the current EHR page DOM (renders charts) to an LLM
- chat.list_conversations — returns conversation titles (free-text the clinician typed)

Keep markers as a secondary backstop. The check already backs CI + pre-commit + the audit-coverage-check skill + a PostToolUse hook, so flipping the default propagates to all four.
notes: Implemented in PR #388 (branch PABLO-xo3-audit-fail-closed). Fail-closed flip + tenant-AuditService tightening + 3 PHI routes wired (chat list patient-scoped, ehr_navigate, ical sync) + 51-entry non-PHI exempt list w/ backstop. Local: engine clean, ruff+mypy pass, audit/chat/ehr/ical tests pass. Platform-audit coverage split out to PABLO-vol. Awaiting CI + merge.

title: Coalesce read-access audit writes within an active-record window
description:
A clinician working in one chart generates many reads -- opening a session, the frontend refetching on focus/navigation, etc. -- and each currently writes a separate *_viewed audit row + Cloud Logging mirror. Over a week of light single-user testing we already saw hundreds of patient_viewed/session_listed rows; this scales per active clinician and every row lands in the 6-year retention-locked sink. The signal we actually want is 'clinician accessed patient X during a work window,' not one row per HTTP GET.

Add a coalescing gate in AuditService for the read actions (patient_viewed, session_viewed, chat_conversation_viewed, patient_document_viewed). Use Redis (the same instance backing rate-limit/idle-session) as a dedup gate: key on (user_id, action, target_id) with a configurable TTL window (~10-15 min). On a cache miss, write the audit row as today and set the key; on a hit, skip the dual-write. Postgres stays the synchronous system-of-record -- Redis is ONLY a 'have we already recorded this access recently?' gate, never a buffer or store for the events themselves.

Critical: fail OPEN. If Redis is unavailable or errors, fall through and write the audit row. For audit the safe failure is an extra duplicate row, never a dropped access -- the opposite of idle_session's fail-closed posture. Make the window TTL a setting (default off / 0 = no coalescing, so self-hosters without Redis keep today's behavior unchanged). Consider NOT coalescing the restricted-category document views (psychotherapy_notes) so those keep full fidelity.
design:
## Implementation design — read-access audit coalescing

### Where it goes
All read audits funnel through `AuditService.log(...)` → `AuditService._persist(entry)`
in `backend/app/services/audit_service.py`. Add the gate as an early return at
the top of `_persist`. Reuse the existing Redis access pattern
(`from ..redis_client import get_redis_client`, gated by `settings.use_redis`),
same as `rate_limit.py` / `auth/idle_session.py`.

### Setting (settings.py)
    audit_read_coalesce_seconds: int = Field(
        default=0,  # 0 = off; self-hosters without Redis keep today's behavior
        description="Coalesce duplicate read-access audit events per (user, record) within this window.",
    )

### Code (audit_service.py)
    _COALESCED_READ_ACTIONS = frozenset({
        AuditAction.PATIENT_VIEWED,
        AuditAction.SESSION_VIEWED,
        AuditAction.CHAT_CONVERSATION_VIEWED,   # added in PABLO-m1y
        AuditAction.PATIENT_DOCUMENT_VIEWED,
        # NOT *_VIEWED_RESTRICTED — psychotherapy notes keep full fidelity
    })

    def _should_skip_duplicate(self, entry: AuditLogEntry) -> bool:
        """True if an identical read by this user was already recorded in the window.

        Fails OPEN: any Redis problem -> write the row. For audit the safe
        failure is a duplicate, never a dropped access (inverse of idle_session,
        which fails closed for security).
        """
        ttl = get_settings().audit_read_coalesce_seconds
        if ttl <= 0 or entry.action not in {a.value for a in _COALESCED_READ_ACTIONS}:
            return False
        try:
            redis = get_redis_client()
            if redis is None:
                return False
            key = f"audit:seen:{entry.user_id}:{entry.action}:{entry.resource_id}"
            first_time = redis.set(key, "1", nx=True, ex=ttl)  # True if set, None if key exists
            return first_time is None
        except Exception:
            logger.warning("Audit coalesce check failed; writing row (fail-open)", exc_info=True)
            return False

    def _persist(self, entry: AuditLogEntry) -> None:
        if self._should_skip_duplicate(entry):
            return
        # ... existing PHI-free assert + repo.append + Cloud Logging dual-write unchanged ...

### Why this shape
- `SET key 1 NX EX ttl` is atomic (no GET-then-SET race), cross-instance, TTL built in.
- FIXED window (key expires ttl after FIRST access, not extended on hits) -> records
  "accessed patient X" ~once per ttl of continuous work. Guarantees at least one durable
  access record per work window. Do NOT make it sliding (could suppress for hours).
- Per-(user, action, resource_id) key -> two different patients still log two rows; only
  repeats of the SAME record collapse.
- Postgres stays the synchronous system-of-record. Redis only decides WHETHER to write,
  never holds the event. (Redis-as-store would be a HIPAA durability gap — explicitly out.)
- Off by default; flip on via deploy env (audit_read_coalesce_seconds=900 ~ 15 min).

### Tests
1. Two patient_viewed for same (user, patient) within window -> 1 row; different patients -> 2 rows.
2. Redis raising -> every row still written (fail-open). Use a fake redis whose .set raises.
3. Restricted document view (PATIENT_DOCUMENT_VIEWED_RESTRICTED) -> never coalesced.
4. audit_read_coalesce_seconds=0 -> behaves exactly as today (no Redis calls).

### Sequencing
Best landed together with PABLO-m1y (which adds the CHAT_CONVERSATION_VIEWED action this set
references, and removes the noisy *_listed events). If fj1 ships first, drop
CHAT_CONVERSATION_VIEWED from the set until m1y lands.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated reads of the same record by the same user within the window produce one audit row; Redis outage falls back to writing every row (verified by test); restricted document views optionally exempt; coalescing is config-gated and off by default; per-record first-access still always recorded.

title: Rationalize read-access audit events: drop list-level, add chat conversation view
description:
Our read-access auditing is inconsistent and noisy. Two changes:

1. Stop emitting the list-level audit events. log_session_list / log_patient_list / log_appointment_list fire on every list load (sessions.py:365,422, patients.py:213, scheduling.py list path) and record only a count -- not which records were returned. The list endpoints are already access-filtered (list_by_user -> only the caller's own/granted patients via has_patient_access), so a list load surfaces nothing the caller isn't authorized to see, and the count tells a reviewer nothing useful. These (session_listed, patient_listed, appointment_listed) are by far the highest-volume audit rows and the lowest forensic value. Remove the call sites. Keep the per-record *_viewed events -- those are the audit-of-record for 'who opened this patient/session.' Leave the enum values defined so historical rows still deserialize, just stop writing them.

2. Add the missing conversation-detail audit. GET /api/chat/conversations/{id} (chat.py:353) returns full message bodies but logs nothing, while get_session/get_patient/document downloads all emit a *_VIEWED. Add a chat_conversation_viewed action and log it on the detail read so chat matches the other PHI-read surfaces. Do NOT add a list-level chat audit (same reasoning as #1).
acceptance_criteria: No session_listed/patient_listed/appointment_listed rows written on list loads; chat_conversation_viewed written on the conversation detail read; per-record *_viewed events unchanged; existing audit tests updated.
notes: Shipped with a refinement beyond the original scope: the two list endpoints that return full SOAP content (GET /api/sessions embeds the note via _embed_note; GET /api/patients/{id}/notes returns every note body) do NOT just drop their audit — they now emit a per-record session_viewed event for each record returned, so bulk content reads keep an audit-of-record. Only the genuinely content-free lists (sessions/today, appointments, patients) drop their count-only audit. Per-record volume is made affordable by the PABLO-fj1 coalescing gate. Guardrail allowlist (test_route_audit_guardrails) updated to exempt only today + appointments.

title: Frontend: per-item response anchors + DIRE entry form
description: The instrument entry form (frontend/src/lib/outcomeMeasures.ts InstrumentMeta + RecordOutcomeMeasureButton) uses ONE shared responseOptions scale across all items (fits PHQ-9/GAD-7's uniform 0-3). DIRE's seven factors each have DISTINCT 1-3 anchors, so DIRE can't render a usable form yet. Add optional per-item response options to InstrumentMeta (fallback to the shared scale when absent), thread through the form render, and add the DIRE meta with real per-factor anchors. DIRE backend already shipped (PR #383). Frontend gates: tsc --noEmit + eslint + vitest.

title: Engine: differentials, prescribing safeguards & medication rationale as definition data + clinician-reasoning capture
description: Extend the metadata-driven diagnostic engine (definitions are data) so a definition can optionally carry: differentials[] ({icd_code, mimics_how, distinguish_how, transcript_cues[], evidence_weights}); prescribing_safeguards[] (configurable-per-jurisdiction attestations — e.g. registry-check captured or its documented exception); and medication_rationale (first_line/alternatives/this_agent_now with citation refs). Add a per-tenant capture record for clinician medical-decision-making: what was considered, what was ruled out and how, alternatives tried/planned, informed consent, intended duration, titration, 'why this agent now', safeguard attestations, signature. title: Diagnostic engine — add 'checklist' evaluator_type + make meets_criteria nullable
description:
Add a no-verdict CHECKLIST strategy to the diagnostic engine, alongside the existing count-threshold 'criteria' strategy. The clinician marks which symptoms apply; the engine records them and offers a suggested code, but produces NO algorithmic 'meets criteria' determination. The clinician confirms the ICD-10-CM code. Rationale: dimensional/network literature (HiTOP, RDoC) — a categorical X-of-Y verdict is the wrong operationalization for these checklists.

Pure engine/schema work — NOT gated by clinical content sign-off (the engine ships with zero definitions today). Buildable independently.

Backend (pablo):
- definitions.py: add EVALUATOR_CHECKLIST = 'checklist'.
- evaluator.py: add _evaluate_checklist returning meets_criteria=None, unmet_reasons=(), and the definition's suggested_icd10 (always a suggestion, clinician confirms). Change DiagnosticOutcome.meets_criteria to bool | None.
- service.py: persist meets_criteria as None for checklists; stop coercing None->False on read (_build_response).
- schemas.py: DiagnosticAssessmentResponse.meets_criteria -> bool | None.
- db/models.py:360: diagnostic_assessments.meets_criteria -> nullable=True. Per-tenant Alembic migration (DROP NOT NULL) + tenant_template.sql regen.

Frontend (pablo):
- lib/diagnostics/evaluate.ts: branch on evaluator_type; checklist returns no verdict.
- RecordDiagnosisButton / determination panel: hide the 'Criteria met' UI for checklist definitions.
- types/diagnoses.ts: meetsCriteria -> nullable.

Tests: backend pytest for _evaluate_checklist (no verdict, suggestion passthrough) + migration up/down/up; frontend vitest for the evaluate mirror + UI branch.

Prereq for the SaaS-managed MDD/GAD content seed (tracked separately).
notes: Implemented + in review: pablo PR #384 (branch feat/diagnostic-checklist-evaluator). Backend: EVALUATOR_CHECKLIST + _evaluate_checklist (NO verdict, NO suggested code); meets_criteria bool|None end-to-end; per-tenant migration c4e8d1f6a2b9 (DROP NOT NULL, downgrade backfills) + tenant_template regen; repo write/read preserve NULL. Frontend: evaluate.ts branch, determination panel hidden + list badge dropped for checklist, code picker shows nothing pre-selected (Save gated on explicit clinician code choice). DESIGN DECISION (confirmed w/ user 2026-06-03): a checklist makes no determination AND suggests no code — checklist responses don't determine the ICD-10-CM specifier (F32 vs F33, severity), so the clinician picks from the definition's icd10_options. => CONTENT SEED (THERAPY-ixvv): populate icd10_options with the valid specifier codes per disorder; a checklist definition's suggested_icd10 is ignored for selection. Tests: evaluator unit, service None-round-trip, migration up/down/up integration, frontend evaluate+UI. All gates green. Aligns with FR-2 + CR-2 in pablo-saas docs/requirements/prescription-justification.md.

Dev now runs the full checklist-evaluator change. Prod not promoted (dev-only ship).

title: Diagnostic engine — bundle ICD-10-CM catalog (F-chapter + Z55–Z65) as data + loader

Replace the 3-code baseline ICD-10-CM seed with a real bundled catalog so the diagnostic-engine code-search/determination UI (6xj.2) has codes to pick from.

title: Diagnostic engine — frontend criterion form + determination
description: Phase 2. Criterion checklist form (group headings, met/not-met per criterion, gate attestations) with a live determination panel ('Criteria met — F32.9' / 'group A needs >=5, 3 selected'). A Diagnoses surface on the patient chart listing current determinations with codes. Mirrors the outcome-measures tab/dialog idioms. Depends on the backend phase.
design:
Role-aware PROMINENCE, not role-gating (SaaS onboarding captures therapist / PMHNP / both).

- Diagnoses tab is shown to ALL clinical roles — it's billing infrastructure: any therapist who bills insurance or writes a superbill needs an ICD-10-CM code (F-code dx + Z-code psychosocial context). Diagnosing is in scope for independently-licensed therapists (LCSW/LMFT/LPC/psychologist); the therapist vs PMHNP line is about MEDICATION/prescribing, not diagnosis.
- Role tunes default prominence, not availability:
  - PMHNP / 'both' -> full criterion-checklist flow surfaced by default (medical-model documentation / medical-necessity).
  - therapist -> lighter 'select diagnosis + confirm ICD-10 code' path by default; full criteria flow available but not front-and-center.
- Prescriber-specific surfaces (medication, AI-drafting wedge THERAPY-5lcy) are what genuinely key off the role flag; diagnosis does not.
- Role signal lives in SaaS; OSS frontend must read it neutrally (a generic capability/role prop), no SaaS framing. Default (no role known) = show the tab with the lighter path.

CLINICAL CONFIRM (clinical lead): verify counselor/LPC diagnosis scope doesn't need state-by-state caveats in copy before shipping role-tuned defaults.
notes: OSS PR #381. Diagnoses tab + record dialog + client evaluator mirror; role-aware prominence prop (lite default). Awaiting CI + merge.

title: Diagnostic engine — backend (table, evaluator, API)
description: Phase 1 backend. Platform tables icd10_codes + diagnostic_definitions (shared schema) with an MDD seed (self-authored labels, F32/F33 codes). Per-tenant diagnostic_assessments table + migration. Single evaluate(definition, responses) -> {meets_criteria, unmet_reasons, suggested_icd10} dispatching on evaluator_type; implement the 'criteria' strategy (per-group min_met + require_cardinal + all gates true). Pydantic schemas + service + repository + router (POST/GET list/GET/DELETE soft-delete), mirroring outcome_measures. determined_icd10 validated against icd10_codes catalog at write. Tests: evaluator (threshold/cardinal/gate/unmet-reasons) + round-trip. Run rls-coverage-check for the new patient_id table.

Three-table design (platform icd10_codes + diagnostic_definitions; per-tenant diagnostic_assessments), single metadata-driven evaluator (criteria strategy), self-authored MDD+GAD baseline, public-domain ICD-10-CM, clinician-confirmed code. ruff+mypy clean, full unit suite green (1506), unit+route+real-PG RLS/seed integration tests. Awaiting review.

title: Diagnostic-criteria assessment engine
description:
Structured diagnostic-assessment capability, distinct from outcome_measures (continuous symptom scores). Metadata-driven: a single evaluate() entry point dispatches on an evaluator_type to a closed set of code strategies (criteria | sum_scale | risk_stratifier); 6xj uses 'criteria'. Definitions are DATA, not per-disorder code.

Three-table design:
- PLATFORM (shared schema): icd10_codes (public-domain ICD-10-CM catalog: code, description, billable) + diagnostic_definitions (code, version, display_name, evaluator_type, params jsonb {groups, gates, icd10_options}, active). One global copy.
- PER-TENANT (practice_{id}): diagnostic_assessments — patient_id, definition_code+version (snapshot), criterion_responses jsonb, gate_responses jsonb, meets_criteria, determined_icd10 (clinician-confirmed, validated vs catalog), diagnosis_label snapshot, criterion_citations jsonb (AI-assist), source, confirmed_at, assessed_at, audit, soft-delete.

Content posture: criterion text is SELF-AUTHORED from clinical facts (clinical-reviewer sign-off; NO DSM-5 or ICD-11 text). Codes copied from public-domain ICD-10-CM. Determination is clinician-confirmed (no algorithmic ICD-11->ICD-10-CM crosswalk). Design: docs/architecture/diagnostic-criteria-engine.md

title: Manual outcome-measure entry — API + chart UI (first writer)
description:
First WRITER to the outcome_measures store (PABLO-o5k): a clinician records a standardized instrument score (PHQ-9, GAD-7, or a generic instrument) directly from the patient chart — entering per-item responses (auto-totaled) or a known total, with the date administered and capture source = 'manual'.

Scope: write/read API + a thin entry form + display on the chart trend alongside vitals/notes.

Why first: smallest possible producer. It lets the chart store and trend scores immediately, independent of richer capture methods (OCR/Form-Parser extraction, patient-completion portal) which layer on later as additional writers to the same table. Closes the loop so downstream chart/trend features have real data to read.

Per-item, not just totals (item-level scores carry clinical meaning). Records capture source on every row for provenance.

Depends on PABLO-o5k (the destination table) landing first.

Measures tab on patient chart: PHQ-9/GAD-7 entry (per-item 0-3 or known total), inline SVG trend + server severity, non-blocking item-9 safety callout. Backend (PABLO-o5k/#374) owns scoring. Awaiting review/merge. tsc+eslint+vitest(880) green.

title: Deterministic grounding guard for imported notes + per-field 'from source' badge
description: Verify the parse didn't paraphrase or fabricate by checking, with plain string/token matching (no extra LLM call), whether each parsed field's text is grounded in the source document. A field is grounded when its text is a whitespace-normalized substring of the source, or its word-token overlap with the source is above a high threshold; anything below is flagged. The source is already persisted as the session transcript, so grounding can be recomputed at review time from (note content + transcript) without storing extra state or a migration. Backend: a pure check_grounding(content, source) helper, attached to the parse result and logged (field PATHS only, never content — no PHI in logs) when fields aren't grounded. Frontend (with the split-pane review, depends on PABLO-yxu.5): a per-field badge — 'from your note' when grounded, 'review — not found verbatim' when not. Complements the verbatim prompt: the prompt makes the parse faithful, this proves each field is, and the clinician reviews what isn't.

title: Emit content-free OpenInference retrieval spans for chat context assembly
description:
Chat LLM calls already emit content-free OpenInference LLM spans (services/llm_telemetry.py::llm_span), but the context-assembly step that runs just before each turn — assemble_context_bundle in chat_turn_service — is invisible to tracing. There's no way to see, in an OTLP backend, which chart sources were retrieved for a turn or how much context was assembled.

Add a content-free retrieval span (RETRIEVER kind) emitted around assemble_context_bundle in the chat turn service. Following the content-free-by-construction design of llm_span, it records metadata only: the retrieved source/document ids, per-source row and token-estimate counts, and the total assembled token estimate. No field accepts retrieved text, so the span cannot leak chart content into telemetry.

This makes retrieval coverage queryable alongside the existing LLM spans and lets retrieval quality be evaluated by document id. Populate it from the bundle manifest (source keys, note/document ids, counts), so no change to the bundle's content model is required.

Out of scope: capturing the retrieved document text itself — content capture is a separate, deliberately gated concern, kept out of the content-free telemetry path.
notes: PR #346 opened. Delivered more than the content-free span: (1) retrieval_span() in llm_telemetry (content-free RETRIEVER span, no-text-by-construction like llm_span); (2) ContextBundle.documents — structured per-item breakdown (id + rendered text per surviving note/doc/pasted block, post-budget, never on the manifest); (3) turn service opens the retrieval span around assemble_context_bundle + calls a no-op _record_turn_content hook on success with the composed prompt/documents/prior turns/reply — the faithful instrumentation seam (an overlay subclass overrides it instead of wrapping the gateway / splitting the prompt). BatchSpanProcessor keeps export off the request path (cold-start safe). make lint (ruff+mypy) clean, 121 tests pass.

title: Refactor auth token verification to Chain of Responsibility — eliminate unverified JWT peek
description:
## Why this issue exists

The current multi-issuer JWT verification flow has a structural flaw: it peeks at the token's `iss` claim *without* verifying the signature (`jwt.decode(token, options={"verify_signature": False})`) to route to the right verifier, then the selected verifier re-checks the signature downstream. This is safe (the second verify is the real one), but it is architecturally wrong — a nosemgrep annotation suppresses the Semgrep rule that correctly flags it, and future devs have to understand a two-step trust model that shouldn't exist. Raised as PABLO-001 in the 2026-05-31 pentest report.

## Current code structure

File: `backend/app/auth/service.py`

```
_unverified_issuer(token) -> str | None
    jwt.decode(token, verify_signature=False)  # ← the problem
    returns iss claim for routing only

_get_verifier_registry() -> VerifierRegistry   # lru_cached
    builds from settings:
      VerifierRegistry(firebase=FirebaseVerifier(), oidc=OidcVerifier(...) if oidc_issuer else None)

verify_token(token) -> VerifiedIdentity
    issuer = _unverified_issuer(token)
    verifier = _get_verifier_registry().get_verifier(issuer)
    return verifier.verify(token)
```

File: `backend/app/auth/providers.py` — `VerifierRegistry` class

```python
class VerifierRegistry:
    def __init__(self, firebase: FirebaseVerifier, oidc: OidcVerifier | None) -> None:
        self._firebase = firebase
        self._by_issuer: dict[str, TokenVerifier] = {}
        if oidc is not None:
            self._by_issuer[oidc.issuer] = oidc

    def get_verifier(self, issuer: str | None) -> TokenVerifier:
        # OIDC if issuer matches, else Firebase catch-all
        if issuer is not None and issuer in self._by_issuer:
            return self._by_issuer[issuer]
        return self._firebase
```

`FirebaseVerifier` and `OidcVerifier` both implement `TokenVerifier` protocol: `verify(token: str) -> VerifiedIdentity`. They raise `HTTPException(401, ...)` on failure with specific error codes: `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `TOKEN_REVOKED`, `USER_DISABLED`, `INVALID_TOKEN`.

## What to build — Chain of Responsibility

The registry's `verify()` method should try each verifier in order and return on first success. No pre-peek. No routing step outside the registry.

```python
# On VerifierRegistry:
def verify(self, token: str) -> VerifiedIdentity:
    first_exc: HTTPException | None = None
    for verifier in self._verifiers:  # ordered list: [firebase, oidc] if oidc configured
        try:
            return verifier.verify(token)
        except HTTPException as e:
            if e.status_code != 401:
                raise  # unexpected — propagate immediately
            if first_exc is None:
                first_exc = e  # preserve the first (most specific) error
    raise first_exc or HTTPException(status_code=401)
```

**Why first error, not last:** Firebase is first and handles >99% of tokens. Its error codes (TOKEN_EXPIRED, TOKEN_REVOKED) are what clients act on for re-auth logic. If we returned the last error, an expired Firebase token would fall through to OIDC (which rejects it as INVALID_TOKEN) and the client would get the wrong signal. OIDC in this system is only the pentest runner — its error quality does not matter.

**Performance:** Firebase fails fast on non-Firebase tokens at the `kid` lookup in its cached JWKS — no RSA operation occurs. The overhead for the OIDC path (Firebase fast-fail + OIDC verify) is a dict lookup, not a network call.

## What to delete / change

1. **Delete** `_unverified_issuer()` from `service.py` entirely — no longer needed.
2. **Delete** `get_verifier()` from `VerifierRegistry` — replaced by `verify()`.
3. **Add** `verify()` method to `VerifierRegistry` (see above).
4. **Change** `VerifierRegistry.__init__` to store `self._verifiers: list[TokenVerifier]` (ordered: firebase first, oidc appended if configured) instead of the `_by_issuer` dict + `_firebase` catch-all.
5. **Simplify** `verify_token()` in `service.py` to: `return _get_verifier_registry().verify(token)`
6. **Remove** the `# nosemgrep: python.jwt.security.unverified-jwt-decode` annotation from `service.py:236` — the offending line is gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- `verify_token()` in `service.py` has no `jwt.decode` call with `verify_signature=False`
- `_unverified_issuer()` is deleted
- `# nosemgrep` annotation on the old line is gone
- `VerifierRegistry.verify()` exists; `get_verifier()` is removed
- Expired/revoked Firebase token still returns `TOKEN_EXPIRED` / `TOKEN_REVOKED` (not OIDC's generic error)
- `make check` passes (ruff + mypy + pytest)
- Running semgrep locally produces 0 hits on `python.jwt.security.unverified-jwt-decode`

title: frontend(auth): wait for authStateReady before reading currentUser in apiClient
description:
Some authenticated requests go out with no Authorization header right after a sign-in transition (notably multiFactor.enroll() during the onboarding MFA step), because getAuthHeader reads getFirebaseAuth().currentUser synchronously while the SDK is briefly between users.

Decoding Playwright traces of a fresh-user onboarding run shows the post-MFA token re-issue lands correctly (next request has firebase.sign_in_second_factor='totp'), but the request that fires in the next tick after the enrollment frame closes — recordCompanionAction's POST /api/saas/users/me/companion, or the frontend's fe-error reporter — goes out with no Authorization header at all. Backend correctly 401s and the user sees a 'Couldn't save that' toast with no clear remediation.

#300's TOKEN_REFRESH_RETRY_CODES retry doesn't recover this case: there's no token to refresh, the if (currentUser) branch in getAuthHeader is simply skipped, and the retry hits the same null window.

Fix: in getAuthHeader, await getFirebaseAuth().authStateReady() before reading currentUser. authStateReady resolves the first time Firebase's auth state listener fires and is a no-op thereafter, so the cost is one microtask in steady state and the right amount of wait during the post-enrollment transition. Same edit applies to the SSE consumer that shares the helper.

Surfaced by chart-render-smoke.spec.ts via the onboardedUser fixture (browser.newContext() exposes the race more reliably than the test's default context). Repros consistently across two full dev e2e runs.
notes: PR #307 (https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/307). One-helper change in frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts: await getFirebaseAuth().authStateReady() before reading currentUser, so requests fired during the multiFactor.enroll() transition wait for the new currentUser to install instead of going out with no Authorization header. SSE consumer (lib/chat/sse.ts) inherits the fix via shared getAuthHeader. eslint + tsc clean locally. Keep open until merged + bumped into pablo-saas via BASE_IMAGE.txt.

title: Validate audio magic bytes at /upload-audio boundary (reject non-audio synchronously)
description:
POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/upload-audio gates uploads on the client-declared Content-Type only (_ALLOWED_AUDIO_TYPES in app/routes/sessions.py). It never inspects the bytes, so a client can send arbitrary content labeled 'audio/wav' and pass the gate. The malformed payload then fails downstream in the async transcription worker (the RIFF sniff + wave.open in app/services/assemblyai_transcription_service.py), surfacing as a FAILED session via the polling task rather than a synchronous 4xx — an orphaned session the user only sees minutes later.

Add a lightweight magic-byte/header sniff at the upload boundary so non-audio is rejected synchronously:
  - WAV: 'RIFF'....'WAVE'
  - MP3: ID3 tag or 0xFFE* MPEG frame sync
  - OGG: 'OggS'
  - FLAC: 'fLaC'
  - MP4/M4A: 'ftyp' box at offset 4
  - WebM: EBML header 0x1A45DFA3

Keep the Content-Type allowlist as a cheap first pass; make the byte sniff the authoritative check. Reject mismatches with 415 (or 422). Apply to both audio parts. Add a unit test that a non-audio payload mislabeled as audio/* is rejected at the boundary, not enqueued.

title: Simplify chat source selection — drop unavailable sources, fix 'Selected sessions', add document picker
description:
## Problem

The chat source-chip rail (frontend/src/components/chat/SourceChipRail.tsx + sourceMeta.ts) exposes 10 sources, but most aren't usable today, so the UI reads as complex while doing little:

- **'Selected sessions' (progress_notes_explicit) is broken.** Toggling the chip sets the key to boolean `true` (ChatPanel.handleAddSource/handleToggleSource), but the backend loader requires `{note_ids:[...]}` (backend/app/services/chat_context_bundler.py:441) and raises InvalidSelectionError otherwise. There is no session-picker UI to supply note_ids. Net: selecting it does nothing useful or errors the turn. This is the user-reported "doesn't appear to do anything."
- **'Uploaded documents' (patient_documents) is all-or-nothing.** Toggling includes EVERY uploaded document. The backend already supports an explicit `ids` list (_load_patient_documents falls back to all-for-patient only when no ids given, chat_context_bundler.py:~569), but there's no UI to pick which documents.
- **Always-empty sources clutter the rail.** most_recent_intake, treatment_plan_active, safety_plan_active, current_medications reference note types (intake/treatment_plan/safety_plan/medications) not registered in the OSS note-type registry — only soap + narrative ship today (see comment chat_context_bundler.py:25-31). They always return row_count=0 / reason=no_data. lab_values_recent + vitals_recent have no data path in a therapy product.
- The "+ Add source" menu only hides sources flagged `module_not_available` in the latest manifest, and only AFTER the first turn — so on a fresh chat all 10 show.

## Asks

1. **Surface only sources with a working data path** in the chip rail + add-source menu: progress_notes_recent, patient_documents, pasted_text. Keep the backend loaders for the not-yet-registered note types (they're forward-compatible) but don't show chips for them until their note types actually ship.
2. **Remove the 'Selected sessions' chip** (progress_notes_explicit) for now — it's broken without a picker. If per-session selection is wanted later, file a follow-up to build a note-multiselect that supplies `note_ids` in the correct shape.
3. **Add a per-document picker** for patient_documents so the clinician can choose which uploaded documents to include (backend already supports the `ids` shape). Ties into the patient-documents UI work in this epic (PABLO-6x5.5).
4. Result: a short, honest source rail where every visible source works.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Source rail + add menu show only sources with a real data path (no always-empty chips on a fresh chat)
- [ ] No visible source can produce an InvalidSelectionError from a boolean-vs-shape mismatch
- [ ] 'Selected sessions' removed (or a working picker added)
- [ ] Uploaded documents can be included selectively, not only all-or-nothing
close_reason: Chat source rail gated to live-data sources (SUPPORTED_SOURCE_KEYS); Selected-sessions removed; pasted_text seeds {content} editor; patient_documents gets all-or-pick document picker; OSS default trimmed. Closing with the PR.

title: Patient search: clarify field + add substring match + expose first-name search
description:
## Problem

Three related UX gaps in the patient list search input (\`PatientTable.tsx:139\`):

1. **No indication search is last-name**. Placeholder says \"Search patients by name...\". The backend defaults \`search_by=last_name\` (\`backend/app/routes/patients.py:160\`), so typing a first name returns nothing — silently. Users assume their patient was deleted or the list is broken.

2. **Prefix-only matching**. The repo uses \`first_name_lower.startswith(search_lower)\` / \`last_name_lower.startswith(search_lower)\` (\`backend/app/repositories/patient.py:206-208\`). \"smith\" matches Smith; \"mith\" does not. Most users expect substring search (\"contains\"), especially when they remember the middle of a hyphenated last name or only a fragment.

3. **\`search_by\` query param is exposed in the API but never in the UI**. The route accepts \`search_by=first_name|last_name\` but \`usePatientList\` callers never pass it. There's no toggle, no dropdown, no smart heuristic (\"if input has a comma, split into last, first\").

## Options

**Minimum viable improvement:**
- Update placeholder to \`\"Search by last name...\"\` so the contract is honest
- Add a small \"First name\" toggle next to the search input

**Better:**
- Change \`startswith\` to \`contains\` (i.e., \`%search%\`) — substring match in both fields by default, no toggle needed. Repo + tests change in one place. Trade-off: substring on a large patient list is slower than prefix, but with the ILIKE pattern and lower-cased indexed columns it's fine through low-thousands rows.
- Drop the \`search_by\` param entirely; always search both fields.

**Best:**
- Substring search across \`first_name || ' ' || last_name\` so \"john smi\" works
- Optional: weight last-name matches higher in ranking
- Keep input copy as \"Search patients...\"

## Recommendation

Go directly to \"Better\" — substring search both fields, drop \`search_by\` toggle. It's the smallest change that produces the least surprising behavior. \"Best\" can follow if users still complain about full-name search.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Typing a middle fragment of a last name finds the patient (substring match)
- [ ] Typing a first name finds the patient (without any toggle)
- [ ] Placeholder text either matches actual behavior or behavior is broadened to match the generic placeholder
- [ ] Repo + route tests updated
close_reason: Patient list: page_size=100 + 'Showing N of M' total (y93); substring search across both names, search_by toggle dropped, generic placeholder (bgr). Closing with the PR.

title: Auto-derive Document AI project + processor at startup
description:
## Problem

The Document AI OCR client (\`backend/app/services/document_ai_ocr.py\`) gates on three env vars: \`DOCUMENT_AI_PROJECT_ID\`, \`DOCUMENT_AI_PROCESSOR_ID\`, \`DOCUMENT_AI_LOCATION\`. If any are unset, \`is_configured\` returns False, OCR silently falls back to \"unavailable\", and finalized scanned PDFs show \"OCR not yet supported — text extraction failed\" in the UI.

This is exactly how the feature broke when the OCR processors were provisioned in pablohealth-dev and pablohealth-prod on 2026-05-24 — the processors exist, the IAM role is granted (in dev), but no one wired the env vars into Cloud Run. The deploy isn't atomic, so we shipped a half-configured feature.

## Why most of this is redundant

1. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_PROJECT_ID\`** is always the same as the running GCP project. Cloud Run already injects \`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT\` automatically (also \`GCP_PROJECT_ID\` in our config). \`google.auth.default()\` returns the project too. Asking operators to set this third copy is pure ceremony.

2. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_PROCESSOR_ID\`** is less trivially redundant — a project can hold many processors (OCR, Form Parser, Handwriting, etc.) — but in practice we always want \"the processor whose displayName is \`pablo-patient-doc-ocr\`\". That's discoverable at startup via \`processors.list\` with a name filter, cached for the lifetime of the process.

3. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_LOCATION\`** can default to \"us\" (where our processors live) and only be overridden if we ever need EU.

## Proposed change

In \`DocumentAiOcrClient\`:
- If \`document_ai_project_id\` is None, fall back to \`os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT\")\` then \`google.auth.default()[1]\`.
- If \`document_ai_processor_id\` is None, on first call run \`processors.list(parent=...)\` filtered by displayName (constant \`PABLO_OCR_PROCESSOR_NAME = \"pablo-patient-doc-ocr\"\`); cache the resolved id on the instance.
- Log once at startup with the resolved values so it's obvious in logs which processor is being used.
- Keep the env vars as escape hatches for tests and local overrides.

Outcome: zero-config OCR in any environment where a processor exists with the canonical name. Provisioning becomes \"create the processor + grant the IAM role\" — no Cloud Run env-var update step.

## Acceptance

- [ ] OCR works in pablohealth-dev with no DOCUMENT_AI_* env vars set
- [ ] Tests still pass with explicit env vars (escape hatch preserved)
- [ ] Startup log shows the resolved project + processor id once
- [ ] Doc string on \`DocumentAiOcrClient\` updated to describe the resolution order
design:
CONTEXT (code-verified against main, 2026-08-17):

`DocumentAiOcrClient.is_configured` (backend/app/services/document_ai_ocr.py:81-86)
is true only when `allow_document_ai_ocr` AND `document_ai_project_id` AND
`document_ai_processor_id` are all set. When it is false, `process` returns
early (:90) and a finalized scanned PDF renders "OCR not yet supported — text
extraction failed" in the UI. There is no signal anywhere that the feature is
merely unconfigured rather than genuinely unable to read the document.

Current settings (backend/app/settings.py:764-786):
  document_ai_project_id   : str | None = None
  document_ai_location     : str        = "us"     <- already defaulted
  document_ai_processor_id : str | None = None
  allow_document_ai_ocr    : bool       = True

Two of the three required values are redundant in practice:

  * project id is always the running GCP project. The runtime already receives
    it, and `google.auth.default()` returns it as its second element. A third
    hand-maintained copy is ceremony that can only ever be wrong.
  * processor id varies in principle (a project can hold OCR, Form Parser and
    handwriting processors) but in practice we always want the one whose
    displayName is `pablo-patient-doc-ocr`. That is discoverable at run time.

Location already defaults to "us" and needs no change.

SCOPE: derive what can be derived; keep every env var working as an override.

  1. PROJECT — when `document_ai_project_id` is None, resolve in order:
     `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` from the environment, then the project returned by
     `google.auth.default()`. First hit wins.
  2. PROCESSOR — when `document_ai_processor_id` is None, list processors under
     `projects/{project}/locations/{location}` and select the one whose
     displayName equals the module constant
     `PABLO_OCR_PROCESSOR_NAME = "pablo-patient-doc-ocr"`. Resolve LAZILY on
     first use, not at import: import-time network calls render the module
     unimportable in tests and in any environment without credentials.
  3. CACHE the resolved project and processor on the instance for the process
     lifetime. Do not re-list per document — `processors.list` is a network
     call and OCR runs per upload.
  4. LOG ONCE, at the point of resolution, at INFO: which project, location and
     processor id were resolved and whether each came from config or discovery.
     This is the diagnostic that was missing when the feature shipped
     half-configured. Project ids, locations and processor ids are
     infrastructure identifiers, not patient data — but log NOTHING about the
     document being processed on this path.
  5. FAILURE IS EXPLICIT AND SEPARATE FROM "OFF". Discovery that finds no
     matching processor, or cannot reach the API, must produce a distinct
     logged reason naming the displayName it looked for and the parent it
     looked under. It must NOT raise into the request path — the existing
     graceful degradation stands — and it must not retry discovery on every
     subsequent document once it has definitively failed.

`is_configured` becomes a weaker precondition: with discovery in place it can
no longer require `document_ai_processor_id` to be pre-set. Keep
`allow_document_ai_ocr` as the hard kill-switch — that one is deliberate
operator intent and must keep short-circuiting before any network call.

OUT OF SCOPE: Form Parser support (PABLO-1oi), handwriting processors
(PABLO-tz6), the async pipeline for large documents (PABLO-q3d), and any
change to what the UI renders when OCR is unavailable.

FILES: backend/app/services/document_ai_ocr.py, backend/app/settings.py
(description text only, if the fields' docs need to say "optional; derived when
unset"), backend/tests/test_document_ai_ocr.py.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With document_ai_project_id unset and GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set, the      
client resolves the project from the environment. A test asserts the        
resolved value.                                                             
2. With both unset, the client falls back to the project from google.auth.  
default(). A test asserts this with the auth call faked.                    
3. With document_ai_processor_id unset, the client lists processors and     
selects the one whose displayName is 'pablo-patient-doc-ocr'. A test with a 
faked list response containing several processors asserts the correct id is 
chosen.                                                                     
4. An explicitly-set document_ai_project_id or document_ai_processor_id     
always wins over discovery, and when both are set NO discovery call is made 
at all. A test asserts the list API is never invoked in that case.          
5. Discovery happens at most once per client instance: a test processing two
documents asserts exactly one processors.list call.                         
6. Discovery is lazy — importing the module and constructing the client make
no network call. A test asserts this.                                       
7. When no processor matches the expected displayName, process() degrades   
exactly as it does today (no raise into the request path) and logs a reason 
naming both the displayName sought and the parent searched. A test asserts  
the graceful return and that a second document does not re-attempt discovery.
8. allow_document_ai_ocr=False short-circuits before any discovery or       
network call. A test asserts no auth and no list call occur.                
9. Resolution is logged once at INFO with project, location, processor id,  
and whether each was configured or discovered. No document content, filename,
or patient identifier appears on this path.                                 
10. 'make check' passes — lint, mypy and the test suite together, not a     
subset.

title: [epic] Patient document import — capability expansion
description:
Parent epic for OSS-side enhancements to the Document AI OCR fallback (commit 5ba5d1b). Groups capability work across four themes:

A. Structured field extraction (Form Parser):
   - PABLO-1oi Form Parser invocation in DocumentAiOcrClient
   - PABLO-g50 FormField → outcome-measure schema mapping helpers
   - PABLO-o5k outcome_measures destination table

B. Processor variety:
   - PABLO-tz6 Handwriting OCR processor support

C. Upload UX:
   - PABLO-e6c Bulk upload UI for multi-file intake batches
   - PABLO-dvv Document-type tagging at upload time
   - PABLO-t7c Auto-categorize uploaded documents by content

D. Scale:
   - PABLO-q3d Async OCR pipeline for documents > 30 pages

Each child bead describes a generic capability. Processor IDs, field-to-schema mappings, and deployment-specific configuration are intentionally outside the engine — each deployment provides its own.

title: Async OCR pipeline for documents > 30 pages
description: Document AI's synchronous OCR endpoint has a 30-page limit. Documents exceeding it currently fail extraction. Add an async batch-processing path: queue the document, kick off Document AI batch operation, poll for completion, store the result. Long-document upload UX shows a 'processing' state until the async job completes.

title: Handwriting OCR processor support
description:
Document AI exposes a handwriting-optimized OCR processor distinct from the default text processor. Add it as a selectable processor type in DocumentAiOcrClient. Default OCR processor produces poor results on handwritten notes; FQHCs and any practice receiving paper intakes need the handwriting variant.

Capability only — processor ID selection is configurable per-deployment.

title: FormField → outcome-measure schema mapping helpers
description:
Generic helper that maps Document AI FormField key/value entries into structured outcome-measure rows. The mapper itself is content-agnostic — it takes a schema definition (field labels, value parsers, score aggregation rules) and FormField entries, and returns parsed records.

Schema definitions are supplied per-deployment.

title: outcome_measures destination table
description: New OSS clinical-chart table for storing scored instruments (PHQ-9 total + per-item, GAD-7 total + per-item, generic instrument rows). Joined to patient_id + appointment_id, displayed in chart UI alongside vitals/notes. Lives in OSS because the score data belongs in the chart regardless of where the underlying form came from (manual entry, OCR extraction, patient portal).
notes:
SINGLE canonical store for scored instruments. All capture paths — manual entry, OCR/Form-Parser extraction, patient-completion portal — are pluggable WRITERS to this one table; do NOT mint per-feature score tables. Each row records its capture source for provenance + chart-trend display. First writer to land is manual entry (PABLO-i4 below). (annotated 2026-06-02)
(correction: first writer bead is PABLO-cwj)

comments.author: Kurt Niemi
comments.text: Store + read/write API done; PR #374 open (pablo-health/pablo). Includes the manual-entry write API (source='manual'), instrument registry (PHQ-9/GAD-7), real-Postgres isolation test, and a self-healing RLS-coverage guard. Frontend entry form + chart trend display remain in PABLO-cwj.

title: Form Parser invocation in DocumentAiOcrClient
description:
Extend DocumentAiOcrClient to call Document AI Form Parser processors (structured field extraction) in addition to the existing OCR processor. Form Parser returns FormField entries (key/value pairs) instead of plain text — needs a different response-shape handler but shares ~95% of the existing client code (auth, project/location resolution, retry, error handling).

Generic capability — processor ID and field schemas are configured per-deployment.

title: EOB upload: OCR a paper explanation of benefits into a draft remittance posting
description: Payers that are not enrolled for electronic remittance mail a paper EOB. Let the practice upload it, run it through the document pipeline's OCR, and turn it into a draft posting the clinician confirms, the same posting path electronic remittances use.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.
- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

- Reuse the patient-document upload + OCR pipeline (backend/app/models/patient_document.py and its service) with a new document kind 'eob'.
- backend/app/claims/eob.py: deterministic extraction (regex/table heuristics over the OCR text) for claim/control number, service date, billed, allowed, paid, patient responsibility, adjustment codes; produce a RemittanceDraft that the remittance bead's post_lines can consume once confirmed. Confidence per field; anything below threshold is left blank for the clinician.
- UI: "Upload EOB" on the claim detail; a review form pre-filled from the draft; "Post" calls the existing posting path with source='eob'.

DECISIONS CLOSED: nothing posts without confirmation; no language model in this bead; unreadable EOBs produce an empty draft, not an error.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Three sample EOB PDFs (committed, synthetic) produce drafts with the expected fields; a blank page produces an empty draft.
2. Posting requires the confirm action; the resulting postings are indistinguishable from an electronic remittance except source='eob'.
3. make check green.

title: audit_logs.actor_type has no CHECK constraint, so a near-miss value silently takes the clinician arm
description:
`audit_logs` carries exactly one constraint — the primary key. `actor_type` is `varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'clinician'` with nothing pinning it to the ACTOR_TYPES vocabulary defined in app/models/audit.py (clinician, patient, anonymous, system, platform_staff).

The RLS policy hard-codes the literal 'patient':

    (actor_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'patient' AND user_id::text = current_setting('app.current_user_id', true))
    OR (actor_type = 'patient' AND user_id::text = current_setting('app.current_patient_id', true))

So only the exact string takes the patient arm. Confirmed: under a patient GUC, 'Patient', 'PATIENT', ' patient', 'patient ' and 'patient_proxy' are all RLS-refused, because they fall into the clinician arm and no clinician GUC is armed.

Fail-closed today, which is the right direction. But it means a future actor kind that is a patient in spirit — a guardian or proxy principal, say — would silently be refused at INSERT rather than recorded: exactly the § 164.312(b) failure #837 existed to eliminate (the action happens, nothing records it), reintroduced through the vocabulary rather than through the policy.
design:
Check the pablo-saas overlay BEFORE writing the constraint. SaaSAuditAction defines COMPANION_* codes documented as actor_type='patient', and overlays are explicitly allowed to name their own actor components. If the overlay also defines its own actor_TYPES, a CHECK pinned to the OSS tuple would break it — that is the whole reason actor_component was left unconstrained free text.

If the overlay needs its own kinds, the options are a CHECK built from a shared constant the overlay can extend, or leaving actor_type free and instead making the policy's patient arm robust (e.g. comparing against a normalised value). Do not pin the vocabulary without checking, or this trades a quiet refusal for a broken overlay.

Related and probably the same fix: arm_current_patient_id validates non-empty but never normalises case, and user_id is varchar so the policy compares byte-exact while the patient_id uuid column canonicalises. The same patient can therefore hold two distinct actor identities depending on the case of the string a resolver hands it. Fail-safe on access, fail-open on accountability.
acceptance_criteria:
- actor_type is constrained to the known vocabulary at the database level, so a typo or unknown kind fails loudly at INSERT instead of silently landing in the clinician arm.
- The constraint ships in the same commit as its migration AND a regenerated tenant_template.sql (guardrail 4).
- Existing rows across all tenants satisfy it, or the migration is explicit about what it does with ones that don't.
- A test asserts an unknown actor_type is rejected, and that all five known kinds still write.
notes: Found while adversarially reviewing #837 (see #840, #841). Lower priority than PABLO-s7qq: current behaviour is fail-closed, so this is about a future actor kind rather than a present defect. The empty-user_id sibling of this problem is already fixed in #840 via CHECK (user_id <> '').

title: Hand-written to_dict/from_dict drift from their dataclasses; delete the dict layer and guard it
description:
Found while landing PABLO-e3a.6 (pablo#791).

#771 added `actor_type` to `AuditLogEntry`. Four sites consume that record's
fields. The two that DERIVE them picked the new field up for free; the two that
hand-list them silently dropped it:

| site | style | picked it up |
|---|---|---|
| `app/services/audit_cloud_logging.py:56` | `asdict(entry)` | yes |
| `app/repositories/audit.py:164` | `asdict(e)` | yes |
| `AuditLogEntry.from_dict` | hand-listed | NO — fixed in #791 |
| `app/repositories/postgres/audit.py:170` `_row_to_dict` | hand-listed | NO — still live |

`_row_to_dict` feeds `metadata_for_review`, the anomaly-review aggregate. That
reviewer therefore cannot tell a clinician-created chart from one created by an
unauthenticated principal — which is precisely the signal the new actor kind
exists to carry. `actor_type` is a short enum-ish string, PHI-free, so adding it
does not disturb `_assert_phi_free`.

An AST scan of every `@dataclass` with a `from_dict` found the same class of
omission elsewhere:

- `app/models/patient.py::Patient.from_dict` drops `origin` (20 fields) — the
  column the public-booking chart-invariant work needs to set.
- `app/models/user.py::User.from_dict` drops `credential_titles`,
  `profile_basics_completed_at`, and the three `inbox_quality_review_opt_*`
  consent timestamps (31 fields).

Four verified instances, all in the hand-written dict layer. `backend/app` has
34 `to_dict`/`from_dict` definitions, so that is a floor, not a ceiling.

The layering itself is NOT the problem and should not be "fixed". A separate
scan of all 31 repositories under `app/repositories/` for construction sites
that silently default a field found three hits, none of them data loss:
`BookingLink.practice_schema` is documented as populated only by `get_by_slug`,
and `_row_to_user` omits `title` / `credentials` / `credential_titles` / `role`
because `PlatformUserRow` has no such columns. The domain-dataclass/repository
split is what lets the unit suite run 2712 tests in ~35s against in-memory
fakes with no Postgres; collapsing it would cost that and buy nothing here.
design:
Pointers verified against OSS main at 52dcae8 plus pablo#791 (merged or in
flight — re-verify `AuditLogEntry.from_dict` before editing, #791 already
fixed that one and adds a round-trip test for it).

MECHANISM, in order:

1. FIX THE LIVE ONE FIRST, on its own commit.
   `app/repositories/postgres/audit.py:170` `_row_to_dict` gains
   `"actor_type": row.actor_type`. Failing test first, in
   `backend/tests/test_audit_repo.py` (or the closest sibling covering
   `metadata_for_review`): a row written with a non-clinician actor_type
   appears in the aggregate carrying that value. `_assert_phi_free` must still
   pass — actor_type is not a PHI field name.

2. INVENTORY the 34 `to_dict` / `from_dict` definitions under `backend/app`
   (`grep -rn "def from_dict\|def to_dict" backend/app`). For each, find real
   callers — excluding tests. The audit pair had ZERO: every live path used
   `dataclasses.asdict()` directly, so the methods existed only to drift.

3. DELETE the ones nothing calls, tests included. CLAUDE.md: "If removing
   unused code, delete it completely." Do not keep one "for symmetry".

4. DERIVE the ones that survive. A `from_dict` that must stay becomes
   `cls(**{k: v for k, v in data.items() if k in _FIELD_NAMES})` where
   `_FIELD_NAMES = {f.name for f in fields(cls)}`, so a new field is picked up
   without an edit. `to_dict` is already derived via `asdict`; leave it.
   Where a call site needs a projection (a subset), that is a projection and
   should say so at the call site, not be a divergent copy of the record.

5. FIX the two drifted survivors if they survive step 3:
   `Patient.from_dict` (`origin`) and `User.from_dict` (5 fields). If step 4
   makes them derived, this is free — verify with a test rather than by eye.

6. ADD THE GUARD: `backend/scripts/check_model_serializers.py`, in the shape of
   the existing `check_route_audit.py` / `check_audit_params.py` — an AST scan
   that fails when a `@dataclass` with a hand-written `from_dict` passes fewer
   kwargs to `cls(...)` than the class declares fields. `cls(**...)` counts as
   derived and passes. Wire it into `make lint` and CI beside the other
   guardrail scripts, and give it a selftest the way the other checks have one.
   A working prototype of the scan exists — see the numbers in the description;
   re-derive it, do not hunt for the scratch file.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:

- KEEP the domain-dataclass + repository split. Do not convert domain models to
  SQLModel, to ORM-rows-as-domain-models, or to anything that makes the service
  layer import SQLAlchemy. The in-memory repository fakes are load-bearing for
  test speed and this bead does not touch them.
- Do NOT convert `AuditLogEntry` (or any domain model) to `pydantic.BaseModel`.
  `dataclasses.asdict()` rejects a non-dataclass and three live call sites use
  it, one of them the Cloud Logging mirror. Pydantic also does not address the
  drift: `_row_to_dict` would still be hand-written either way.
- `pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass` is likewise OUT. It would keep `asdict()`
  working and add validation, but neither is the problem, and neither
  `pydantic.dataclasses` nor `TypeAdapter` appears anywhere in `backend/app`
  today — introducing a pattern for one class is a cost with no return here.
- The fix is deletion plus derivation plus a static check, not a new
  serialization framework.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not touch:

- The `metadata_for_review` baselines and the `is_novel_user_patient`
  computation. Step 1 adds a field to the payload; it does not change which
  rows are aggregated or how novelty is scored.
- The `User` dataclass declaring `title` / `credentials` / `credential_titles`
  / `role` when `PlatformUserRow` has no such columns. That is a real modelling
  question and it is NOT this bead — file it separately if it matters.
- `AuditLogItem` and the other Pydantic API-edge models. Pydantic at the API
  boundary is correct and stays.
- `platform_audit.py`'s `to_dict` unless step 2 shows it unused.
acceptance_criteria:
`make check` green in the OSS repo (ruff + ruff format + mypy + pytest).
Failing-test-first for items 1 and 5. No Alembic revision and no
`tenant_template.sql` change — this bead adds no columns.

1. `metadata_for_review` carries the actor kind. A new test seeds audit rows
   with two different `actor_type` values and asserts each appears in the
   aggregate with its own value; the existing `_assert_phi_free` assertion in
   `metadata_for_review` still passes unmodified.

2. Inventory is recorded. The PR description lists every `to_dict` /
   `from_dict` under `backend/app` with its non-test caller count — the
   evidence for what step 3 deleted and what step 4 kept.

3. Dead serializers are gone. `grep -rn "def from_dict\|def to_dict"
   backend/app` returns strictly fewer than 34, and for every remaining
   definition at least one non-test caller exists.

4. Survivors are derived. No remaining `from_dict` enumerates field names one
   by one; each either takes `**`-expansion filtered by
   `{f.name for f in fields(cls)}` or is a documented projection whose docstring
   says which fields it deliberately omits and why.

5. The two known drifted serializers round-trip completely. If `Patient` and
   `User` keep a `from_dict`, a test asserts that for each, a fully-populated
   instance survives `from_dict(to_dict(x)) == x` — which fails today on
   `Patient.origin` and on `User.credential_titles`,
   `profile_basics_completed_at` and the three `inbox_quality_review_opt_*`
   fields. If instead they were deleted, this criterion is satisfied by their
   absence and the PR says so.

6. `backend/scripts/check_model_serializers.py` exists, exits 0 on the fixed
