title: Booker-side reschedule via the manage token (cancel + create, token rotates)
description: Split from PABLO-e3a.9 to keep cancel one sitting. A booker holding the manage capability picks a new free slot; the server cancels the old appointment and creates the new one in one transaction, rotates the token, pushes both changes to Google, audits the pair and sends a best-effort 'rescheduled' notice through the email seam.
design:
Booker-side RESCHEDULE on top of PABLO-e3a.9 (cancel). Same conventions and preconditions as e3a.9: phase 1 on main, e3a.2/.3/.10/.9 merged; [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] pointers re-verified at implementation time.

MECHANISM:
1. `POST /api/public/booking-links/{slug}/manage/reschedule` body `{"token": str, "start_at": str}` on the public router with the write rate limit (10/h/IP), `ctx=Depends(get_public_booking_context)` and e3a.3's sweep dependency. Token lookup and refusals exactly as e3a.9 (one 404 body).
2. Validate the new time the way the booking POST does (backend/app/routes/public_booking.py:307-310 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]): recompute the owner's free slots for the target date and require `start_at` to be one of them, else 409 "That time is no longer available." (same message). Because the booker's own appointment blocks its current slot, moving within the same day to an adjacent free slot is allowed; moving onto its own current slot is a no-op 200.
3. Atomically (one request, one session — DatabaseSessionMiddleware commits on success, backend/app/db/middleware.py:107-115 main): `scheduling.cancel_appointment(old.id, owner_id)` (clears the old hash), then `scheduling.create_appointment(owner_id, data={patient_id: old.patient_id, title, start_at, end_at, duration_minutes, session_type, notes, status: "confirmed", confirmation_token_hash: sha256(new_token)})` with a FRESH `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, then Google push for the new row and cancellation push for the old (helpers as in e3a.9 #3), then audit APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED (old) and APPOINTMENT_CREATED (new) with changes.source "public_booking" and changes.rescheduled_from = old.id on the new one. If create fails after cancel, the middleware's rollback restores the old row — assert it.
4. Response: `PublicBookingConfirmation` with the new times and a NEW manage_url carrying the new token (the old token is dead: single-use).
5. Notice email: kind "booking_rescheduled", best-effort background, body = old time → new time as the practice's local wall-clock, host name, the new manage link. Same failure semantics as e3a.9 #4.
6. Frontend: the manage page from e3a.9 gains a "Pick a new time" section that reuses the public slots fetch and date navigation already on frontend/app/book/[slug]/page.tsx [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]; on 200 it swaps to the new card and replaces the URL's token with the new one (history.replaceState) so a refresh keeps working.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: reschedule = cancel + create in one transaction, not an in-place time edit (keeps every rule, buffer and overlap check on the create path and gives a clean audit pair); the token rotates; the patient record is reused, never re-looked-up by email; same-slot reschedule is a 200 no-op; no reschedule of a pending (unconfirmed) hold — 404 like any other invalid token.
Do NOT touch: e3a.9's cancel route; the confirm handler; the booking POST beyond extracting a shared "validate requested slot" helper if you need one.

MIGRATION: none.

LANE: never-dispatch, Kurt-paired; no llama-ok — same walk as PABLO-e3a.9: auth/RLS design (anonymous capability mutating and creating tenant rows) · outbound (booker-facing send path; fake in tests) · PHI: times + address only, never logged · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: none of the known surfaces (OSS, trigger holds in full). Base-gated on phase 1 and on e3a.9.
acceptance_criteria:
1. backend/tests/test_public_booking_routes.py [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]: reschedule with a valid token to a free slot → 200 with the new start_at/end_at and a manage_url whose token differs from the old one; the old appointment is "cancelled", a new confirmed appointment exists for the SAME patient_id; `GET .../slots` no longer offers the new slot and offers the old one again.
2. The old token now returns the e3a.9 404 body on manage/cancel/reschedule; the new token returns 200 on manage.
3. Reschedule to a time not in the free-slot list → 409 with the booking POST's exact message; the appointment is unchanged. Reschedule onto its own current slot → 200, no new row, no audit entries.
4. Failure atomicity: with the appointment repository's create patched to raise after cancel, the response is 5xx-free (the engine error maps as the booking POST's does) and the original appointment is still confirmed with its hash intact after the request.
5. Audit fake: exactly one APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED (old id) and one APPOINTMENT_CREATED (new id, changes.rescheduled_from == old id), both with source "public_booking"; gcal mock: delete_event for the old and the create path for the new.
6. Email: InMemoryEmailSender captured one message with kind "booking_rescheduled" and a body containing both times; NoneEmailSender → still 200.
7. Frontend vitest: the manage page's "Pick a new time" flow POSTs reschedule once with the chosen slot and re-renders with the new times; the URL token is replaced.
8. `make check`, `npm --prefix frontend run lint`, `npm --prefix frontend test -- --run` green.

title: Send the browser to the dashboard after a native sign-in that hands off through a custom scheme
description: After a desktop-app sign-in, the browser tab the therapist authorized in should land on the web dashboard, not on a "you can close this tab" card — the dashboard is the primary UI and the point of signing in from the app is to arrive there signed in. Today the tab dead-ends. The thin-client design doc says this redirect lives in the backend's native-callback handler, but no such browser-facing handler exists: /api/auth/native/code is a fetch from the sign-in page and /api/auth/native/exchange is called by the app. Where the browser actually ends up depends on the redirect_uri: for a loopback redirect the tab is served by the app's local server (fixed in the companion repo), and for a custom-scheme redirect the tab stays on the web sign-in page — that half is this change.
design:
Frontend + docs only. Two files touched plus two new.

1. Extract the decision into a pure helper. NEW frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/nativeAuthCompletion.ts (new file) exporting `completionPathAfterHandoff(redirectUri: string): string | null` — returns "/dashboard?from=companion" when the redirect_uri's protocol is neither "http:" nor "https:" (a custom scheme: the browser launches the app and the page keeps running), and null for http/https (loopback: the navigation leaves the page, nothing to do). Invalid URL → null.
2. Use it in frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/NativeAuthScreen.tsx:86-89: after `window.location.href = callbackUrl.toString()`, if `completionPathAfterHandoff(redirectUri)` is non-null, `window.setTimeout(() => window.location.replace(path), 1500)`. Keep the "Sign-in complete — you can close this tab" card (:117-124) as the interim view during the 1.5 s. Clear the timer on unmount.
3. NEW test frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/__tests__/nativeAuthCompletion.test.ts (new file; sibling of the existing client.test.ts): custom scheme → "/dashboard?from=companion"; "http://127.0.0.1:53211/callback" → null; "https://example.test/cb" → null; garbage → null. Test the helper, not window.location.
4. Docs: rewrite docs/design/companion-thin-client.md:162-168 (Enrollment step 2) and :334-336 (rollout step 6) to say where the redirect lives — the app's loopback response for loopback redirects, the web sign-in page for custom-scheme redirects — and drop the "server-side redirect in backend/app/routes/auth.py" wording, which describes a handler that does not exist.

The `from=companion` query parameter is deliberately inert: nothing in frontend/src reads it today; it is there so the dashboard can show a one-time "connected" notice later without changing this contract.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: the path is exactly "/dashboard?from=companion"; 1.5 s delay (long enough for the scheme handoff to leave the page's event loop, short enough not to feel stuck); `location.replace`, not `href`, so Back does not return to the handoff page; no backend change of any kind; no change to the loopback (http) branch here.

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI: none · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none · auth/RLS: post-sign-in navigation on the web page; the code exchange, tokens and enrollment are untouched, so not auth design · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: OSS-landing so the trigger is walked in full — sign-in completion navigation is not a claimed construct · outbound: none.
acceptance_criteria:
1. FAILING-FIRST: frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/__tests__/nativeAuthCompletion.test.ts (4 cases) fails before the helper exists and passes after.
2. NativeAuthScreen.tsx calls `completionPathAfterHandoff` and schedules `window.location.replace("/dashboard?from=companion")` only for non-http(s) redirect_uri values; the loopback branch is byte-for-byte unchanged.
3. docs/design/companion-thin-client.md no longer says the redirect is a backend auth.py handler; `grep -n "native-callback handler" docs/design/companion-thin-client.md` returns nothing.
4. Frontend lint, typecheck and vitest steps that CI runs are green; `make check` green.
5. PR text reads as ordinary OSS work; no tracker ids.

title: Booking link availability should track owner account state, not just subscription
description:
From the 2026-08-20 review of claude/public-booking-links.

_require_owner_may_accept_bookings (landed) gates the booking POST on the owner's SUBSCRIPTION access level. It does not consider owner account state: get_public_booking_context only checks that user_repo.get(link.user_id) returns a row. A deactivated or offboarded clinician whose subscription still resolves to FULL keeps a live, bookable public link.

Decide the rule — probably: a link resolves only while its owner is an active user of an active practice — and pin it with a test. Recorded in docs/design/public-booking.md under 'The wound-down practice'.
design:
Spec pass 2026-08-26 (pass 1). (main) = verified on OSS main at 84f9fb0; [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] = verified on origin/claude/public-booking-links (no PR yet, 53 commits behind main). PRECONDITION: phase 1 on main; re-verify [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] pointers then. Land BEFORE PABLO-e3a.9 (both edit get_public_booking_context).

THE RULE (closed): a booking link resolves only while its owner is not disabled and its practice, when there is one, is active. Refusal is the SAME 404 as a missing or deactivated slug — the link simply does not exist to the public — on the card, the slots and the booking POST alike. This is deliberately stricter than the subscription gate (docs/design/public-booking.md:174-205 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]: reads stay open, writes refuse with 403): a wound-down subscription is temporary and the card is still the clinician's; a disabled account is not.

SUBSTRATE:
- backend/app/routes/public_booking.py:92-124 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] `get_public_booking_context`: :104-106 `link_repo.get_by_slug(slug)` then `if link is None or not link.is_active: raise NotFoundError(_LINK_NOT_FOUND)`; :115-118 tenant schema switch (None → 404); :119 `arm_current_user_id`; :121-123 `owner = user_repo.get(link.user_id)` / `if owner is None: raise NotFoundError(_LINK_NOT_FOUND)`. :81 `_LINK_NOT_FOUND` is the one message. :158-197 `_require_owner_may_accept_bookings` (subscription gate; untouched).
- Owner state on main: backend/app/db/platform_models.py:174 `PlatformUserRow.status` String(20) default "approved" — the ONLY account-state column (no is_active / deactivated_at); the value "disabled" is written by backend/app/routes/admin.py:107-119 `disable_user` and enforced for sign-in at backend/app/auth/service.py:751. Domain model backend/app/models/user.py:166 `User.status`. backend/app/repositories/postgres/user.py:24-36 `get` returns disabled users too (correct — do not change the repo).
- Practice state on main: backend/app/db/platform_models.py:44 `PracticeRow`: :54 `status` String(20) default "active", :55 `is_active` Boolean default True, :73 `deleted_at`. The branch's `get_by_slug` already outer-joins PracticeRow to read `schema_name` (backend/app/repositories/postgres/booking_link.py:49-62 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]) and surfaces it as `BookingLink.practice_schema` (backend/app/models/booking_link.py:48-68 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]).
- Tests: backend/tests/test_public_booking_routes.py:213-221 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] `test_unknown_and_inactive_slugs_are_identical_404s` asserts `missing.json() == inactive.json()`; :95 `_FakeUserRepo` / `_owner()`; :143 `link_repo` (InMemoryBookingLinkRepository, backend/app/repositories/booking_link.py:62 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]).

MECHANISM:
1. `BookingLink` gains `practice_is_active: bool | None = None` (None = single-tenant, no practice row). Postgres `get_by_slug` selects `PracticeRow.is_active` and `PracticeRow.deleted_at` through the existing outer join and sets `practice_is_active = row.is_active and row.deleted_at is None` when a practice row exists. The in-memory repository accepts the field verbatim.
2. In `get_public_booking_context`, immediately after the existing owner check: `if owner.status == "disabled" or link.practice_is_active is False: raise NotFoundError(_LINK_NOT_FOUND)`. Nothing else changes; the subscription gate keeps its 403 semantics for the POST.
3. Docs: replace the paragraph at docs/design/public-booking.md:202-205 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] ("this is a subscription gate, not a user-state gate…") with the rule above and the reason the two gates differ.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: owner rule keys on `status == "disabled"` only (the sole account-state value on main; do not invent an is_active column); practice rule keys on `is_active` and `deleted_at`, not `status` (status is a free-form provisioning string); refusal is the 404 identical to a missing slug on ALL three public routes; no new error message; repositories return the rows, the context dependency decides.
Do NOT touch: the subscription gate; user or practice repositories' `get`; the management routes (backend/app/routes/booking_links.py [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] — a disabled owner cannot sign in anyway).

MIGRATION: none.

LANE: fleet-eligible on the trigger walk — PHI: none (fixtures synthetic; no patient data on the path) · money/entitlement: none (does not touch the subscription gate; no access granted or revoked, only an existing account state honoured) · prod infra: none · auth/RLS: a guard on an existing status value inside the existing context dependency, not a change to auth or policies · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: none · outbound: none. BUT base-gated: phase 1 has no PR and is not on main — no llama-ok until it lands and the [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] pointers are re-verified.
acceptance_criteria:
1. backend/tests/test_public_booking_routes.py [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]: `test_unknown_and_inactive_slugs_are_identical_404s` (:213-221) is extended (not duplicated) with two more cases — a link whose owner has `status == "disabled"` and a link whose `practice_is_active is False` — and asserts all four responses have the same status code and byte-identical bodies for `GET /api/public/booking-links/{slug}`, `GET .../slots?date=...` and `POST .../bookings`.
2. A link with `practice_is_active None` (single-tenant) and an "approved" owner still serves the card and slots and accepts a booking (the existing happy-path tests, e.g. :261 `test_booking_creates_patient_and_appointment`, pass unchanged).
3. The disabled-owner refusal happens before any write: the patient repo is empty and `audit.calls == []` after the POST (mirror :482-484).
4. Repository: a test on the Postgres `get_by_slug` (or the in-memory one if there is no Postgres fixture on the branch) shows `practice_is_active` is True for an active practice, False when `is_active` is false OR `deleted_at` is set, None with no practice row.
5. docs/design/public-booking.md no longer says the gate is "not a user-state gate"; the new paragraph names the rule and the 404 behaviour.
6. `make check` green; no new alembic revision.

llama-ok applied by eng-head 2026-08-26 (pass 2): OSS-landing; seven triggers clear (fixtures; no send; no infra; auth untouched; not a claim surface). Public-repo rules: human-toned commit/PR body, no tracker ids. PRE-LANDING: mechanically held by the dependency on PABLO-e3a.12 (phase 1 on main); dispatches the night after it closes. Re-verify pointers against main first.

title: Booker-side cancel and reschedule via signed tokens
description:
Phase 1 leaves this out: the clinician cancels in-app and the booker has no self-service path. Needs signed tokens hanging off the email path, so it depends on the email seam.

From docs/design/public-booking.md 'What phase 1 deliberately leaves out'.
design:
Spec pass 2026-08-26 (pass 1). Pointer conventions: (main) = verified on OSS main at 84f9fb0; [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] = verified on origin/claude/public-booking-links, which has NO PR yet and sits 53 commits behind main. PRECONDITION: phase 1 must be on main, then PABLO-e3a.2 and PABLO-e3a.3 (this bead redeems the token they introduce), then PABLO-e3a.10 (edits the same context dependency; land it first). Re-verify every [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] pointer at implementation time.

SCOPE (this bead): booker-side CANCEL from a link nobody has to sign in for. Reschedule is split into PABLO-e3a.9.1 (depends on this).

WHY "SIGNED TOKENS" BECOMES "THE CONFIRMATION TOKEN": main has no signing key (backend/app/settings.py has no SECRET_KEY/APP_SECRET; grep for itsdangerous/hmac in backend/app is empty; pyjwt at pyproject.toml:29 only VERIFIES third-party tokens), and the sibling beads already settled the capability-token pattern — 32-byte urlsafe secret, sha256 at rest in `appointments.confirmation_token_hash` (PABLO-e3a.2, after backend/app/services/launch_intent_store.py:48-54 main), looked up via `get_by_confirmation_token_hash(user_id, token_hash)` and CLEARED by `cancel_appointment` (PABLO-e3a.3; backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:322-328 main). PABLO-e3a.3 deliberately keeps the hash after confirm. So the booker already holds exactly one secret, delivered by e3a.2's confirmation email; this bead lets that secret cancel the booking it confirmed. Single-use and expiry fall out for free: cancel clears the hash; a token for an appointment whose start_at has passed is refused.

MECHANISM:
1. Manage URL. `f"{settings.app_url}/book/{link.slug}/manage?token={token}"` (app_url: backend/app/settings.py:230 main). It is exposed in two places, neither of which edits e3a.2's email body: (a) the confirm page that PABLO-e3a.3 recommends as PABLO-e3a.12 shows "Need to change it?" with the token it already holds; (b) `PublicBookingConfirmation` (backend/app/models/booking_link.py:139-146 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]) gains `manage_url: str | None` — the "no internal ids" docstring still holds, a capability is not an id. If e3a.12 is not yet filed when this lands, (b) plus the manage page are sufficient.
2. Routes, on the public router (backend/app/routes/public_booking.py:73-76 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]: `truly_public` + browse rate limit), both taking `ctx=Depends(get_public_booking_context)` (:92-124 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet] — after PABLO-e3a.10 it also refuses disabled owners) and the same sweep dependency e3a.3 attaches:
   - `POST /api/public/booking-links/{slug}/manage` body `{"token": str}` → 200 `PublicManagedBooking { title, host_name, start_at, end_at, duration_minutes, status }` (link-derived fields + the appointment's status; NO patient fields, no ids). POST not GET, for the same reason e3a.3 gives (link scanners consume GETs).
   - `POST /api/public/booking-links/{slug}/manage/cancel` body `{"token": str}`, with `require_public_booking_write_rate_limit` (10/h/IP) → 200 `{"cancelled": true}`.
   Lookup for both: `appt = appt_repo.get_by_confirmation_token_hash(ctx.link.user_id, sha256(token))`; refuse with ONE fixed 404 message ("This link is not valid or has expired.") when appt is None, status is cancelled, or `appt.start_at <= now` — identical body for never-existed / wrong link / already cancelled / expired, preserving the no-oracle property pinned by test_public_booking_routes.py:315-365 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]. Owner scoping is structural: the hash is looked up under `ctx.link.user_id` (the context already armed RLS as the owner at :119 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]).
3. Cancel path = the in-app path: `scheduling.cancel_appointment(appt.id, ctx.link.user_id)` (scheduling.py:322-328 main; sets CANCELLED, clears pending_expires_at and — after e3a.3 — the hash), then `_push_cancellation_to_google` exactly as backend/app/routes/scheduling.py:238-249 (main) does for the clinician's DELETE at :471-497, then `audit.log_appointment_action(AuditAction.APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED, ctx.owner, http_request, appt.id, patient_id=appt.patient_id, changes={"source": "public_booking"})` — the same `source` marker phase 1 uses at public_booking.py:333 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]. Actor fidelity is PABLO-e3a.6's; do not touch actor_type here.
4. Notice email, best-effort, AFTER the cancel commits: `sender: EmailSender = Depends(get_email_sender)` (factory owned by e3a.2 in backend/app/services/email_sender.py main; protocol :64-82, InMemoryEmailSender :152, NoneEmailSender :85); `OutboundEmail(to=patient email, subject=f"Your {link.title} with {link.host_name} is cancelled", kind="booking_cancelled", text=date/time as the practice's local wall-clock + host name + "book again" link to /book/{slug})`. Sent from a FastAPI BackgroundTask (docs/design/public-booking.md:378 [branch-only: does not exist on main yet]); any exception is caught and logged with `kind` only (recipient is PHI-adjacent, :370). With NoneEmailSender the cancel still succeeds. Unlike e3a.2's verification send, this one is NOT required for correctness, so it never refuses to arm.
5. Frontend: frontend/app/book/[slug]/manage/page.tsx (NEW) — sibling of frontend/app/book/[slug]/page.tsx [branch-only: does not exist on main yet], same `params: Promise<{slug}>` shape at :126): reads `?token=`, POSTs manage, renders the booking card (times as the host's local time, wording as page.tsx:270/:289), a "Cancel appointment" button with a confirm step, then a "Cancelled" state; 404 → the one generic "link not valid" state. The success state at page.tsx:248-277 adds the manage link when `manage_url` is present.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: the confirmation token IS the manage capability (no second token column, no signing key); tokens die on cancel (hash cleared by the engine) and at start_at (checked at redemption); 404 with one message for every refusal; cancel reuses cancel_appointment + the same Google push and audit marker as the clinician's DELETE; notice email is best-effort background, kind "booking_cancelled", no PHI in logs; manage/cancel are POST with the token in the body; no clinician-facing UI change (PABLO-e3a.7).
Do NOT touch: e3a.2's send or column; e3a.3's confirm handler, sweep or the not-cleared-on-confirm rule; the audit actor model (e3a.6); rate limiter keys.

MIGRATION: none (the column is e3a.2's).

LANE: never-dispatch, Kurt-paired; no llama-ok — auth/RLS design: this bead defines an unauthenticated principal's capability to MUTATE a chart-attached tenant row (cancel) under RLS armed as the owner; that is auth design even though the token mechanics are inherited · outbound communication: adds a booker-facing send path (default EMAIL_BACKEND "none", InMemoryEmailSender in tests, no live send in the done-signal) — drafts fine, sends are the owner's call · PHI: recipient address and appointment times only, never logged; fixtures synthetic · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: OSS so the trigger holds in full, but capability-link cancellation is commodity booking mechanics, none of the known claim surfaces. title: CAPTCHA seam: CAPTCHA_PROVIDER setting with a Turnstile adapter
description:
Rung 3 of the anti-automation ladder in docs/design/public-booking.md. Only worth adding once rungs 1 and 2 are being beaten.

A CAPTCHA_PROVIDER setting ('none' default; Cloudflare Turnstile as the first adapter) verified server-side as a dependency on the booking POST only — browsing the card and slots stays free. The public link card carries the site key so the page knows whether to render the widget. The provider sees browser signals and a token, never form contents, so nothing PHI-adjacent leaves the deployment.

The engine defaults to 'none' and hard-codes no vendor. The WHEN is a deployment decision with a clear split: a single-practice deployment can reasonably wait for evidence of abuse; a deployment hosting many clinical practices should enable it at rollout, because its operators — not its clinicians — hold the knob.
design:
Spec pass 2026-08-31. All pointers verified on OSS main at d4fbff9 (phase 1 + the phase-2 core are on main; nothing here is branch-gated).

SCOPE (this bead): rung 3 of the anti-automation ladder, exactly as docs/design/public-booking.md:269-289 frames it — a CAPTCHA_PROVIDER setting, a verifier protocol with a no-op default, one Cloudflare Turnstile adapter, the site key on the public card, the widget on the booker page, and server-side verification as a dependency on the booking POST only. Browsing the card and slots stays free.

OUT OF SCOPE: no per-link toggle (the knob is deployment-wide by design — the design doc's "the operators hold the knob"); no CAPTCHA on the card GET, slots GET, or confirm POST (confirm arrives from an emailed link with no widget in sight); no second vendor adapter (the protocol leaves room); no clinician-facing UI; no DB change and therefore no migration; actually enabling the provider on any live deployment (env + keys) is an operator step outside this bead.

MECHANISM:

1. Settings (backend/app/settings.py): captcha_provider: Literal["none", "turnstile"] = "none" — mirror transcription_provider (:661) for the Literal-with-explanatory-description shape and email_backend (:779-787) for the "selection is a configuration change, not a code change" voice. Beside it, turnstile_site_key: str = "" and turnstile_secret_key: SecretStr = SecretStr(""), styled after smtp_password (:792).
2. NEW backend/app/services/captcha.py, a structural mirror of services/email_sender.py: a CaptchaVerifier Protocol (site_key: str | None; verify(token: str | None, remote_ip: str | None) -> bool), NoneCaptchaVerifier (site_key None, verify always True — the default a bare deployment gets), TurnstileVerifier (form-encoded POST of secret/response/remoteip to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify; client_factory test seam exactly like SmtpEmailSender's, email_sender.py:97-116; a SYNC httpx.Client — create_public_booking is sync def at routes/public_booking.py:524 — with a ~5s timeout so a hanging vendor call cannot pin a worker; httpx is already a direct dependency, pyproject.toml:63), and captcha_verifier_from_settings + get_captcha_verifier mirroring email_sender_from_settings/get_email_sender (:162-177). The verify request carries ONLY secret + token + remoteip — never names, emails, or the note — and log lines carry outcome only, never the token, following the PHI-note discipline in email_sender.py's module docstring.
3. Route wiring (backend/app/routes/public_booking.py): a require_captcha dependency taking the token from an X-Captcha-Token header (Header(None, alias="X-Captcha-Token")) plus verifier: CaptchaVerifier = Depends(get_captcha_verifier), appended to the booking POST's decorator dependencies (:518-523) AFTER require_public_booking_write_rate_limit, so the 10/h/IP write window (rate_limit.py:268-275) still runs first and a bot burning verify calls burns its budget too. Not attached to the card GET (:273), slots (:287), or confirm POST (:727). Refusal is 403 ForbiddenError (api_errors import already at :38) with ONE fixed message, "Verification failed. Please refresh and try again." — missing and invalid tokens are indistinguishable.
4. remoteip: reuse the client-IP resolution the rate limiter already keys on (rate_limit._get_client_ip, :197-216) — promote it to a public name if the underscore import offends ruff. remoteip is optional in the siteverify API, so None on the in-memory path is fine.
5. Card: PublicBookingLinkResponse (models/booking_link.py:138-146) gains captcha_site_key: str | None = None; get_public_booking_link (:273-285) fills it from the verifier's site_key. The "everything a visitor may see" docstring still holds — a site key is public by definition (it is rendered into the page).
6. Frontend (frontend/app/book/[slug]/page.tsx): when card.captcha_site_key is non-null, load https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js (explicit render) and mount the widget inside the form (:355) above the submit button; hold the token from the widget callback in state; keep submit disabled until it arrives; send it as X-Captcha-Token in submitBooking's fetch (:173-183). On a 403 whose body detail is the verification message, show that message and window.turnstile.reset(); the existing 403 branch (practice-not-accepting copy, :189-195) keys off the detail so its behavior is unchanged. With a null site key — every deployment by default — the page renders exactly as today and no vendor script is ever requested.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- Names: CAPTCHA_PROVIDER ('none' | 'turnstile', default 'none'), TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY (SecretStr). Deployment-wide; no per-link column, no migration.
- The token travels as the X-Captcha-Token HEADER, not a body field: verification runs as a decorator dependency (the design doc's "as a dependency on the booking POST only"), and a header keeps CreatePublicBookingRequest vendor-free.
- FAIL-OPEN on infrastructure failure ONLY. A siteverify network error, timeout, or 5xx logs a warning (outcome only, no token, no secret) and lets the booking proceed. Why: the booker cannot induce that failure (the call is server-to-vendor), the write rate limit and rung-2 email confirmation remain the abuse floor, and failing closed converts a vendor outage into a total booking outage for legitimate clients — the worse harm for an appointment page. A definitive answer always wins: HTTP 200 with success:false refuses. No fail_closed knob until a deployment asks for one.
- Refusal is 403 with one fixed message; missing token is treated identically to an invalid one.
- The two Turnstile URLs (widget script, siteverify) live only in the adapter and the widget code path, both inert unless configured — that is what "hard-codes no vendor" means here, the same posture as SmtpEmailSender living in-tree behind EMAIL_BACKEND.

SEQUENCING: no dependency edges; independently landable. It does share four files with open sibling PABLO-e3a.9/.9.1 (page.tsx, models/booking_link.py, routes/public_booking.py, test_public_booking_routes.py) — chain rather than parallelize with them; either order works.

LANE: dispatch-eligible — PHI: none; the verify call carries token + IP only, never form contents, and logs carry outcome only; fixtures synthetic · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none — ships with captcha_provider defaulting to 'none' everywhere; turning it on for any deployment (env + keys) is a separate operator step outside this bead · auth/RLS design: none — a pre-handler check on an already-public, rate-limited POST; touches no session arming, no tokens, no capabilities · vendor dashboards: obtaining Turnstile site/secret keys is an operator step, not this bead's — the code targets the documented siteverify API and every test uses fakes, no live vendor call in any gate · patent-adjacent: public repo so the trigger is walked in full — a CAPTCHA provider seam is commodity anti-abuse plumbing, none of the known claim surfaces · outbound communication: none — no email/SMS; the only outbound request is the server-side verify to the vendor endpoint.
acceptance_criteria:
1. backend/tests/test_captcha.py (NEW, mirroring test_email_sender.py's class-per-backend shape): NoneCaptchaVerifier — site_key is None and verify(None, None) is True. TurnstileVerifier with a fake client_factory — the request is a form POST to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify whose fields are exactly {secret, response, remoteip} (no other field ever appears); success:true → True; success:false → False; a raised connect error, a timeout, and a 500 response each → True (fail-open) with a warning log line containing neither the token nor the secret. captcha_verifier_from_settings: default settings → NoneCaptchaVerifier; provider 'turnstile' → TurnstileVerifier carrying both keys.
2. backend/tests/test_public_booking_routes.py, with get_captcha_verifier overridden by a fake that records calls: with the fake active and no X-Captcha-Token header the booking POST → 403 and no appointment and no patient was created; with an invalid token → 403 with a byte-identical body; with a valid token → 201 and the booking flow is unchanged. The card GET's captcha_site_key equals the fake's site key when active and is null under the default no-op. The card GET, slots GET, and confirm POST never call verify (the fake's recorded call count stays 0 across all three).
3. Every pre-existing test in test_public_booking_routes.py passes unmodified except any card-shape assertion, which gains the new nullable key — provider 'none' must be a true no-op.
4. Frontend vitest at frontend/app/book/[slug]/__tests__/page.test.tsx (NEW; directory convention from app/launch/[intentId]/__tests__/page.test.tsx), with window.turnstile mocked: a card without captcha_site_key renders no widget container and submit works as today; with a site key the widget mounts, submit stays disabled until the token callback fires, and the booking POST then carries the X-Captcha-Token header; a 403 verification response resets the widget and shows the verification message, not the not-accepting-bookings copy.
5. make check green; npm --prefix frontend run lint and npm --prefix frontend test -- --run green.
notes:
PROMOTED llama-ok — spec pass 2026-08-31. Six gates pass: pointers verified at d4fbff9 (settings.py transcription_provider :661 / email_backend :779 mirror, public_booking.py :524 sync route, booking-link card models :138); decisions pinned (header token, single 403 message, fail-open on infra failure only with the rate-limit + email-confirmation floor, default-off); acceptance names test files + assertions; no deps; no DB change. Seven triggers walked clean — Turnstile keys + env activation are explicitly operator steps outside the bead. Sequencing: shares page.tsx / models/booking_link.py / public_booking.py / test_public_booking_routes.py with e3a.9/.9.1 (both needs-kurt, inactive) — if e3a.9 activates, chain, don't parallelize.

title: Absolute audit-log immutability via DB role separation (pablo_app runtime role)
description:
Follow-up to PABLO-5zy. The append-only trigger shipped in PR #432 is defense-in-depth, not absolute: the app shares the table-owner DB role (pablo) with the retention cron, so a fully-compromised app process could SET LOCAL app.allow_audit_purge='on' itself or ALTER TABLE audit_logs DISABLE TRIGGER. Absolute §164.312(c)(1) immutability requires DB role separation.

Verified design (2026-06-07): single Cloud SQL user 'pablo' owns all tenant tables; app + all Cloud Run jobs share one pablo-database-url secret; the app process itself does DDL (create_practice_schema at boot via ensure_schemas, and the pentest admin route), so it cannot be a pure low-priv role without a dual-engine split.

Plan:
- New cluster-level role 'pablo_app' (runtime, least-privilege). Created ONCE as a bootstrap step (gcloud sql users create + password in Secret Manager + new pablo-app-database-url secret) wired into setup-solo.sh; run manually against existing oss/dev/prod. NOT a per-tenant alembic migration (CREATE ROLE is cluster-level).
- Keep 'pablo' as the owner/DDL role used by provisioning, alembic, and the retention purge.
- Dual-engine: a privileged engine (pablo) for create_practice_schema + audit_retention purge; the low-priv engine (pablo_app) for normal request traffic. create_practice_schema already takes an engine arg, so the injection point is contained.
- Per-schema grants to pablo_app (full DML on most tables; SELECT,INSERT only on audit_logs) plus ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for future tables. Lives in tenant_template.sql + a backfill migration (same touch-points as the trigger).
- App Cloud Run service switches its DATABASE_URL secret to pablo-app-database-url; jobs needing owner keep pablo-database-url.
- With pablo_app non-owner and lacking UPDATE/DELETE on audit_logs, it genuinely cannot mutate or re-grant or DISABLE TRIGGER -> absolute immutability; the trigger remains as a complementary layer.
- Re-verify RLS/FORCE-RLS behaviour under the non-owner role; integration test that pablo_app cannot UPDATE/DELETE audit_logs even by attempting to arm the GUC.
Effort ~1-2 days + multi-env credential rollout.

title: Absolute audit-log immutability via DB role separation (follow-up to PABLO-5zy)
description: PABLO-5zy made practice.audit_logs append-only via a BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger with a SET LOCAL app.allow_audit_purge GUC exemption for the retention cron. That is defense-in-depth, NOT absolute: the app shares the table-owner DB role with the cron, so a fully-compromised app process could SET the GUC itself or ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER and mutate audit_logs. Absolute immutability needs role separation: app connects as a non-owner role with UPDATE/DELETE REVOKE'd and NOBYPASSRLS; the retention purge runs as a distinct privileged role/job. Requires a second DB role + credentials + Cloud Run job wiring across oss/dev/prod. Heavier (~1-2 days + infra). Owner accepted shipping the trigger first; this is the follow-up for absolute §164.312(c)(1) integrity.

title: ORT screener — weighted, sex-conditional scoring extension
description: Add the Opioid Risk Tool (ORT, Webster 2005). ORT does NOT fit the uniform per-item scale: items are checked/not, carry DIFFERENT point weights, and several weights are SEX-CONDITIONAL (e.g. family hx alcohol abuse scores differently M vs F). Needs a weighted-scoring path in the registry (compute_total is a plain sum today) AND a way to pass the respondent attribute the weights depend on — which changes the scoring signature through service/router/schemas and pulls in a PHI-adjacent attribute. Design the weighted-instrument representation before building. Licensing: ORT is freely reproduced (verify, like the PHQ-9 analysis). Bands: 0-3 low / 4-7 moderate / >=8 high risk.

GUARDRAILS: AI drafts, clinician determines (diagnosis is a licensed act); every proposed 'met' must carry a citation or it is not shown as met; PHI goes through the existing LLM-gateway + audit/redaction seams, no PHI in logs. Reuses the SOAP-generation path posture. Depends on backend + frontend phases.

title: Bump redis-py 5→8 (PR #306) — verify retry_on_timeout still works
description:
Dependabot PR #306 bumps `redis` (the redis-py client) from 5.3.1 to 8.0.0 — three majors. Deferred pre-launch (06-08) for safety; revisit after.

## Audit of our call sites

We use redis-py in three places:
- `backend/app/redis_client.py` — single-instance sync client (Redis, ping, ConnectionError)
- `backend/app/rate_limit.py` — pipeline, zrem, scan_iter, delete
- `backend/app/services/auth_code_store.py` — pipeline, setex
- `backend/app/auth/idle_session.py` — exists, set, pipeline

All sync, single-instance, no async / cluster / pubsub / streams / sentinel — the surfaces that took the heaviest churn across 6/7/8.

## Likely papercut

`retry_on_timeout=True` is passed in `redis_client.py`. It was deprecated in 5.x in favor of a `retry=Retry(...)` object and may be silently dropped or warn in 8.x. Worst case: retry behavior disabled, not a crash. Verify and switch to the `retry=` form if needed.

## Plan when revisited

1. Check out PR #306 branch locally.
2. Install with poetry, confirm constructor accepts our kwargs without warnings.
3. Run rate_limit + auth_code_store + idle_session test suites against a real Redis container.
4. If clean, merge. If `retry_on_timeout` is gone, swap to `retry=Retry(ConnectionError, retries=3)` and amend the PR.

title: Audit Cloud Logging dual-write is synchronous on the request path
description:
AuditService._persist() mirrors every audit entry to Cloud Logging via audit_cloud_logging.write_to_cloud_logging(), which calls the low-level google.cloud.logging Logger.log_struct() — a synchronous write_entries() API round-trip. Because _persist runs inside the request handler (e.g. every patient view, session action, audio upload), each audited request pays a synchronous Cloud Logging round-trip (~tens of ms same-region) after the Postgres write.

It is best-effort (wrapped in try/except, so a mirror failure never fails the request), and the client build is one-time per process (@lru_cache on _gcp_logger), which is cheap on GCP where the metadata server is local. The remaining cost is the per-request synchronous mirror write on the hot path.

Improvement: move the mirror write off the request path — batched/background transport (e.g. BackgroundThreadTransport / the handler-based async logging path) or an outbound queue — so the canonical Postgres write is the only synchronous audit cost per request. Keep the best-effort, fail-open semantics. Postgres stays the audit-of-record; Cloud Logging stays the tamper-evident mirror.

Ref: backend/app/services/audit_cloud_logging.py (write_to_cloud_logging / _gcp_logger), backend/app/services/audit_service.py (_persist, audit_dual_write_enabled). Low priority: current cost is modest and bounded; revisit if audited-endpoint latency or audit volume grows.

title: Migrate e2e test runner off deprecated otplib 12 to otplib 13
description:
The e2e runner pins otplib 12.0.1, whose internal packages (@otplib/plugin-crypto, @otplib/preset-default, @otplib/plugin-thirty-two) are deprecated upstream in favor of otplib 13. This is a maintenance deprecation, not a vulnerability — npm audit on e2e/ is clean — hence low priority.

otplib 13 is a breaking API rewrite, not a drop-in bump:
- The authenticator singleton (.options / .generate()) used in e2e/fixtures/totp.ts is gone; v13 exposes functional generate()/verify() plus TOTP/HOTP classes.
- The package is ESM-first (type: module) with dual CJS exports.

Scope:
- Rewrite e2e/fixtures/totp.ts to the v13 API and bump otplib to ^13 in e2e/package.json.
- Confirm the three @otplib/* deprecation warnings are gone after the bump.

Acceptance (load-bearing): generated TOTP codes must stay RFC-6238 compatible (SHA1, 6 digits, 30s step) and keep satisfying the Firebase MFA enrollment + sign-in challenge. Verify by comparing v12 vs v13 output for a fixed secret/epoch, and by a green e2e run that exercises MFA.

Follow-up to the e2e Playwright suite work; no functional impact today.

title: migration-lint flags doc-only model changes; refresh Icd10CodeRow docstring
description:
Two small follow-ups surfaced by PABLO-6xj.5 (pablo PR #380):

2. Deferred because of (1): Icd10CodeRow docstring in platform_models.py still says 'Seeded from app.diagnostics.baseline (a curated subset ...); a managed deployment may seed the full catalog.' After #380, codes are seeded from the bundled catalog (app.diagnostics.catalog, F01-F99 + Z55-Z65). Refresh the docstring to match — bundle it with the next PR that legitimately touches the model + a migration.
